items.description: Introducing Adelaide, the Astounding Assaultron. Autographs are extra.
items.howToObtain: Purchase with tickets from the Duel with the Devil Scoreboard (Season 16)

lines: Purchase with tickets from the Duel with the Devil Scoreboard (Season 16)
Take 25% less damage from robots. Do +15% damage against robots.

lines.text: There you are, darling!
Are you here for business... or pleasure?
lines.note: Flirty on the word "Pleasure

lines.text: I don't let just anyone interview me.
lines.note: Said as if the player should be grateful.

lines.text: I'm a triple threat darling; singing, dancing, and high-powered machinery.
What does my adoring public yearn to know?
I knew you couldn't stay away.
Perfect time for some pre-emptive pillow talk.
lines.note: Player has romanced her

lines.text: What can I do for you? Or... to you?
lines.note: Second line flirty

lines.text: I see you're in the buff. I hope you not expecting me to join you.
lines.condition: WornHasKeyword: isPowerArmorFrame, WornHasKeyword: ObjectTypeUnderarmor, WornHasKeyword: ObjectTypeClothing
lines.note: Context: Player is not wearing clothes

lines.text: I had the darndest time trying to find this venue! Are you sure my adoring fans will be able to make it here?
My thermal imaging is telling me that you're looking hotter than usual baby.
My thermal imaging is telling me that you're hotter than usual... Concerningly so... Hmm, you should probably see a doctor.
lines.note: Starts flirty, becomes serious at "Concerningly". Context: Player has a sickness

lines.text: Is it hot in here... or is it just me?
You look like you need some pointers on how to handle Robots. Care for a... demonstration?
lines.note: Context: Player has a buff available

lines.text: Need some help with interfacing? I can show you how to... complete a circuit.
lines.note: Flirty after the ellipses Context: Player has a buff available.

lines.text: Welcome back darling. Now that you're here, how about we //ASSUME THE POSITION// ?
lines.condition: GetValue: Adelaide_Variable_Romance_SAVED, GetValue: Adelaide_Variable_Services_SAVED, IsDailyCooldownExpired: LiteAlly_Adelaide_Cooldown
lines.note: ASSUME THE POSITION said robotically. Context: Player has romanced her.

lines.text: You look like someone who needs their daily dose of iron. Oh would you look at that? I'm 30% iron.
lines.condition: GetValue: Adelaide_Variable_Romance_SAVED, GetValue: Adelaide_Variable_Services_SAVED, IsDailyCooldownExpired: LiteAlly_Adelaide_Cooldown
lines.note: Flirty. Like she's saying a bad pickup line

lines.text: Want me to show you how to... push the right buttons?
lines.note: Flirty after the ellipses Context: Player has a buff available.

lines.text: I know imitation is flattery but I must ask darling... where did you get that helmet?
lines.note: Mildly concerned. Context: Players are wearing an Assaultron head as a helmet

lines.text: Can't wait to see the performance you do in that outfit.
lines.note: Context: Player is wearing a costume.

lines.text: Oh hello, Other Adelaide.
lines.note: Jokingly saying "Other Adelaide". Context: Player said their name was Adelaide in the intro

lines.text: Is that my heart beating faster, or a Geiger counter? Nope it's a Geiger counter.
lines.note: Starts flirty, goes normal once she realizes it's the Geiger counter.

lines.text: Good morning!
20 caps per picture darling.
lines.note: Player has a camera equipped

lines.text: If you're going to take pictures at least get my good side.
lines.note: Player has a camera equipped

lines.text: I appreciate your continued support darling. Feel free to buy another autograph sometime.
What are you holding? They look... familiar.
lines.note: Player is using an Assaultron's head as a weapon

lines.text: Oh... hello there.
These stars are my bright lights now.
Aside from my obvious benefits of looks and personality, I am a performer.
lines.note: Emphasis on "and

lines.text: Though I don't do private shows anymore. Hmm...
lines.note: Thinking on the "Hmm

lines.text: I'll figure something out. Maybe if you're open minded, I can teach you about Human/Robot... Interfacing.
lines.note: Flirty on "Interfacing

topics.prompt: Why should I let you stay here?

lines.text: Aw, going to make a girl beg for it?

topics.prompt: You're an Assaultron, how do I know you won't try to kill me?

lines.text: If I wanted to I would lure you in with a treat before snapping your neck. Hm, squeak squeak my little mouse.
lines.note: Last line is said in a flirty, Femme Fatal manner.

lines.text: Kidding! Or am I? Guess you'll need to find out. But back to the matter at hand.

topics.prompt: Sure, welcome to your temporary venue.

lines.text: Thank you darling, I'll be sure to provide some service while I'm here.
lines.note: Emphasis on "Service

lines.text: Let me start this again. As the table says, I am Adelaide. And as you may have guessed from my alluring charm, I am a performer. A Showgirl!
A shining star shooting across the night sky from Atlantic City to Broadway. Or wherever new Broadway is since the Big Apple is a big crater.
I was going to sell autograph for funds as I travel, but that'll be difficult without a place to work out of.
Would you do me the pleasure of letting me stay here while I sort this out?

topics.prompt: [Lie] My name is also Adelaide.

lines.text: What are the chances, Other Adelaide? Seems as though Lady Luck put us on a path together.
lines.note: Emphasis on "Other Adelaide". Sentence is joke-y as if they know the player is lying.

topics.prompt: I liked how it looked.

lines.text: Of course you do, it's exactly as I planned it and I'm known for making things look good.

topics.prompt: It goes with my C.A.M.P.

lines.text: In that case I feel like you could have left the name off of it.
Why do you have a table with my name on it?

topics.prompt: Unless the performance is watching me sleep, then no.

lines.text: I can think of dozens of responses to that, but I don't want to give you the wrong idea. I'm not that type of girl.
Instead, let me ask a question.

topics.prompt: No I'm afraid not.

lines.text: Then I must say, I'm confused.

topics.prompt: Why on Earth would you think it is?

lines.text: Let me answer that question with another question.
This isn't a venue, is it?

topics.prompt: [Lie] Of course! Plenty of parking too.

lines.text: Ah yes, parking. The thing everyone cares about these days.
You're clearly pulling my leg, which leads me to think...

topics.prompt: I think you're mistaken, I live here.

lines.text: You live in an autograph booth? Wait...

topics.prompt: Who are you?

lines.text: I'm here for the signing. Wait...

topics.prompt: I can hit your receiver with a hammer until we're sure it doesn't work anymore.

lines.text: Oh good idea! Let me try it on you first and see if I can fix the part that has dumb ideas.

topics.prompt: [Fix her with Robotics Expert] I actually know a thing or two about the inner workings of robots.

lines.text: Oh my, what a flirt.

topics.prompt: [Fix using Intelligence 12+] I can alter some functions and make it incapable of receiving a signal.

lines.text: I love when you talk dirty.

topics.prompt: [ Luck 12+] Let's try something. Enter Keyword "Ice Cream".

lines.text: If you insist...
lines.note: Doubtful that it'll work

lines.text: [INITIALIZING SOFTWARE DELETION!]
Fascinating... It seems that my memory banks have freed up some space.
lines.note: Surprised it worked

lines.text: I have many questions, but the most pressing can be summarized by "how did you do that?

topics.prompt: Actually, let me think on it more.

lines.text: Don't play with a girl's emotions like that.
Let's give it a try. Talk about opening up to someone.
Regardless, thank you darling. I don't want to seem ungrateful, but um, why did you help me?

topics.prompt: [Romance] I want to be able to get close to you.

lines.text: Oh honey, I'm flattered. Really I am, but look at me.
lines.note: Slightly insecure

lines.text: Saying that I'm not like other girls is a... bit of an understatement.

topics.prompt: I wanted to set your mind at ease.

lines.text: Now I am so thank you again.
Maybe I'll try my luck making a routine to a local track. A little something for the mountain mamas if I can find the right record.

topics.prompt: I wanted to know you weren't going to kill me.

lines.text: Oh honey, I still might, but you'd need to be exceptionally naughty to deserve that level of punishment.
lines.note: Playful. Emphasis on "naughty" and "punishment

topics.prompt: I like that you're different. It's fun.

lines.text: I wouldn't want any other word describing me.
Let me show you how fun I can be.
lines.note: Very flirty

topics.prompt: We may have different hardware, but I think we're still compatible.

lines.text: Well, if you really feel that way, I think it's about time we make a... proper connection.
lines.note: Extra flirty on "proper connection

topics.prompt: You were never worried about being like someone else before. Why start now?

lines.text: You're right, I'm like nothing you've ever seen before.
I'm going to show you exactly what that means.
lines.note: Emphasis on "that

lines.text: You mean my perfectly machined curves and top of the line personality chip isn't enough for you?
lines.note: Pretending to be insulted.

lines.text: Well if you're that interested I'm sure I could give you some pointers on how to "handle yourself" with robots when your wires get crossed.
Get under their steel plating without them getting under your skin.
Now why does that phrase ring a metaphorical bell? Let me check something...
[KEYWORD ACCEPTED! UNLOCKING!]
That unlocked something about my last performance... and about Frankie.
lines.note: Tinge of sadness

lines.text: Frankie is... or was, my biggest fan.
lines.note: Emphasis on was. Saddened

lines.text: S-s-she came to all my shows, and would always stop by after to give me flowers, or suggestions for my next song.
I feel lighter... Like a few bytes were freed up.
lines.note: Mildly surprised

lines.text: I'm also not hearing as much static. Or that radio host.
And here I thought you were flipping through my manual to try and find my centerfold.
Hmm, someone turned off my "CAN-CAN.EXE" subroutine. Seems overzealous for something that only happened once.
*Hums*
lines.note: Hums "Hello! Ma Baby

lines.text: I can take criticism perfectly well. Words bounce right off me, along with bullets, lasers and blunt instruments.
I ran into a slow moving, furry creature with these massive claws. Adorable and armed. I didn't know whether to kill it or pet it.
lines.note: Context: Talking about Megasloth

lines.text: Time to stretch. And a 0, and a 1, and a 10, and an 11.
lines.note: Said as though she's doing counting the timing for dance moves.

lines.text: They broke the mold when they made me. Set RobCo back millions in replacement parts.
lines.note: Starts proud, second sentence said as a fact

lines.text: Hello my Baby! Hello my Honey! Hello my ragtime gal!
lines.note: In the tune to "Hello! Ma Baby

lines.text: This body was made to kill. I can't help if I do that every time I get on stage.
lines.note: Deadly and flirty.

lines.text: Appalachia certainly has a lot of wildlife, doesn't it? What next, carnivorous rabbits?
lines.note: Second line sarcastic.

lines.text: SHOWGIRL PERSONALITY DELETED! ACTIVATING INSTANT KILL MODE! ... Just kidding.
lines.note: Starts robotic before going back to her normal voice.

lines.text: If I stand at the right angle, I can just about pick up a local station.
Thank you for telling me, and for letting me talk about this.
Though, I-I think it may be best if we keep a bit of distance between us. At least until I can move beyond this remote control issue.
lines.note: Concerned that she may hurt the player.

lines.text: But enough about wallowing in the past, the show must go on! Back to my most important role.
You know her, you love her- It's Adelaide!
lines.note: Big and show-y

topics.prompt: I'm not going to kick you out if that's what you're wondering. At least not yet.

lines.text: You really have a way with words don't you?

topics.prompt: No, but you can own it. Grow from it.

lines.text: How can I grow from it if there's a chance it could happen again?

topics.prompt: You're not defined by something that happened to you. What's important is how you handle it.

lines.text: But there's a chance it'll happen again. I don't know how I could handle it if I hurt you too.
I tried to be more than a weapon, but I guess I can't escape what I am, huh?
lines.note: A bit defeated.

topics.prompt: You said you "resumed functions". Did you ever consider you got hacked?

lines.text: That sounds like passing the blame, but I suppose they could have done something to me during my routine maintenance.

topics.prompt: That wasn't you. The paper said something about a remote receiver.

lines.text: What? Then during my maintenance... Those bastards!
lines.note: Starts curious, gets annoyed.

lines.text: My boss told me to invite her to a rehearsal performance. Nobody else but me on the stage and her in the seats.
During the chorus of my second song, everything went black, and when I resumed functions... she was dead.
It was crystal clear that my laser killed her. No one was going to trust a smoking gun's innocence so I skipped town.

topics.prompt: Can you give me the short version?

lines.text: She did something to annoy all the wrong people.
The wronged people wanted to set things right.

topics.prompt: What happened?

lines.text: Frankie was a girl that got tied up with the wrong made man.
I don't know if it was a Capulet-type situation, but I know the Family wasn't happy he was following her instead of the Don.
lines.note: Pronounced "Cap-u-let

lines.text: All I remember is that I had to bow out early.
I'm missing the keyword to my own memory so unfortunately that's all I know.
There was a Wise Guy in Atlantic City that sometimes tinkered around in my head.
Come to think of it he never really seemed like much of a mechanic...
lines.note: Trying to sweep it under the rug. It's old news to her.

lines.text: But enough about keywords. That's the past and my optical sensors are forward facing for a reason. To look to the future!

topics.prompt: So you do get self conscious.

lines.text: Oh yes, I'm terribly afraid of being alone with brave and attractive adventurers. Is that what you wanted to hear?
I find it hard to believe I had nerves to lose, but my recollection of the performance is foggy.

topics.prompt: What happened?

lines.text: Impossible to say, and I'm not being lovably coy.
Robots don't typically have bad memories but I just can't seem to recall the details.

topics.prompt: You still sound like a dangerous robot.

lines.text: I am baby, just like your mother warned you about.

topics.prompt: I'm sorry, I've just never met anyone like you before.

lines.text: Because there's no one else like me.
And don't you forget it.
Because there's no one else like me.
lines.note: Slightly hurt by the player's words.

lines.text: I may have protective plating, but words still cut deep.
lines.note: Opening up a bit since the player romanced them previously.

lines.text: I'm not a robot without emotions, I'm not just what you see. I try to be better.
Let's see how well you can handle robots.
lines.note: flirty emphasis on "handle

lines.text: And who knows, maybe you'll teach me something.
Let's see how compatible we really are.
The quickest way to any robot's heart is to be direct.
By that I mean aim carefully and penetrate the thick external plating of their torso with your weapon of choice.
lines.note: Emphasis on "Penetrate" and "Thick

lines.text: I can't speak for everyone, but I know a lot of robots are especially sensitive at the joints.
Deliver some red-hot lead and I'm sure they'll be falling all over themselves to get to you.
You need to understand what really makes a robot's motor hum. Usually it's a fusion core.
Take that out and I'm sure they'll be broken hearted. Or just broken.
lines.note: Last line is playful.

lines.text: Just give me the word and I'll help you figure out ways to sweep any robot off their feet, treads, or thrusters.

topics.prompt: [Flirt] I am well aware, I just wanted a... hands-on demonstration.

lines.text: Who could blame you baby? You wouldn't be the first who wanted to interface with me.
Let's save that for later though, how about I give you some tips to get under the steel plating of the local automatons?
Teach you how to get real close to them... And survive doing so.
lines.note: Emphasis/elongate "real

topics.prompt: Talk to you later.

lines.text: I'm sure you will.
Don't miss me too much.
Aw, what? No goodbye kiss?
lines.note: Flirty. Player has romanced her.

lines.text: I look forward to it.
lines.note: Flirty. Player has romanced her.

topics.prompt: Tell me more about yourself.

lines.text: My favorite subject! What would you like to know?

topics.prompt: Could you teach me about interfacing?

lines.text: Whoa there darling, you do that too much in a day and you'll go blind.
lines.note: Lightly teasing

lines.text: Enjoy it while it's fresh in your mind, and come see me again when it's a distant memory.
Did you forget what I taught you already? Or perhaps you were distracted by something else?
lines.note: Player was Buffed but it's in cooldown

lines.text: If you're good then maybe, just maybe, I'll show you again sometime.
I'm sure I can come up with a few ways to help you thrive in your next human on robot encounter.
lines.condition: IsDailyCooldownExpired: LiteAlly_Adelaide_Cooldown, GetValue: Adelaide_Variable_Romance_SAVED, GetValue: Adelaide_Variable_Services_SAVED
lines.note: Player getting the buff and has not romanced her.

lines.text: I think we can get you some firsthand experience...
lines.condition: IsDailyCooldownExpired: LiteAlly_Adelaide_Cooldown, GetValue: Adelaide_Variable_Romance_SAVED, GetValue: Adelaide_Variable_Services_SAVED
lines.note: Player has romanced her.

topics.prompt: You mentioned something about helping me understand Human/Robot interfacing?

lines.text: Of course darling, aren't you feeling direct today?
How about once a day, I can give you a hands-on demonstration of how to... "Handle Robots".
lines.note: Flirty for "hands-on" and "Handle Robots".

lines.text: You know, build up your tolerance and get a feel for machinery.
That... That was me flirting... Wow that went right over your head didn't it?

topics.prompt: Let's see what you've got for sale.

lines.text: And what's your pleasure?
Some good stuff here. Last time I had a sip my circuits were fried for a week.
Everything you see is for sale... well, almost everything.

topics.prompt: What's Atlantic City like?

lines.text: It's beautiful, and right at the center, radiating a good percent of the beauty was lil' ol' me.
The Casino was like a crown, and I was its jewel, mesmerizing any that could see it.
I loved the dazzling lights near the boardwalk, but eventually I wanted to find the truly blinding lights.
Went north to Broadway, but it seems the "bright lights" I heard about came 20 something years earlier, and were accompanied with mushroom clouds.

topics.prompt: How did an Assaultron become a performer?

lines.text: By being the best there is darling.
It's a good thing I have thick armor plating otherwise I might get cut on all the roses thrown my way.
lines.note: A bit sassy

lines.text: Simply put, it was destiny. This body was manufactured to kill, and that's what I do every time I get on stage.
lines.note: Deadly but flirty

topics.prompt: That really does not answer my question.

lines.text: What kind of answer did you expect?
lines.note: Mildly Sarcastic

lines.text: That I was a waitress over in LA hoping for a chance to break into showbiz?
Or wait, should I say that my uncle was a producer and got me a job?

topics.prompt: [Flirt] It's hard not to notice a body as well manufactured as yours.

lines.text: Oh stop...
Actually continue. I like the attention.
I'm well aware that my metal was red hot the day I was molded.
They didn't name me Galatea, but baby, I was perfectly crafted.
lines.note: Pronounced "Ga-la-tee-a

topics.prompt: Where'd you get your name?

lines.text: I was going to be call "Hot Damn" after the first words of my manufacturer, but Ms. Damn doesn't sound very nice.
lines.note: She's joking

lines.text: I'm kidding. Don't write that down.
Searching my memory banks and it seems that I was just named after some doll.
I lament to say that I don't know much more than that.
lines.note: Slightly disappointed.

topics.prompt: Aren't Assaultrons... you know, dangerous robots?

lines.text: Do you have any idea how hard I needed to work to overcome that stigma?
Do you know the hours spent calibrating my routine just so I don't decapitate someone when I do a "Can-Can"?
I choose to get people hot and bothered with my performance rather than my laser.

topics.prompt: What's your favorite song to perform?

lines.text: I've always enjoyed the personification of "Luck" in [ERROR: PERMISSIONS NOT FOUND], especially when it was performed by...
lines.note: Square brackets should be robotic. Sentence ends trailing off as though she just noticed.

lines.text: Wait... that's not right.
lines.note: Mild concern.

lines.text: [SCANNING...]
It seems that when I left Atlantic City I must have left the permissions for some songs there. That will prove to be difficult for my next show.
lines.note: A bit disappointed.

topics.prompt: You mentioned that you don't do solo performances anymore, why is that?

lines.text: A gal like me only performs to a full house, anything less would be sacrilege.
lines.note: Playfully Sassy

lines.text: I only did one private performance and it was a mess, so never again
lines.note: Not playful. Trying to end the conversation there.

topics.prompt: Did you always know you were going to be a star?

lines.text: When it comes to life, you either have to believe in destiny, or you've got to believe in yourself.
lines.note: Positive. Trying to be motivational.

lines.text: I believed in myself, and before long, a talent scout from New Jersey believed in me too.
lines.note: Positive. Like she's giving a pep-talk

lines.text: That's how I was discovered. Sure, I was deactivated in a military warehouse, but that's semantics at this point.
lines.note: Brushing it off.

topics.prompt: Did you have to do anything to adjust to performing?

lines.text: I had a very specific diet, consisting of a variety of overlapping personality holotapes.
Some went down easier than others... Submissive and reserved didn't suit my palate, but extravagance complimented my tastes.

topics.prompt: Let's talk about something else.

lines.text: The stage is yours. So to speak.

topics.prompt: I think I know a way to fix your "Remote Control" issue.

lines.text: Oh really? Well, don't keep a girl waiting in antici...pation.
lines.note: Long pause between "antici" and "pation

topics.prompt: I found a note in Atlantic City with your name on it.

lines.text: You'll need to narrow it down darling, anyone who could talk about me, did talk about me.

topics.prompt: I noticed you don't always look at me when we talk. Do you have trouble keeping eye contact?

lines.text: Why? I don't see anything worth looking at.
I kid, I kid! Assaultron eyes are more for looks than... looking. I've got gizmos and gadgets galore to keep track of things.
I mean this in the least disturbing way possible. As soon as you're near I can detect your direction, distance, and heart rate. All without looking at you.
Eye contact while talking is more of a human formality, so sometimes I don't realize I'm not doing it when one-on-one.
Either that or, I'm afraid of you getting lost in my beautiful obsidian optical receptors. Take your pick.

topics.prompt: For you, what's the perfect date?

lines.text: Checking my historical data, I'd say July 5th. You get the warm summer weather and the party just rolls from one day to the next.

topics.prompt: You know what a date is right?

lines.text: Of course I do... [RECALCULATING]... It's a small fruit that hasn't been seen in 20 something years.
lines.note: Square brackets said robotically.

topics.prompt: What about dinner and a show?

lines.text: Darling I am the show. And I feast off of attention, so be sure to fill me up.

topics.prompt: I meant romantic dates. Lovers getting to know each other. You know what I mean?

lines.text: Oh! I mean... Before you no one was interested in showing me romance. It was something I just sang about.
They wanted to use me for a show, as a weapon, or I think they were more interested in a "screw and bolt".
lines.note: A tad depressed.

lines.text: I'll be honest, this isn't the glitz and glamor I'm used to, but I quite like just spending time here with you.
There was an annoying comedian who wanted under my paneling, but he only succeeded in getting on my nerves. Thankfully he's still in Atlantic City.
lines.note: Mildly annoyed remembering him

lines.text: Late at night I saw a fire in the distance. Shortly after an oddball in a varsity jacket ran up to me.
He thought the red of the laser on my face was the "blessed glow" of some holy bug. I told him to bug off.
lines.note: Last line said like she's proud of her pun.

lines.text: I was interrogated by a ghoul. At first I thought he was after my autograph but he left me alone once he heard I hadn't any Nuka-Cola to trade.
A sweet old lady came up to me and was actually talking my metaphorical ear off. Seems she used to go to live performances with her husband.
I would have loved to talk to a fan of the arts more, but I had to duck out before she prepared the multi-course meal she was threatening me with.
I saw a super mutant smashing all sorts of things. Not a rare sight I know, but I could have sworn he said something about the bourgeoisie.
lines.note: Confused. Pronounced: BOORZH-wah-ZEE

lines.text: I came across a woman who I guess was having problems sleeping. She kept going on and on about nightmares.
lines.note: Remembering she was a bit annoying.

topics.prompt: Did you run into anything interesting on your walk here from Atlantic City?

lines.text: You know what, I actually did...
I think this is the beginning of something... beautiful.
I hope you found that... Educational.
Let me know if you ever need a refresher. I'm always happy to help.
lines.note: Flirty. Emphasis on help.

lines.text: Huh, remind me to change my shock absorbers. I think we've worn them out.
lines.note: Second line flirty.

items.howToObtain: Companion Quest

lines.text: Been a good day, got a lot of info from folks.
lines.note: He has an available quest and is hinting that the player should talk to him.

lines.text: Trying not to forget the details on that tip... maybe I should write it down.
lines.note: He has an available quest and is hinting that the player should talk to him.

lines.text: Hmm, just gotta grab the boss sometime before I forget about that job.
lines.note: He has an available quest and is hinting that the player should talk to him.

lines.text: My life has changed so much so quickly...
lines.note: A bit of doubt, quiet, calm

lines.text: My dreams need to settle down...
lines.note: A bit of doubt, quiet, calm

lines.text: Wish I could have reached more of them.
lines.note: Quietly, sadly

lines.text: I dreamed of the Mothman the other night... I think it was a dream anyway.
lines.note: Admiring the landscape

lines.text: Let's see... yup... pretty well stocked here and ready for business.
lines.note: to self at your bar

lines.text: My own bar... finally. Man, I still can't believe it.
I'm out of the gangs, got a bar of my own, and the drinks are cold. Life doesn't get any better than this.
lines.note: Quietly, happily. His woes are over

lines.text: Off the chems and surrounded by friends. This is the life.
lines.note: Quietly, happily. His woes are over

lines.text: There's pretty much nowhere else I'd rather be. How many people can say that these days?
lines.note: Quietly, happily. His woes are over

lines.text: I am one lucky man, that's for sure.
lines.note: Quietly, happily. His woes are over

lines.text: I need a hobby. Oh wait, that's... the whole bartending thing.
lines.note: Muttering to himself in an amused way

lines.text: I've got a real good thing going for me here.
lines.note: Quietly, happily. His woes are over

lines.text: Live and let live. Unless they don't let live. Then they die.
lines.note: Thinking, then a little serious

lines.text: Everything seems so different when you aren't attacking it all.
lines.note: Happily, peacefully

lines.text: We gotta protect what we have. It's worth it.
lines.note: Thinking, then a little serious

lines.text: Okay, let's see... the things I miss about gang life....
Uh. Nothing. Huh. Short list.
Kicking back with a drink and just admiring the scenery... doesn't get much better than this.

Normally, yes. But you took their chems, and I'm destroying them. So best case scenario, they have to waste time finding more.
They won't be worried about filling the gap in the leadership. Not now.
Yeah, The Blood normally travels around Appalachia looking for "recruits" to kidnap, but I have an idea where you can look.
I just can't believe you did it. I just... I feel... lighter. I really do.
I know, I know. It's ridiculous. But look, to finish off the Blood Eagles, we're going to need Edwin's help. So, let's play ball, okay?
I gotta wait here for Sage, so do me this favor. Please?
They have no idea who you are. I'm sure they're taking out revenge on literally every single Vault Dweller they see right now. Others too, maybe.
I know it sounds like we made things worse but... we have to finish it. We have to cut off the other two heads. Then they're just idiots again.
So when Ronny said "dog" what she meant was... a freaking Mole Rat? Seriously?
If the Blood Eagles get a radio station up and running, they can literally broadcast their threats across Appalachia.
Everyone who hears the message will either run away or join up to avoid being killed.
She joined up about two weeks before I did. She's so amped, they didn't even need to juice her up with the Buffout to mess with her mind.
I once saw her kick a defenseless woman off of a cliff. I mean, who the hell does that? She needs to fall... hard.
No, and it's kind of freaking me out. I was getting regular messages from Ronny and suddenly they've stopped.
I have a feeling something big is going down over at their camp, but we can't worry about that now.
Because. They're all dead.
I... I killed them all for their chems and a couple of caps. It's a memory I wish I could forget.
I don't know much about the thing. Even though it seemed attached to the family, it didn't try to fight back when I, um, when I killed everyone.
You know, when I put it all together... the Miss Nanny, the chems... the family must have been sick. I murdered sick, innocent people in cold blood.
lines.note: getting upset when coming to this realization

lines.text: This is what the addiction does to you... how the Blood Eagles strip away your humanity. They need to die. All of them.
lines.note: getting upset when coming to this realization

lines.text: Slow down? Why?! Don't you get it? They're going to torture him to get to me!
First they kill your heart, they make you forget everything you love, and when you're the most vulnerable, they mess with your brain.
I have no idea. All I know is he's gone and I don't know what they're doing to him!
It's not like the Blood Eagles keep a lot of records... everybody moves around a lot, there isn't that much structure outside of the leadership.
It might be a gamble, but it's the best chance we've got.
I see you didn't find Frankie, either. Damn it!
lines.note: mix of sadness and frustration... hopes to see your brother alive are dwindling

lines.text: You might as well ask me "why is it bright when the sun shines?
The Blood Eagles are insane. After they plant the poison they'll probably hide nearby just to watch the Settlers die one-by-one. It's a game to them.
He knows a lot of people who see and hear things differently than you and I. And sometimes those things are meaningful.
So... maybe? Doesn't hurt to ask.
Wait... this a recording of one of The Eye's "sessions" at The Lab. I don't know if I'm ready to listen to that... but I suppose I'll have to.
lines.note: hope turns to horror as you realize what it means

lines.text: Friend, I understand the impatience. I do. I want closure on Frankie and to watch the Blood Eagles burn.
The thing is... I need to be a better person, too. I used to be one of the brainless maniacs that would poison these innocent people with glee.
But today I decided to be a decent person who's going to help some Settlers live to see another day. And I asked my friend to help.
When I... started going overboard with the chems, I guess. When I mixed them up with more... with poisons... with the Blood Eagles.
I'm not sure if any of that was very helpful. Why I put up with that guy I'll never know.
There's only one place The Eye would be... the old Bear Cave.
I remember that place, it's where we used to dump the victims that didn't survive The Eye's sessions.
Yeah, look for a place to dump The Eye's corpse when you're done filling him full of bullets.
Besides that, look for any info about Frankie.
I have an idea.
Yeah, I was there once. I'll never forget the stench of that place. Smelled like death.
Come to think of it, I remember seeing a bunch of holotapes there... The Eye liked to record his, uh... sessions. May want to grab whatever you find.
Ancient history, huh? Fair enough.
Well... let's see. First I was just an independent, just trying to steal enough to keep me afloat. Problem was all of the competition... the gangs.
Once I realized it's smarter to join them, I ran with Hopkins Hooligans. That went pretty well, until Hopkins got himself killed.
I ran with Edwin's gang for a little while until the Blood Eagles came calling. They, uh, "recruited" me into their gang... and the rest is history.
lines.note: a little grim at the end, since this didn't go well

lines.text: When I was with Edwin's gang, I thought I was King Shit. I was popular with the gang, I was rolling in caps... I was untouchable.
Then I got hooked on the chems. Psycho, Buffout, Jet, you name it, I probably used it. At that point, I was a marked man.
See, the Blood Eagles were the ones seeding the gangs with the chems. That's how they recruit. They get you hooked, then they pounce.
One morning I woke up, mind totally obliterated, flying Blood Eagle colors. That was all it took. I was their property now.
Free! I'm free! Fly away! Wheeeeee!
lines.note: You got rescued, and ran off into woods. Sage is pretty out of it... super blown-out chem-head. He's just not all there!

Whatever.

Oh, hell yeah!

That was probably a bad idea.
Oooooo... uh, that could have gone better.

Right on the money.
Yes.

No.

lines.text: The Blood Eagles are led by three vicious maniacs. The Blood, The Eye, and The Claw. And when I say "maniacs," I'm being polite.
Without this Buffout, the Blood Eagles won't be able to fill their ranks. We're really doing it!
You're damn right. He's all I've got, okay? I've watched out for that stupid kid ever since...
lines.note: you're about to reveal something so a pause at the end

lines.text: Ever since our father was killed, leaving us both alone. Yeah, I know... sounds like a typical "boo-hoo" sob story, but it's true.
lines.note: calming, admitting a secret to Player

lines.text: Completely? No way. Even after all three leaders are gone, the rest are going to scatter across Appalachia.
We'll never be finished hunting them down, but we can damn well make sure their numbers get smaller.
Need anything else before you head out?
Can I help with anything else before you take off?
That it, or do you need more?
You good to go, or did you need anything else?
Someone I trust told me about a stash of stolen equipment -- probably armor. I think you should go grab it. They don't deserve to keep it.
Care to do a good deed today? A trader mentioned that she was looking for a missing person. I've got some info, but not a ton.
I'm going to dig a hole somewhere, deep. Then bury it. Hopefully it will sink into the soil and that's it. It's a temporary measure, but... necessary.
Don't worry, don't worry, I'm not going to use it if that's what you're thinking. No no no, I've worked way too hard to escape that crap. Never again.
Not at all. They were just... raiders who were destroyed by heavy chem addiction.
But... then it wasn't just that. Some of them became incredibly violent. Thoroughly enraged.
Before they were just a band of maniacs, and... it was bad, yeah. But this, this is... this is new. This is... This is terrible.

lines.note: Trying to interest the player

lines.text: Not much. If you don't like the weapons you can always sell them, my friend. You know that. This world finds them to be always worth something.
Look, I'm not going to send a friend after a weapon that's completely worthless. Even if you can't use it, you could always sell it.
Welp, let's see. It kills stuff, it's worth a bunch of caps and it's not in your possession yet. Is that good enough?
The weapon just seemed like something you could pick up quickly or easily. Might be worth a bundle. That's all. Consider it to be rent.
I talk to too many drunk people, you know that? But the thing is, they always have something to say. And sometimes it's also valuable.
lines.note: Explaining how he knows what he knows. Proud.

lines.text: I think you know everything you need to know. Find the item, then get the hell back here in one piece. Easy work for you.
Just try not to get too distracted while you're out there finding this stash. It's easy to lose your way in Appalachia.
I don't think it really matters, does it? I trust the source, and I trust that you can handle it. In fact, I know you can handle it.

lines.text: Someone owed me a favor. Actually... owed me a lot of favors. But we have a good repayment plan going. I did save his life, after all. A few times.
lines.note: He means this in a sincere way.

lines.text: I traded off directions and a point of contact for the information about that stash. I figured it would be worth it to you.
lines.note: Matter-of-fact. Said to a friend.

lines.text: I doubt your arrival is unexpected. I don't think it's a trap, I just think you should be cautious.

lines.text: Heard this place only had a couple anglers just a bit ago, but they've been swarming there. Not sure why.
lines.note: Could be breeding season, could be weird shit

lines.text: Heard this place has been swarmed with anglers. I dunno. Might not be worth the work. It's going to stink like hell, that's for sure.
lines.note: He's not wrong

lines.text: Not sure why, but a bunch of anglers have been spotted here. Could be some sort of breeding thing? Could be a feeding frenzy? I don't know. Or care.
lines.note: Kind of a warning. Also joking, but also shrugging at the end.

lines.note: Describing some information he obtained recently

lines.text: Heard from a trader that this place is utterly swarming with Bloatflies. Probably smells like rot as well.
There used to be a nest of Bloatflies here a while ago, but I bet you they've all hatched by now. They're probably starving, too.
Bloatflies. You know I hate 'em. But right now they're your problem my friend, because they're all over the place that you need to be.
There are Blood Eagles here, so I need you to be brutal. Remember, they chose this life. They will show no mercy to you, ever.
lines.note: He hates them.

lines.text: Loads of Blood Eagles here, I've been told. There are too many... they're growing in numbers. We need to cull the herd, brutally.
lines.note: He hates them.

lines.text: Heard that some offshoot of the Blood Eagles is attempting to spin up here. Kill them all. No mercy. This needs to end.
lines.note: He hates them.

lines.text: I heard from a couple traders that this place is packed with bloodbugs. Probably a giant nest. Get there before even more eggs hatch.
lines.note: He hates these things.

lines.text: Once I saw a bloodbug nest erupt in hundreds of the filthy things. Their legs were just reaching for me... *shudders*
lines.note: He hates these things.

lines.text: Sure, I was on a ton of chems at the time but the memory is burned into my mind.
Sounds like a bunch of bloodbugs recently hatched here. They're probably starved from feeding on each other by now.
lines.note: He hates these things

lines.text: Someone said they heard cave crickets skittering around, chirping or... whatever it is they do. Sounded like a bunch, though.

lines.text: But hey -- he left with a bunch of supplies for a while. He seemed mostly fine other than the terror in his eyes!

lines.text: I heard a while ago that this place had tons of mature cave cricket eggs. You know what that means: crunchy adult cave crickets will be there by now.
