I'll transfer the coordinates to a local military base, but I can't vouch for its security status. It's hard to detect anything specific right now.
lines.note: she is going to send you a location

lines.text: They let me take a crate of personal items! We weren't supposed to be in Deep Sleep the whole time, you know.
lines.note: Pretending to be defensive

lines.text: I'm not sure exactly but... I do know that my ship's auto-pilot took us here to Appalachia for a reason. Maybe this beacon was it.
lines.note: The ship was steering towards something in this area. She thinks it HAS to be connected.

lines.text: I noticed another U.S.S.A. signal approach it a bit ago, and then they both disappeared completely for a moment... and only this one reappeared.
lines.note: This is hinting to the player that it's a robot and that it's an assaultron (because they have cloaking abilities)

lines.text: I'm not sure what that means but... there are only a few reasons why a signal disappears. Death is one of them.
lines.note: She admits that it's possible, but she doesn't want to say for certain. She doesn't know.

lines.text: Yes. I believe the other crew members were in a separate part of the ship. The signal moved a bit. Could be survivors, could be scavengers.
lines.note: Considering the options of what this could be, but not holding onto a lot of hope.

lines.text: Can you find a Scanner Upgrade Module for this? It would help us find so much more, and much more quickly.
lines.note: Asking the player to do the mission

lines.text: Might just be a crate of space food. But maybe it's got some emergency contact codes for the satellites.
lines.note: Asking the player to do the mission

lines.text: Heck, it could even be my personal crate full of my Unstoppables comics that I foolishly brought with me to space. I thought I'd have time...
lines.note: She drifts off at the end here, sort of annoyed, sort of amused that she was so naive.

lines.text: If you grab the beacon, I'm sure whoever is monitoring it will come looking for us. Let's make them find us.
lines.note: Emphasis on *them* -- Let's make THEM find US (for a change).

lines.text: Think you could just... sneak over there and poke your head in? If they seem problematic, maybe... stop them somehow? I don't know.
lines.note: Asking the player to do the mission. Not sure what it is, so she isn't sure how to take care of it. Could be a person or robots or anything.

lines.text: Can you go there and see what's there? It might be just empty wreckage, but I need to know.
lines.note: She isn't sure if she can make it due to the pain of possibly seeing her friends' bodies.

lines.text: Copy that. Just let me know when you have time for this, please.
lines.note: Slightly annoyed that the player isn't willing to help right now, but willing to give them the benefit of the doubt.

lines.text: Okay, but this scanner could be useful to you too. Maybe I can configure it to find resources or valuables or something for you. You know? Ok... bye.
lines.note: Kind of annoyed, but she understands.

lines.text: I hear you. My head has been utterly killing me since the wreck... so go take a break then come back when you have time, maybe?
lines.note: Player is declining quest. Said if the player didn't get the med kit in the intro quest.

lines.text: I hear you, for sure. The Med Kit that you gave me earlier helped a lot but... I'm still having sharp pangs every now and then...
lines.note: Player is declining quest. Said if the player got the med kit in the intro quest.

lines.text: So I'm going to sort of take it easy for a bit, maybe work on the console when I can. Just let me know when you have time.
lines.note: Telling the player to come back soon.

lines.text: Okay, I understand. I really ought to be resting anyway. I'm still recovering from serious trauma, you know? I push myself too much sometimes...
lines.note: Player declined the quest. She hopes they come back some other time, and she realizes she should just take it easy for a bit anyway.

lines.text: No problem. I'll be around here, I've got a lot of work to do with this console anyway.
lines.note: A little set back or put off, but not entirely upset about it. She doesn't really know if she can count on the player anyway.

lines.text: I was thinking about updating the display so I could play a holotape game on it... or something. Hmm.
lines.note: She is a gamer nerd. If the player isn't going to help, she's going to have some fun.

topics.prompt: I'll find a scanner upgrade module for you.

lines.text: Swell. In the meantime, I'll fix up this console a bit. Did you know that it *still* uses the outdated P14-b configuration for its power chamber?
lines.note: She says this like you should know what a shame that is. EMphasis on the Still

lines.text: I mean, I know you all survived the end of the world, but... using this as-is would be like living in squalor *and* the apocalypse.
lines.note: Nerd shaming

lines.text: Hah. I doubt it is. They probably all burned up on re-entry, sadly. I had a full collection... argh!
lines.note: She's sort of joking but not really.

lines.text: Anyway, it's probably astronaut food or something else that the U.S.S.A. thought I might need.
lines.note: She isn't sure what it might be.

lines.text: In the meantime, I'll cross-reference some data from the flight recorder and the scanner's readings. I need to find my crew, and I think I'm close.
lines.note: Player accepted the quest, and she is saying what she will be doing while the player is gone. Nerdy. Excited.

lines.text: Okay. Just... be careful. I wish I could tell what it is but... it just seems so... unnatural. But what does that mean in a world like this?
lines.note: She's surrounded by mutants, so she isn't sure anymore what IS natural.

lines.text: If you do find them, then we'll have to make room for them here. Right? Bunk beds, maybe? There would be three others, you know...
lines.note: She's kind of excited, maybe a little delirious momentarily by the thought of it actually working out.

lines.text: This console looks pretty good. A little rusty in places though... I guess you got these parts from a junkyard, huh? Resourceful.
lines.note: Checking over the console quickly, kicking the tires

lines.text: The scanner currently has a model 38-x2, which is built for scanning very specific locations. Not bad, but... I would like to improve it.
lines.note: Checking it out

lines.text: The year before I launched, the military was rolling out some scanner upgrades. One of those could give us more speed and detail in our scans.
In the meantime, I found some sort of emergency supplies crate that must have splintered off while the ship broke apart.
lines.note: Speculating on what it could be. She is going to send the player off to find this item and she wants to explain why it exists.

lines.text: I found an old U.S.S.A. Beacon with a strong signal. It was activated here after my ship launched...
lines.note: This is mysterious to her. It's not related to her crash.

lines.text: Which means it isn't from someone on my ship, it isn't one of my crew.
lines.note: She's just spelling it out for the player here.

lines.text: The interesting thing is, this beacon should have lost power years ago. But it's still active.
lines.note: She thinks someone is actively monitoring it.

lines.text: It just seemed like after the signal approached this place, it just... spun around and took off. It was strange. Sudden.
lines.note: It's moving around in one location.

lines.text: But... I need to know for sure. I found some wreckage from the rest of the ship that has one of their suit beacons... maybe all of them are there.
lines.note: She needs to know, she needs to put this to rest.

topics.prompt: [Confirm Relationship] We're just friends.

lines.text: I know. I'm just glad we're able to move on together as friends. That's so much more important to me.
lines.note: Glad she can move on.

lines.text: So... did you want to talk about something less depressing, or what?
lines.note: Sort of jokingly

lines.text: Agreed. I'm glad we sorted that out... and it was fun while it lasted. What else is on your mind?
lines.note: Happy she can move on

lines.text: I mean, yeah. That's what I thought too. What else was on your mind, anyway?
lines.note: Neutral. She doesn't know the player well.

lines.text: Well yeah, of course we're friends! So anyway, what's on your mind?
lines.note: Thrilled. Yep, they're still good friends.

lines.text: Roger that, my friend. Got anything else you want to chat about, or is that all?
lines.note: Happy that they're still friends.

lines.text: Of course we're friends! I have to say... we should honestly start some sort of team. Solve mysteries, fight space crime... you know. That stuff.
lines.note: Happy that they're still friends.

lines.text: You mean... like super best friends, right? Right?!
lines.note: Happy that they're super best friends.

lines.text: Hmm, maybe more, huh? All right... I like the cover art to this issue.
lines.note: Jokingly, but interested. Referencing a comic book's cover art.

lines.text: Oh? Do go on... my friend.
lines.note: Said flirtingly. Said with a friendly chuckle at the end.

lines.text: Just maybe, huh? Well. It's a start. My ignition switch has already been started and primed. Just counting down now, my friend.
lines.note: Interested and a bit forward, but in a friendly way

lines.text: Our wavelengths are in harmony on this one. Though I am beginning to think there's less of a "maybe" here...
lines.note: Hinting that they should start the romance now.

topics.prompt: [End Romance] I didn't mean to flirt with you.

lines.text: Oh, okay. That's... unexpected. I wish I had noticed signs that this was coming, but... I didn't.
lines.note: Player is breaking up with her after being in love with her. She's disappointed, sad, hurt, but won't be mad with them.

lines.text: I... hear you, I'm glad you told me. I just... need a moment to myself now, if that's okay.
Gotcha. It happens, don't worry. Glad we cleared that up!
lines.note: Barely knows the player so this isn't a huge deal.

lines.text: Roger that, loud and clear. Over and out!
lines.note: Absolutely okay with this.

lines.text: No problem, friend. Things have been so hectic lately, I completely understand how things could get mixed up between us.
lines.note: Absolutely okay with this.

lines.text: But I am very glad we sorted that out! Phew!
lines.note: Very relieved, and completely okay with this

lines.text: Oh, I see. I must have... I must have mistaken those readings. Is it okay if I blame Deep Sleep for this uh... stellar brain freeze moment?
lines.note: Embarrassed, but absolutely okay with this.

lines.text: I'm glad we cleared that up though. Now, my friend. Where were we?
lines.note: Completely ok with this

lines.text: Oh... okay. I'll survive another crash landing... somehow. Heh.
lines.note: Embarrassed, disappointed, but totally okay with this.

lines.text: It's... okay, my friend. Truly. Thanks for letting me know that I still have an amazing friend here.
lines.note: Completely ok with this

lines.text: That was a smart move, you know. Transferring her sensory link to the other robot.
lines.note: Proud of the player

lines.text: We did the right thing, you know.
I already feel the effects of her connection diminishing... my headaches are still here, but... it's more of a dull ache and less of a stabbing pain.
lines.note: Previously she had terrible headaches.

lines.text: But... it's worth it, I think. She is... free and so am I. Thanks to you, you know.
lines.note: Grateful for the player's choice

topics.prompt: [Start Romance] Everything I did was for you, Sofia.

lines.text: I could tell. At first I wasn't sure, but... over time I knew it was more than that.
lines.note: Begins a Romance if the player has a flirt.

lines.text: I was digging into the Flight Recorder Data some more, and one signal seemed nearby enough to investigate.
lines.note: She's excited she found this data

lines.text: The Upgrade Module is active and I can now pick up more signals around Appalachia. Time to check it out!
lines.note: She's excited she found this data

lines.text: I was tracking this signal and it came right up to the camp then did a full reverse thrusters and went somewhere else.
lines.note: It's a mystery. She's excited!

lines.text: Emerson didn't seem to think that anyone would survive the crash. I get it.
lines.note: Somber, she knows it's unlikely.

lines.text: Emerson didn't seem to think that anyone would survive the crash. I get it.
lines.note: Somber, she knows it's unlikely.

topics.prompt: What's so important about the scanner module?

lines.text: The upgrade module should extend the range of the scanner in our console here rather substantially.
lines.note: Explaining in non-technical terms

lines.text: I can then cross-check some of the U.S.S.A. data that you gathered from my ship's console which will help isolate specific useful signals.
lines.note: Explaining continues

lines.text: Yes, but I'm not sure how accurate the data is or if anything has scavenged it. It's hard to tell much more until I install the upgrade module.
lines.note: It's been a while, could be torn apart by wild animals.

lines.text: It has nearly full power right now. That can only mean someone is still out there replacing its power cell regularly.
lines.note: This means someone is out there.

lines.text: I can't tell what it's doing there exactly, but it's moving around. So... I think it's alive? Or... I guess it could be a robot.
lines.note: She can't tell from the scanner what it is. Could be anything, but the way it moves suggests that it's alive.

lines.text: What are the chances they also ran into a benevolent Appalachian survivor who invited them to live in a charming wilderness abode, anyway?
lines.note: Said in a somewhat desperate attempt at humor.

lines.text: I couldn't have done any of this without you, you know... and that means a lot to me.
lines.note: She is genuinely thankful.

topics.prompt: If I wasn't into this, I would have kicked you out of my C.A.M.P. already.

lines.text: Fair enough. Well. I'm glad I can provide you with some entertainment, my good friend. That means a lot to me, you know.
lines.note: Laughing a bit, or a chuckle.

topics.prompt: I don't have anything else to do, so why not? I like adventure.

lines.text: That's exactly the reason why I became an astronaut. Well. I had plenty to do. I mean the love of adventure, really.
lines.note: Amused, sort of joking.

topics.prompt: You mean... you're not paying me? Geez.

lines.text: That's the spirit! Haha. You always know how to make me laugh. Thank you, my friend.

topics.prompt: Of course, Sofia. I'm here for you. I promise.

lines.text: It means so much after... after everything else has been changed. You've been here for me the whole time.

topics.prompt: Of course. I'm here for you, Commander. I promise.

lines.text: Please... call me Sofia. And thank you.
lines.note: Genuinely grateful to hear this.

lines.text: It means so much after... after everything else has been changed. You've been here for me the whole time.
lines.note: Solemn mixed with gratittude.

topics.prompt: Well? What did you find out?

lines.text: Succinctly? I was the experiment, and Emerson knew everything. I think they were hooking me up to some sort of robotic intelligence named Athena.
I think the serum was used to open my neural pathways to allow the Athena unit to borrow my senses.
lines.note: She's angry, cold... this was a cruel thing that they did to her.

topics.prompt: What is Athena?

lines.text: I've seen... fragments mentioning this before, here and there. I remember some conversations from before launch.
lines.note: She's remembering.

lines.text: I thought it was just someone who worked at the U.S.S.A. but... this has to be some sort of primitive robotic intelligence, I think. What else?

topics.prompt: Your crew died because of Emerson.

lines.text: I know... no wonder he didn't think they were alive. He knew those pods weren't in the right part of the ship. What was he thinking?
lines.note: Sighs, angry.

topics.prompt: What should we do next?

lines.text: Well... it sounds to me like we need to find whatever this "Athena" thing is and destroy it. Somehow. But I doubt it's a regular robot.
lines.note: Worried, unsure. Something about this is familiar though.

topics.prompt: What should we do about Emerson?

lines.text: He says he's a changed man, but can anyone change this much? I don't know. I really don't.
lines.note: Unsure of his ability to change from a devious conniver to anything better in 30 years.

lines.text: So... this was their plan all along. And they were all involved. All of them. Especially Emerson.
lines.note: Angry. Disappointed. Betrayed. Everyone she thought she trusted was actually out to get her.

topics.prompt: [Lie] Sure. It was... you know. Intense and stuff.

lines.text: Ah... okay. I will have to give it a listen for myself, I think... one moment.
lines.note: She's skeptical that the player actually did that.

lines.text: Hmm... okay.
lines.note: She's listening to the holotape and muttering to herself.

topics.prompt: Yes. You were the experiment, my friend.

lines.text: Uh. What? Let me listen to this.
lines.note: Worried, upset, a little frantic. She has to listen to the holotape for herself.

topics.prompt: A little bit. I got distracted.

lines.text: Okay, give me a moment to listen to it, then we can talk about it.

topics.prompt: Yeah. You should listen to it right now.

lines.text: Okay, doing so now. Won't take me long.
lines.note: Nodding, sensing this is important.

topics.prompt: Nah. I just figured it was boring.

lines.text: That may be true! Give me a moment, I'll see.
lines.note: Laughing a bit.

topics.prompt: I'll go get those medical records.

lines.text: Listen, I know you've done a lot for me already. Got me out of that sunken bunker and let me stay here. It means a lot.
lines.note: Grateful, tired but grateful. She knows it could have been worse.

lines.text: If you don't mind, I'm going to continue scanning the console and listening to stray broadcast signals. It'll help me figure out what's going on.
lines.note: Trying not to get overwhelmed. Nervous

lines.text: If you find anything, bring it back here if it seems useful. If it's astronaut food well... you can uh, keep it.
lines.note: Said as she turns back to do her work. She doesn't know the player well. She's also sick of astronaut food at this point.

lines.text: Remember, when you pick up the beacon, whatever you do -- do not press any red buttons, do not ingest it, and do not sell it to communists.
lines.note: jokingly, just covering her bases.

lines.text: Listen, this could be a trap... or it could be just a big misunderstanding. I can't really say for sure. Just be careful.
It's possible that you won't find anything there. It might just be rubble or... maybe it's been scavenged by animals. It's hard to know.
lines.note: She expects the player to find nothing. She's kind of hoping they won't find anything.

lines.text: In the meantime, I picked up an Unstoppables comic book from a visiting trader the other day. Maybe it will help me relax...
lines.note: She isn't sure if it will help, but she needs to get some rest.

lines.text: It's probably just as hostile as the last Robot. So be careful.
Thanks, friend. I wonder if I can play some music from this console... Hmm. Oh, I don't think it has speakers... hmm...
lines.note: Thankful that the player is doing this for her.

lines.text: Anyway, be careful out there. I'll be around if you need anything or want to talk.
lines.note: Friendly, neutral. She considers the player to be an okay new friend.

lines.text: Thanks, friend. I got some Sugar Bombs from a trader while you were out last... I might plow through a box. Or ten. I need some comfort food.
lines.note: Half-serious, half-joking. She is anxious about all of this.

lines.text: I know this has been a lot of running around for you. I wish I could be out there too, but recovering from these headaches has been tricky...
Resting has helped a lot. Besides... I kind of like being the technical wizard here. We make a good team, you know?
lines.note: She means it.

lines.text: Thanks, friend. I'm going to scan the area for any more robots, at least that way I can keep myself busy and not be entirely pissed off.
lines.note: Appreciative, annoyed, trying to be less annoyed.

lines.text: I feel like we're a strong team here. I investigate leads and you do the field work.
lines.note: Genuinely excited.

lines.text: It's like that issue of the Unstoppables with the Mistress of Mysteries and her team finally locate the lair -- er. Anyway. Good luck out there.
lines.note: Excitedly geeking out then reigning herself back in.

lines.text: Anyway. Good luck out there.
lines.note: Said before sending the player on a mission.

lines.text: Already sent. While you're out, I'm going to track down that Robobrain that Emerson mentioned...
lines.note: Thinking about it. She wonders if it is really a huge threat.

lines.text: Be careful. We know this thing is probably deranged.
If you want to listen to the holotape, go ahead. It's not like anyone can do anything about it, you know.
lines.note: What can they do... sue you?

lines.text: Everything I knew is turning upside down. Everything... except for you. You're the only person I can still trust.
lines.note: Grateful to the player for being there.

lines.text: This is it. After this... when you get back... we have to prepare to confront this thing. Please be careful. Please.
lines.note: Very concerned about the player.

lines.text: Confirmed at least a few Sentry Bot signatures at this location, and seemed like they were signaling for more.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: I thought this was a joke at first, but... nope, the scanner indicated that at least one Sheepsquatch is at this spot.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: Did you know it's Sheepsquatch mating season? I actually just made that up because I have no idea how else to explain why so many are at this place.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: Scanner was picking up a vocalization at a very specific resonance: Sheepsquatch mating signals. Might just be one loner, could be... more.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: Snallygasters. The scanner was absolutely dead clear about this.
I thought I was tracking a single Snallygaster but it turned out to be many of them. Good luck, friend.
I found a group of Snallygasters who are hunting together. I mean... is that wild or what? Do you think they're a family?
There was one huge signal like a massive cloud that was circling this spot. I did a second sweep on the data, and it's really dozens of Stingwings.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: The environmental data from this location indicates that if any Stingwing eggs were laid here recently, they would be hatched by now. Beware.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: This area is full of Stingwing signals on the scanner. They move quicker than the signal refresh rate on my console, so I don't even know how many.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: A gang of Super Mutants have taken over this spot. Or... clan? Or... family? I actually don't know how their social unit is organized... hm.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: Of course, it's overrun with Super Mutants. So, you know. Be careful.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: Scanner picked up some Super Mutants at the location, and more in the peripheral areas.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: I've been tracking this mess of signatures for a while now... and all I can say for sure is that they're aggressive and there are a lot of them.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: Scanners indicate that the area is full of something strange. I've only seen these signatures in the swamps, so... swamp creatures, I'd guess?
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: Got some strange signals here. Swarms of... something unusual. Something possibly dangerous. Be careful, there are a lot of them... whatever they are.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: I scanned this place just a bit ago and there was nothing... but just scanned it again and it's swarming with Ticks. They move way too quickly!
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: I'm getting signals here indicating blood in the air and tiny creatures moving very quickly in a pack. That means you should expect to encounter Ticks.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: The scanner is showing an abundance of small creatures and traces of blood in the air. Probably Ticks, and it's likely a nest of them.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: This place is packed with hungry, aggressive Rad Toads. I saw some Stingwing signatures fly in here and then suddenly disappear...
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: I checked the recent temperature, radiation levels, and wind data... and the Rad Toad eggs at this location definitely hatched recently. Beware.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: There are some Radtoads here. On the scanner, they stay still for a while and then bustle with activity if anything else wanders up. Fun to watch!
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: There are so many Vicious Dogs here that the scanner isn't able to give me a decent headcount.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: I've been monitoring another pack of Vicious Dogs and they ended up circling this spot for a while before settling in. Expect them to defend it now.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: I've been tracking this pack of wild Vicious Dogs for a while on the scanner, and they've decided to settle down here. Be careful.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: I've been tracking this pack of hungry wolves for a while. They got chased into this place and it's now their territory. They'll defend it, too.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: The scanner picked up activity in this area, and judging by the movement of the creatures, it seems like it's a good old fashioned Wolf pack. Beware.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: This particular pack of Wolves disappeared for a while. I figured they left the area. But their signals appeared again at this location recently.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: There are a ton of Yao Guai in this area according to the scanner. Not sure why, but... just be careful.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: I thought I was tracking one Yao Guai, but then another few showed up. Could be a family of them for all I know. Be alert.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: Scanner picked up one Yao Guai at first, but more have arrived since then. Not sure why. Just be careful, more could be incoming.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: So, let's intercept one of the U.S.S.A. robots that is heading this way. I want to know why they're doing this.
lines.note: She's reasoning it out. Determined to move forward, despite being very sad about the deaths of her crew.

lines.text: Okay, let's think about this logically. Either this is actually a high security tape or it is mislabeled somehow. Right?
lines.note: Rhetorical question.

lines.text: Let's... assume it's real for now. They used to make us listen to these whalesong tapes while we were using the Deep Sleeper Pods.
lines.note: She's working through the situation, trying to link it to something that makes sense.

lines.text: Hmm... "suspension of living tissue" is right... not sure about the cyclic energy transfer stuff... I guess that could be anything though.
lines.note: She's reading along with the document.

lines.text: Two things jump out at me here though: something about sensory data transfers and...
lines.note: She's listing the generally concerning issue first...

lines.text: And the fact that Emerson was the supervisor. What the hell?
lines.note: She is feeling betrayed a little, but she is going to give him an opportunity to explain.It's shocking, though. Surprised, Angry, Shocked

lines.text: We need to find that contract, I think. I want to know what that serum... did.
lines.note: Curious, annoyed. That serum could have done permanent damage to her. Maybe it caused her headaches?

lines.text: I might be able to find a correlation somewhere associated with the timestamps... it's just a matter of finding out where they stored their backup data.
lines.note: Pondering... this is information for a future mission.

lines.text: I've pinpointed one of them using Emerson's tip, so let's start with this one.
lines.note: Asking the player to do the mission. Emerson told them to look for certain kinds of signals last time he visited, and she has now done that.

lines.text: The signal's signature is tagged with a code that indicates it is a high security holotape related to the Deep Sleep mission.
lines.note: Excited, eager -- this could mean something huge!

lines.text: So... let's see if we can dig up anything on the pods themselves. Documentation, user manuals, Dr. Bernard's designs, anything really.
lines.note: It doesn't make sense. It's like keeping a receipt from McDonald's.

lines.text: Okay, here's my plan. I found some old medical data from the U.S.S.A. stored nearby, and I want you to look for a copy of my records there.
lines.note: Determined. She knows this should have some information.

lines.text: If this stuff caused my headaches, then maybe they... made an antidote? It's... it's a start anyway.
lines.note: Determined but a bit exasperated. She isn't sure where to go from here.

lines.text: In the meantime, let's just eliminate that rogue U.S.S.A. robot that's lurking around monitoring us? It gives me the creeps.
lines.note: Shivering at the end. What are these things reporting to anyway?

topics.prompt: [Confirm Relationship] We're more than friends.

lines.text: Oh! I've got a good one here. Ok. Brace yourself.
lines.note: Said jokingly

lines.text: I may have crashed into Earth, but you crashed into my heart. Yeah, right?!
lines.note: Dad joke. She ends it like HEYYY HOW WAS THAT?!

lines.text: Uh. Anyway...
lines.note: Jokingly, embarrassed a bit, changing the subject

lines.text: Was there ever any doubt?! What else is on your mind, my love?
lines.note: Said lovingly

lines.text: Duh! Okay, I got another one.
lines.note: Said jokingly

lines.text: It actually *did* hurt when I fell from the heavens... Falling for you, though, that felt much better.
lines.note: Cackles madly at the end of it all...

lines.text: Geez, I should say that one more often. Anyway... what's on your mind, lover?
lines.note: Recovering from laughter, jokingly.

lines.text: You better believe it. Got anything else you want to talk about, my love?
lines.note: In love

lines.text: I love you too.
lines.note: Pleasant but matter-of-fact

lines.text: I know. I've known for a bit... and, well, I love you too. I really do. It feels so good to finally say it.
I'm... relieved. I wanted to tell you the same thing for a bit now but... I wasn't sure if you were ready.
I was hoping you would say that...

topics.prompt: Enjoy the games, Commander.

lines.text: You better believe it.
Oh, wow. Wow! I didn't even think to ask... I just figured, what with the world and all that people might stop making games...
lines.condition: HasCompletedChallenge: Challenge_Lifetime_Collect_Holotape_Games_Automatron "Collect the Holotape Game: Automatron", GetValue: Astronaut_PlayerGave_HolotapeGame_Automatron

lines.text: This is amazing, the best... I can't wait to play this. Thank you so much, my friend. My... best friend in the whole world. Wee!
lines.condition: HasCompletedChallenge: Challenge_Lifetime_Collect_Holotape_Games_Automatron "Collect the Holotape Game: Automatron", GetValue: Astronaut_PlayerGave_HolotapeGame_Automatron
lines.note: She says the last part jokingly.

topics.prompt: I'll copy some games to your console.

lines.text: There's nothing quite like curling up with a good game. This brightens my day.

topics.prompt: Want a copy of my Grognak Holotape game?

lines.text: You're looking at the reigning East Coast Champion of the Ruby Ruins, my friend.
And yes -- for the record, I would love to play it even more. Transfer it to my console?

topics.prompt: Thanks for the chat, Commander.

lines.text: Anytime... Commander.

topics.prompt: I'll be back later, Sofia.

lines.text: I hope you won't be gone for too long...
lines.note: Smiling, happy.. saying goodbye

lines.text: Initiating the countdown until you return...
lines.note: Flirty, fun

lines.text: I'll be here, friend.

topics.prompt: I'll be back later, Commander.

lines.text: It's pretty clear to me that you're fond of me, and... if things weren't so chaotic right now, if I didn't have these headaches all the time... well.
lines.note: Player has flirted. She acknowledges that. They're also friends. She likes the player and may be okay with continuing.

lines.text: I think I could see you that way too. Does that make sense?
lines.note: She's asking the player if those feelings are right.

lines.text: I'll be honest. At first I sort of though you were... just bored, I guess. But it truly seems like you care.
lines.note: Player has flirted. She acknowledges their good friendship as well. She likes the player and may be okay with a romance later. Not now.

lines.text: You're really starting to grow on me, you know that? What's your take on this anyway?
lines.note: Said with a grin. She likes where this is all headed.

lines.text: I... I'm glad you asked. I wanted to talk to you about this, but I wanted to see how you felt, first.
lines.note: She wants to talk about whether there's more here. Starts the Romance scene.

topics.prompt: I have something else to say, may or may not be SPECIAL.

lines.text: My best guess is... a program? Or another Robot?
I just feel in my gut that Arachne is the key. To everything.
lines.note: Scared, mad

lines.text: Not surprised. While you were there, I saw a bunch of blips for other U.S.S.A. Robobrains that had been destroyed over the years.
lines.note: Informing the player of a new angle

lines.text: And there were a great many of them around some old U.S.S.A. Data facilities. Trying to get inside for some reason? I don't know.

topics.prompt: Let's talk about the world.

lines.text: I thought about it a lot. For a while, I thought... what is the point of comics? Of games?
lines.note: Depression, sadness

lines.text: Seemed like such a distraction from the stress in my life, from finding out the truth, from fixing what was left...
lines.note: She is about to find some meaning in all of these woes.

lines.text: But I realized that it's not only a distraction. Enjoyment is a fundamental part of life, even a stressful life.
lines.note: This was a realization for her.

lines.text: And you know what? I am still stressed and trying to fix my life... but it's easier to remember why I care when I can still feel joy.
lines.note: It's easier to remember because she finds joy in the world.

lines.text: Maybe. For all I know, there could be other astronauts stranded up there in other experiments.
lines.note: She gets quiet, this is upsetting.

lines.text: Or maybe some of them went to work for other programs and are trying to save what's left of the world. I wish I knew, my friend. I wish I knew.
lines.note: She wants to believe.

lines.text: I assume you mean, do I feel like my mind is being toyed with for some nefarious purpose?
I don't know. I feel like... me. But how can I even trust my own feelings?
I don't know where else I would go. Everyone I knew is probably long gone by now...
lines.note: Because they have aged also 25 years and there was the war, so it's unlikely anyone survived.

lines.text: I think I'll stay here and watch out for you, for a change. It's only fair, my friend.
lines.note: Smiling at the end. Telling the player she won't disappear.

lines.text: Not much. Headaches still come and go, and it's hard to sleep through those. I'd give anything for these headaches to end.
lines.note: Sighs at the end.

topics.prompt: Let's talk about the world.

lines.text: When you were out the other day, I tried to shoot some sort of giant insect. Took... a lot longer than I thought. I'm working on it, though!
Yes. A protectron has been circling the camp. It hasn't approached yet though, so I'm going to monitor it for data, and then we can go after it.
lines.note: She isn't sure why it's doing this.

lines.text: I think it's collecting data about us, so I'm waiting to see who it's sending the data to, if I can...
lines.note: Almost whispering, unsure if the robot can hear them.

lines.text: He's always seemed a bit odd, honestly. Even back before I launched. We used to be friends in college, but... people change so much in college.
lines.note: Acknowledging the player's instinct

lines.text: Strange. I haven't really considered it much. I just... can't imagine anything beyond these headaches right now, and finding out what they did...
But... I guess, well. I hope whatever happens, we're still together. We make a good team, friend.
lines.note: A little flirty but not too heavily.

topics.prompt: Let's talk about you, Commander.

lines.text: Truthfully? It was a blur. We were sent up as a team and were in our deep sleep pods in under an hour after achieving a stable orbit.
But that single hour... It was exhilarating.
You know... I did. What does that mean, I wonder? It was a sudden spike right behind the eyes.
lines.note: They are linked, but she doesn't know how.

lines.text: Oh, sure. Let's see. I don't really want to talk about my family because, well, I don't even know if they... *sighs*
Ok, so... hobbies. I had a small apartment near the U.S.S.A. headquarters. Nothing special. I wasn't home much, you see.
When I had time, I used to go to the comic book shop down the road and sit and drink coffee and read the latest issues of the Unstoppables.
I used to want to work for the Mistress of Mystery when I was a kid, you see.
But I did the next best thing, I guess, and went to space.
No, I think I know what I need to know about you... and I'm impressed. You're tough... resilient. And I respect that.
lines.note: She is genuinely impressed.

lines.text: No, you've answered my question well. We're on the same wavelength, and I think that's going to carry us far as a team. I'm relieved, honestly.
lines.note: Grateful, relieved, happy to find someone like her.

lines.text: Nope, I know everything I need to know. You're a natural leader, and I can absolutely work with that.
lines.note: She's impressed with the player's charisma.

lines.text: Not really. I don't really believe in luck that much, but... I am truly intrigued.
lines.note: Fascinated by the player's luck.

lines.text: No, friend. Not really. This world is chaotic and strange, but together we can survive. That's my hope anyway.
lines.note: She feels pretty confident about this.

lines.text: This world is so peculiar, so dangerous... and I just am amazed at the fact that life continues. You know?
lines.note: Truly impressed that anyone is still alive.  Leads into the next scene question, "So... how did you survive?" File 0056F6F3_1

lines.text: I mean, who doesn't, right?
You don't happen to have any, do you? Now that would be a warm blanket on a cold night right about now.
It's been soothing to play games again -- a few moments of normalcy once more. I think it even helps my headache a bit.
They come and go in spikes. It's really pronounced at times. Haven't had one in a while... I wonder if there's a pattern to them.
lines.note: Thinking about it, concerned.

topics.prompt: Tell me about space, Sofia.

lines.text: When they strapped me into the capsule, I knew anything might happen.
Could crash into a million pieces. Could fling us off course and off into who knows where. I even joked to myself about seeing aliens...
I never -- ever -- thought that we might be the last people to see Earth from up there, though.
I hope we can return someday... there's so much that we need to do to get us back in that position though.
Oh -- wait. I was supposed to say something like... "No, I've got all I need right here." Right? *laughs*
lines.note: She says the quoted part in a sweet, but slightly sarcastic way.

lines.text: Well, both of those things are true.

topics.prompt: Let's talk about these missions.

lines.text: Sort of. Right before you killed it, the robot sent out some signals to specific targets. I think it pinged my console, too.
lines.note: She seems frustrated because she isn't sure WHY this happened, she only knows what happened.

lines.text: It was hard to tell if anything changed though. My headache was back in full force so I had to lie down... I could barely see.
lines.note: She feels awful for missing the crucial data due to her headache.

lines.text: I expect that another U.S.S.A. Robot will be activated and sent after us soon, so maybe we can try again.
lines.note: Defiant because there's another chance that they can take, but she also wishes she had more data now, so a little embarrassed perhaps.

lines.text: Just whalesong, repeating... so pleasant. Headaches sort of melted away...
Dr. Bernard was one of the scientists that I worked with in the U.S.S.A., he was an engineer. Mostly mechanical.
lines.note: Thinking back

lines.text: I knew he had developed the sleeping pods for this mission, so that wasn't particularly new information for me. But...
lines.note: With a giant "BUT..." at the end

lines.text: It looks like there's something about the sleeping pod establishing a sensory link between the user and... something else. I don't know what that is.
lines.note: Confused, annoyed

lines.text: And also... Emerson was the supervisor for this project. So he absolutely does know what this was about. In detail.
He has to be hiding something. I need to know what happened... I need to know what he knows.
lines.note: Annoyed the player suggested it.

lines.text: No, nothing. Looks like it was going on for... years. How? How could this have happened without me knowing anything?
The year or two prior to going on the mission we just tried to relax. They gave us meditation tapes so we could get adjusted to the silence of space.
lines.note: She's thinking back...

lines.text: Some people had white noise, others had thunderstorm sounds... I listened to whale songs...
lines.note: She sighs

lines.text: Clearly whale songs were more effective than I thought.
lines.note: It was brain washing her

topics.prompt: [SPECIAL] I have something SPECIAL to say.

lines.text: That is not how it was presented to us. It was supposed to maintain our ambient health levels and that's it. Nothing else.
The schematics say the pod was designed to help transfer sensory data. To what end?
lines.note: She needs to know why she was experimented on.

lines.text: Agreed. It seems like some sort of experimental bio-medical formula. It might be worth checking records about Arktos. Maybe they knew something?
Sure... maybe that will help with the pain. Dr. Bernard was our engineer, worked exclusively on the Sleeping Pods. Very by-the-books type guy.
Specialist Nowak had been on a few missions before this one. Always seemed distracted. But, well, it was a stressful mission.
lines.note: Pronounced Novock

lines.text: Dr. Lee was our ship's engineer and a robotics expert. We all went out to celebrate the night before lift off.
It feels like it was only yester... day.
lines.note: She trails off in the middle of the word "yesterday" because she realizes it was actually decades ago.

lines.text: I guess it doesn't matter if it feels like it was only yesterday. It was a long time ago, and... they're gone.
They're... strange. For a while, I felt like they were non-stop, but I think it's actually a sharp ping followed by a moderate dull ache.
In a way... the cycle of pain is sort of fascinating. I wonder if my brain is thawing?
I don't think that was how it worked, but... I'm not a medical doctor. Dr. Bernard would have known, he built the sleeping pod.
I technically had some training with firearms before, part of the military boot camp prior to becoming an astronaut.
It's not much, but... maybe I'll brush off those skills and start practicing. Just in case.

topics.prompt: [Flirt] How are we doing, Commander?

lines.text: We really do. In this world, it's hard to imagine how anybody can survive all alone anymore.
lines.note: She thinks about how different it could have been. Being alone would be sad.

lines.text: I'm glad I don't have to be alone.
lines.note: It could be bad if she was alone, she realizes

lines.text: And I'm very glad that I'm here with you.
Call me Sofia... please. After all we've been through. After all, I'm in your... ship now. That makes you the Commander here.
lines.note: Affectionate turns into a little flirty

lines.text: Okay. I'm from Chicago, parents moved there when I was little...
After college, I went to the D.C. area and applied for the astronaut program a couple times until I was accepted. My folks were so proud...
Hmm... other than that... I had a few relationships. Nothing serious.
Had a pet turtle for most of my life. That *was* pretty serious.
I dunno. That's the high level overview anyway. I'm not a weirdo, if that was what you were asking.
Well, right now I think we need to track down some medical records. Then maybe we can...
lines.note: Trails off at the end

lines.text: Oh! Oh... hmm. I'll keep that in mind, friend. Uh. *clears throat*
lines.note: Sheepish, taken entirely off guard.

lines.text: It is, it really is. I know I've said it before, but thanks for letting me uh... crash here. *laughs*
lines.note: She made a bad joke / pun because she crashed her spaceship near the player and they let her stay with them.

topics.prompt: Let's talk about these missions.

lines.text: I hear you. I thought they were coming after me, but I'm not sure. Maybe they have other motives, too. Safer to just deal with them, though.
lines.note: Fixed typo in "Safer

lines.text: The Serum is partially synthetic, and... the injector won't even really work with human blood vessels.
It was produced a year or two after I went to space, interestingly enough.
lines.note: Thinking about it

lines.text: I think the one that you retrieved wasn't made for human usage at all. I... think it was made for a Robobrain.
I found one U.S.S.A. Robobrain that might have been subjected to it. And... that's where I'm at with the research here.
lines.note: Where she's at in terms of the research

lines.text: It was a board meeting between the U.S.S.A. and some corporations. They were talking with my crew after I was inside the Sleeping Pod.
I was asleep in the pod when this was recorded... and, well, it sounded like they were all in on the experiment and I was the subject.
They were, however, forced to partake in the same experiment against their wills. It doesn't bring me joy to hear it... but they did deserve it.
They were connecting me to some external A.T.H.E.N.A. unit. And Emerson was there. So he knew everything this whole time. Because he did it all.
It has to be a prototype for something bigger. That's all I can figure. I'm going to need additional samples to know more though, I think.
It should give us, well, access to the A.T.H.E.N.A. unit, which will allow us to use the Arachne program and delete the connection entirely.
In theory, I'll be free. No more headaches. Free.
lines.note: Scared but also glad.

topics.prompt: [SPECIAL] I have something SPECIAL to say.

lines.text: I thought maybe it was a corrupt command sent out to a source console somewhere. It was just "Red Sunset" and that's it.
lines.note: Giving information very matter of factly.

lines.text: Oh, interesting... "Blue Sunset" permits data access and "Red Sunset" makes these U.S.S.A. Robots hostile... maybe we can use that.
I shot three flying insects while you were dealing with the U.S.S.A. Robot, and I didn't miss a single time.
Then I traded their parts to Grahm when he passed by... and well. Here. You can have this stuff, I don't need it.
lines.note: Proud. Giving the player something. Grahm is pronounced GROM.

lines.text: Oh! Oh gosh. There was a whole story arc like this! She used the Phantom device to sneak into the Mechanist's lair with the Shroud at her side!
lines.note: She is thrown back into a memory.

lines.text: The other Unstoppables were captured one by one... it was so dramatic over several issues! Fans thought it was over. It seemed so dire...
But together, they stopped an entire robot army from taking control of unsuspecting citizens and they rescued the other Unstoppables.
lines.note: Recapping a story arc that she loved.

lines.text: Thank you for the reminder... that was encouraging! Inspiring! Not sure if I have those issues, but take these. They should give you courage, too!
lines.note: She is feeling brave again!

topics.prompt: [Flirt] How are we doing, Sofia?

lines.text: You're a conundrum, my friend. I thought about the Manta Man, but... there's something peculiar about you. Something delightfully unpredictable.
lines.note: Said because the player has high Luck. This line is very similar to a few others, with some changes.

lines.text: Oh! Be still, my beating heart! That sounds like a dream come true, my dear friend. But also, you don't stand a *chance*!
lines.note: Excited that the player is offering. Maybe some joyful giggles at the end. She's being playful.

lines.text: I don't know what my future holds, but... I hope you're there, and I hope we're together.
lines.note: Sincere, very loving, flirty.

lines.text: We can do this -- together. I trust you, my friend, my... Commander to Commander.
lines.note: She got the feels. Said affectionately then it becomes a little reals.

lines.text: You know, I'm not very eager to plan a new long term mission quite yet. Let's just take it one day at a time. Okay?
lines.note: Reasonable approach

lines.text: After everything that happened, you were always there for me. Always.
I'll always feel safe here -- with you.
Really? I was worried for a bit that you might be unenthused about taking care of some random stray.
lines.note: Amused that the player is flirty.

lines.text: Even though my options were clearly heavily limited by the uh... entire world situation... the only decent thing so far has been meeting you.
lines.note: Flirting back, not that strongly

lines.text: We've been through so much already. I hope you know that I care about you a lot, right? I feel like you care about me, too.
lines.note: She is saying that they're very close and it could become something more than this, if the player wants to take it there.

lines.text: And if that care becomes something more -- if you want it to -- then I would want to explore that too.
lines.note: Emphasis on "if you want it to

lines.text: But as long as you and I are together, doing what's best for each other and for the world... well, that's what matters to me the most, my friend.
lines.note: My dear, kind, wonderful friend.

lines.text: With your charming demeanor, could you be anything other than my dear Shroud? But... you already knew that, didn't you?
lines.note: Said because the player has high Charisma. This line is very similar to a few others, with some changes. Sultry.

lines.text: If we're dressing up, I presume? Hm. I like it. Well, of course... you're the Inspector. I think that's obvious. I've seen how your mind works.
lines.note: Said because the player has high Int or Perception. This line is very similar to a few others, with some changes.

lines.text: Did you really think you weren't some form of Grognak? I mean... you're kind of a monster. A... *very* likeable monster, mind you.
lines.note: Said because the player has high Strength, Endurance, or Agility. This line is very similar to a few others, with some changes. Emphasis on the Very.

lines.text: Thank you, my dear, kind friend. I've come to think of your place as my home. And I've come to think of you as... more than a friend, too.
lines.note: Flirty, nervous, sincere.

lines.text: I know I can depend on you, and that you care about me... and that means a lot to me. And I care about you too.
lines.note: It could be more if the players wants to go there.

lines.text: Er, I mean... we're a great team together! We're hunting down my tortured past, righting the wrongs and trying to build a better tomorrow, together!
lines.note: She got too close to being squishy romantic and decided to pull back a bit so not to pressure the player.

lines.text: But seriously, I sort of think we should start our own team when all this is said and done. Rebuild Appalachia by righting all the wrongs! Together!
lines.note: Excited, still recovering from a close call with the Feels

topics.prompt: [Flirts] ATHENA was saved.

lines.text: Until the end, I thought I was just going to die or become some sort of brainless host to a crazed robot. You're my lucky rabbit's foot, you know.
Well, I get to spend it at this fancy campsite with a great person. So I'd say, you know, pretty good all things considered.
They're slowly diminishing. I think... in time, they will be gone entirely. It's mostly manageable now, though.
For the record, it was worth it.
I suppose it's in A.T.H.E.N.A. now. Maybe that makes me part of her, in some way?
It took a lot of guts to do what you did. But you saved two lives, you know that? You're a hero.
Headaches are present but diminishing regularly. No more sharp spikes of pain, just a dull brain ache really.
I hope she is wandering around, experiencing anything she wants. She deserves the freedom.

topics.prompt: Ever think about Emerson?

lines.text: I don't think I'll think about him anymore. I need to purge all of that from my mind, honestly.
lines.note: Emerson betrayed her.

lines.text: He was a problematic person even back then, and... I knew that. That's why we were only friends. I could tell something was off about him.
But... it's been decades. I can tell he's different now, of course... but I don't think I can care about him anymore.
She stops by from time to time, and is different every time. More and more enthralled with the world.
lines.note: ATHENA is the Assaultron AI

lines.text: I'm not sure exactly what her future holds, but she seems incredibly happy to listen to birds or collect junk... I don't know. She seems happy.
lines.note: Sofia is happy for her

lines.text: She was in pain, friend. I thought my headaches were bad, but... her existence was torture. You did what she asked.
lines.note: Player deleted the ATHENA unit, killing her.

lines.text: That was a mercy, and... it takes a lot of compassion to grant such a thing in this world, I think.
lines.note: She's impressed the player could do it.

lines.text: He stops by from time to time to check on me. I'll allow it... only because I know he's learned from all of this.
lines.note: Player deleted the ATHENA unit, killing her, Emerson continues to visit.

lines.text: Things will never be okay between us. We'll never chat like we used to. Those days are gone. But I'll let him visit. That's all.
lines.note: Shrugs. He is what he is.

lines.text: I do like seeing the variety of life in Appalachia. It's so odd, so strange. Sometimes I think I should have been a botanist or a biologist.
lines.note: Musing about the location

lines.text: I've adjusted the scanner so it should be able to continue to pick up good signals around here, at least.
lines.note: Technical business

lines.text: Before going to space? Sure. Of course. I mean... it wasn't so long ago to me, you know?
But I'm trying to remind myself actively that it's over. It's like walking through a door and closing it behind me.
lines.note: She's come to peace with this

lines.text: Almost everybody I knew is behind that door, and it's just... right there. So close I can hear them. But the door is locked, and the key is gone.
lines.note: Trying to explain the separation

topics.prompt: [Flirts] ATHENA was killed.

lines.text: You kept your promise.
Believe me, my brain thanks you immensely. I haven't felt this... normal... for, well, decades? *laughs*
But I knew I could have, and I knew you'd have my back.
Everything is so much clearer now. So calm.
I know you made the right call. I know you thought through all of the potential outcomes. I trust your judgment here entirely.
And you kept your word.
Same thing we do every other day, my friend. We try to destroy the systems of oppression that somehow survived the end of the world.
And... we make sure to keep an eye out for the best equipment so we can do it better, and in style.
Listen, I know you've done a lot for me already. Got me out of that sunken bunker and let me stay here. It means a lot.
lines.note: Grateful, tired but grateful. She knows it could have been worse.

lines.text: Remember, when you pick up the beacon, whatever you do -- do not press any red buttons, do not ingest it, and do not sell it to communists.
lines.note: jokingly, just covering her bases.

lines.text: Listen, this could be a trap... or it could be just a big misunderstanding. I can't really say for sure. Just be careful.
It's possible that you won't find anything there. It might just be rubble or... maybe it's been scavenged by animals. It's hard to know.
lines.note: She expects the player to find nothing. She's kind of hoping they won't find anything.

lines.text: In the meantime, I picked up an Unstoppables comic book from a visiting trader the other day. Maybe it will help me relax...
lines.note: She isn't sure if it will help, but she needs to get some rest.

lines.text: Some government and military holotapes are easier to pinpoint than others, depending on whether they're in a tracked depot.
These bureaucratic depots are the trickest to pin down.
It's probably in a bin full of unrelated government documents, holotapes, and other junk.
Hopefully it's still intact and readable. All I can determine is that it exists.
You need to be careful. We know it's expecting you now. We also know that it knows we're bringing Arachne with us...
lines.note: Trails off a bit.

lines.text: Look, I'm not kidding around here. We know this is a trap. We know this is planned, and we know *it* knows *we* know. Right? I know!
lines.note: Tongue twisted at the end. A bit joking at the end.

lines.text: Do what you can to make my headaches stop, but also... I need to be free, I need to be extricated from this so I can leave all this behind me.
lines.note: She's not thrilled about this.

lines.text: We just need to go in about this with that knowledge as our shield. I need you to help me, because... I may be compromised here.
lines.note: She's pleading with you to help, in the most dignified way possible.

lines.text: You need to be careful. We know it's expecting you now. We also know that it knows we're bringing Arachne with us...
lines.note: Trails off a bit.

lines.text: Look, I'm not kidding around here. We know this is a trap. We know this is planned, and we know *it* knows *we* know. Right? I know!
lines.note: Tongue twisted at the end. A bit joking at the end.

lines.text: We just need to go in about this with that knowledge as our shield. I need you to help me, because... I may be compromised here.
lines.note: She's not thrilled about this.

lines.text: Do what you can to make my headaches stop, but also... I need to be free, I need to be extricated from this so I can leave all this behind me.
lines.note: She's pleading with you to help, in the most dignified way possible.

topics.prompt: I'll find the serum, just send me the location.

lines.text: You're my best friend, you know that, right? My only friend really. Aside from Grahm and Chally, I suppose...
lines.note: Grom and Cha-lee (like Charlie without the R)

lines.text: I love chatting with all my friends when I have the time, of course... but I'll say that your chats are less uh, meaty. I suppose. In a good way.
lines.note: Compared to a smart Super Mutant anyway. Joking because Grahm talks about meat a lot.

lines.text: Already sent. While you're out, I'm going to track down that Robobrain that Emerson mentioned...
lines.note: Thinking about it. She wonders if it is really a huge threat.

lines.text: Be careful. We know this thing is probably deranged.
If you want to listen to the holotape, go ahead. It's not like anyone can do anything about it, you know.
lines.note: What can they do... sue you?

lines.text: Everything I knew is turning upside down. Everything... except for you. You're the only person I can still trust.
lines.note: Grateful to the player for being there.

lines.text: This is it. After this... when you get back... we have to prepare to confront this thing. Please be careful. Please.
lines.note: Very concerned about the player.

lines.text: It feels like forever since we had a regular chat like two normal people in the irradiated remnants of the great wide world.
lines.note: Trying to be funny, kinda?

lines.text: Of course. We should chat more, you know? Makes this dreary world a little less so when you've got a friend to commiserate with.
lines.note: Friendly, she likes the player and wishes they'd talk more.

lines.text: I'm always happy with chat with you when we have the time.
lines.note: She's good friends with the player at this point, potentially romantic

lines.text: I know this holotape isn't going anywhere, so we do have some time to relax for a moment...
lines.note: Grateful to spend some time with the player after all this time.

lines.text: I knew you'd want to chat. You just had that look on your face.
lines.note: She knows the player well by this point. This is said with kindness.

lines.text: Sure. A normal conversation would suit me just fine right now.
lines.note: She knows the player well by this point, and everything else in life is rough, but... she wants to be less stressed.

topics.prompt: I need to finish something else, then I'll be back.

lines.text: Things are getting tense, and I understand that. I need you to hang in here with me though... okay? Finish things up first. I'll be here.
lines.note: Affectionately, understanding, sympathetic

lines.text: You're not getting cold feet here, are you? I hope not, my friend. We are so close... I can feel it.
lines.note: A little antagonistic but still overall friendly. Trying to push the boundary to see if the player is backing out.

lines.text: We can hold off on this a bit but... please come back when you can. I need to see this through, and I need your help.
lines.note: Guilt trip, but just a little.

lines.text: Sure, not a problem. I picked up some magazines from a trader who stopped by recently. I should be relaxing more...
lines.note: She's not sure if she can.

lines.text: No problem. I'll be around, waiting for your return like a lost puppy. I mean... an irradiated puppy? Oh, that doesn't sound very good actually...
lines.note: said jokingly, this is a goodbye.

lines.text: Roger that, my friend. Finish that thing up and then we can work on this together.
lines.note: Understanding, sympathetic.

lines.text: Aside from the mounting stress of everything else... you and I are solid. I love our friendship and I know I can trust you.
lines.note: Player has flirted and is great friends with Sofia. Sofia is signalling that once things are okay, she's ready for more.

lines.text: And don't think I haven't noticed your sly advances, my friend... I promise. Once we're done with figuring out... all of this... I want to hear more.
lines.note: She sort of gestures around when talking about "all of this" in order to mean the missions, etc.

lines.text: But I should ask first... what do you think about us?
lines.note: Warm question, she wants to know

topics.prompt: Sorry, Commander, I can't right now. Maybe later?

lines.text: Of course. I trust that you'll come back. I'm still working on getting this console to play holotape games anyway.
lines.note: She trusts the player will return later

lines.text: Roger that. I was planning on running some diagnostics on the scanner anyway, and maybe... just maybe... catching some shut-eye.
lines.note: Unsure if the player is being diligent or pushing her off

lines.text: Roger. I'll be around here, I was thinking of just... relaxing for a change. I'm not sure if I remember how, though...
lines.note: Kind of excited about the idea of just relaxing

lines.text: Copy that. I need a break as well. I'm in the middle of a very intense issue of Grognak, and... I am just enthralled.
lines.note: She's tired, she's been through a lot.

topics.prompt: What will you do with this serum?

lines.text: Honestly, I'm not sure. Part of me just wants to see it, to see what they used. To know it was real, I guess.
lines.note: Frustrated, conflicted. She isn't sure.

lines.text: Agreed. I followed Emerson's signal when he left, and he had quite a strange route. Acted like he was being followed. But I don't think he was...
lines.note: Conspiracy like. Whispering almost.

lines.text: He went to a few locations, maybe collecting supplies? I'm not sure. One of them had some high security holotapes.
lines.note: She's proud that she did this.

lines.text: I'll clean up the signal for you to track by the time you're back.
lines.note: Nerdily, she is proud of this

lines.text: I know my old department and... they didn't record a lot. Not unless they had to. But... when they had to, it was a big deal.
lines.note: It HAS to be important. They never documented anything.

lines.text: He... sounded sincere. And if he really was worried anything I saw or heard was being intercepted...
I mean, it kind of holds together? Or it could be a lie? I just don't know.
I heard of it before but... it was some other department, I thought. Dr. Nowak transferred to our department from theirs... I think.
lines.note: Frustrated, she feels like she should have known.

topics.prompt: What do you think Emerson is up to?

lines.text: Sounded like he had some demons in his past that he wanted to take care of. Probably has been putting it off for a while... that's my guess, anyway.
lines.note: She shrugs. Maybe she's giving him the benefit of the doubt.

lines.text: I bet they started on Robobrains because they could be more easily controlled. Right? I guess that didn't pan out.
lines.note: Shrug. She doesn't know.

lines.text: I hope they didn't feel a lot of pain, it seemed like they weren't putting them into the Deep Sleeper Pods. Maybe that's why they became aggressive?
lines.note: Sympathizing with them

lines.text: Right there with you. I've set up the scanner to monitor him separately and give me updates. Right now he's near a bunch of random robots....
lines.note: She agrees with the player, but is way ahead of them.

lines.text: I think he is also monitoring us, you see. So... we have to pretend like we don't care what he's doing.
lines.note: She's way ahead of the player here.

lines.text: Very little. Before all this all I ever overheard was the name. That's it.
But she's been... spying? on me for years. And I hope it's just that.
Everyone I knew was manipulating me. Using me.
lines.note: Angry, but holding it together

lines.text: I was their guinea pig... I need some time to process.
lines.note: Anger, but she's a thinker - processing

topics.prompt: Consider it done.

lines.text: It's probably decades old and unusable by now, but... it might tell us something. I'm not a chemist though, but maybe... I don't know.
lines.note: She isn't sure how valuable this will be

lines.text: I'll be right here, then.
Don't worry, you don't miss that much while you're out. Traders stop by from time to time... couple other random people, but it's pretty quiet.
lines.note: She misses adventure, a bit. Trying to make this task seem exciting by comparison.

lines.text: Yes. I suspect it's a holotape, but... it is in an unusual place. As if it was moved here to hide it, maybe.
lines.note: She knows she's being manipulated

lines.text: It's got to be connected to A.T.H.E.N.A. Both are from Greek mythology. Arachne was a weaver, and a brilliant one.
lines.note: She geeks out at you. Greeks out? I gotta use that.

lines.text: She challenged the Goddess Athena somehow and... well, she was turned into a spider. You know, like Arachnids. Right?
lines.note: Thinking about it, she wonders what this could mean

lines.text: Some versions of the story say she won, others say Athena won. I don't remember the details... and does it matter? I don't know, either.
lines.note: Just musing... get it?

lines.text: I know it's a stretch, but it's the only connection I can think of.
I just want this nightmare to be over. Thank you.
lines.note: Nervous energy

topics.prompt: Is this robot like the last one?

lines.text: Looks... similar, but might be a different type. The strange thing is, its mobility patterns are very similar:
lines.note: Recalling the data from a few hours of monitoring it

lines.text: It was heading towards us, and then it turned around and went to this location and stayed there.
lines.note: She thinks this is very weird.

lines.text: I think Emerson was right. It just seems like they have corrupt targeting data or something.
lines.note: Speculating. Unsure. But seems reasonable.

lines.text: Emerson's Emergence Kit helped a bit, but the headaches are very persistent. I could almost keep time with the spikes of pain.
lines.note: She's in some pain.

lines.text: I... believe you. I don't know why exactly but... I feel like I knew it was more than just relaxing ocean sounds.
lines.note: This confirms a dread she has felt before.

lines.text: I'm not sure. There's something strange about the whalesong holotape... since we used it with the Deep Sleeper Pods, I'm hoping there's a link.
lines.note: She's anxious about something, she feels like there's more to this tape.

lines.text: Maybe five or six times, I suppose. Every couple months for the two years prior to launch, anyway.
lines.note: Trying to remember.

lines.text: Yes... I'm not a doctor but it seems like they used the serum to reduce my brain's higher functions so something else could... I don't know what.
I signed up for space, not abuse.
lines.note: Angry, furrowed brows. She is livid about this. Emphasis on the NOT abuse part.

lines.text: That's a big question. I guess... I just want to know why so I can move on in this weird new world. Some closure, you know?
Then I can start to figure this place out... I can start fresh. Then maybe I can help you out for a change.
lines.note: She is grateful for all the player's help.

topics.prompt: Do you want to talk about your crew?

lines.text: Not right now... not really. I'd rather just keep busy for a bit.
lines.note: Reasoning it out. She just found out her crew is dead, and this is a way to keep busy.

lines.text: I mean... who would care now, right? Listen to it if you want. I can't guarantee it'll be interesting. I'm not sure what it is, exactly...
lines.note: She is saying "who would care" because nobody exists in the world anymore who would arrest the player for doing so.

lines.text: But... if you are a communist or a sympathizer then it might trigger some sort of explosion or brain wave obstruction thing... I can't remember.
lines.note: She seems serious here, but she is joking in the next line.

lines.text: They just used to tell us that to scare us, I think. I never tested it out, though...
lines.note: Laughing. Then sort of wondering if it was true.

lines.text: Dr. Bernard designed it to help us sleep for long periods of time in space. It clearly worked... maybe too well.
lines.note: Just giving information.

lines.text: I think that's a fine question for Emerson, honestly.
lines.note: She doesn't know, but she also wants to know.

lines.text: I can tell he feels guilty about something. I'm not sure if he's lying boldly or by omission though...
lines.note: She used to know him, but it's been a while.

lines.text: I think they're being intercepted. I think they get close and then something updates their algorithm and they leave...
lines.note: She is pretty sure of this from looking at the signals on the scanner.

lines.text: But who is doing that, or why? I don't have enough data to make a hypothesis.
lines.note: Shakes her head. She can't get that sort of data. That would be speculation. Nerdy.

topics.prompt: Consider it done.

lines.text: I'll monitor it from here and see if anything about its signal changes radically, I'm wondering if it shows signs of expecting this confrontation...
lines.note: She is worried if this could be a trap?

lines.text: It's got to be something significant. This could give me some closure here, finally... then I can move on like Emerson suggested.
lines.note: She's being optimistic.

lines.text: It just seems strange that this holotape is considered high security, and I want to know if that's real.
lines.note: She's worried it's sort of a waste of time, but it could potentially be something big too. She's on the fence about it.

lines.text: Since it was used exclusively with the Deep Sleeper Pods, I feel like that has to be the best lead for us right now.
lines.note: She's almost peaceful and hopeful about it.

lines.text: Something just seems unsettling about the whole thing. I'll start to investigate other signals, too.
lines.note: She's worried it's sort of a waste of time, but it could potentially be something big too. She's on the fence about it.

lines.text: I wish that Whalesong holotape wasn't... whatever it is. It would be soothing right about now to listen to that.
lines.note: She isn't even sure if she believes you, but she kind of does.

lines.text: Something just isn't right here, and I'm sort of terrified to see these medical records...
lines.note: Trailing off with worry

lines.text: I'm going to play that new Holotape game that you gave me for a bit, I think. Kill robots, save people. That kind of objective is just relaxing.
lines.note: She cheers up by the thought of playing a game.

lines.text: Something just isn't right here, and I'm sort of terrified to see these medical records...
lines.note: DUPLICATE OF VOICE FILENAME: 0057268A_1

lines.text: I need to relax for a bit. I got an issue of "Tesla Science" from a trader who stopped by recently, so I'll probably dive into that.
lines.note: She cheers up by the thought of doing something else.

lines.text: While I was looking for the Deep Sleeper Pod documents a while ago, I found another location that might have stuff like old U.S.S.A. contracts.
lines.note: She's annoyed by this situation

lines.text: Back in my college days, we used to watch robots fight in the basement of the science building. We used to joke about how scary that could be.
lines.note: Ironic right

lines.text: You know. If they ever came after us all. That kind of thing. Uh... yeah. Anyway... thanks.
lines.note: It's not so funny now, is it. She gets awkward towards the end.

lines.text: Locating a medical cache that has that serum wasn't actually as hard as I thought it might be... hopefully it will be a milk run to pick up, too.
lines.note: She pauses at the end. Does the player know what a milk run is? It's the apocalypse.

lines.text: I suddenly realized that the expression "milk run" might not have much of a meaning in this apocalyptic world, since everything is dangerous now. Huh.
lines.note: She's making a realization.

lines.text: It was rather easy to pinpoint it once I realized I had to recomputer the signals for things that had some organic parts...
lines.note: Nerd alert

lines.text: From the signature of the signal here, it seems to be a classified meeting between top officials regarding the Deep Sleep Project.
lines.note: Tempting the player with info

lines.text: Can you stop by and pick it up? I figure... it might give us some more leads or a name, or anything.
lines.note: Asking the player to pick it up.

lines.text: There's a signal coming from some sort of object... Something called Arachne. It's got to be related.
lines.note: Following a hunch, leaning on the player

lines.text: We need a U.S.S.A. Access card. I have the Sugar Grove personnel records. My hope is you can find an access card... here.
lines.note: Frustrated that she's a hinderance.

lines.text: Are you with me on this, my friend? Can I count on you?
lines.note: She asks the player if they will continue to help her.

lines.text: Part of me wonders if Emerson told us about this Robobrain so he would have more time to do... whatever he's up to.
lines.note: How did he know?

lines.text: A lot of these signals are high security signals, things related to the Deep Sleep Projects... other projects too, ones I don't know much about.
lines.note: Hinting at a future revelation.
