lines.text: But... One thing at a time... The key seems to be A.T.H.E.N.A.
lines.note: She's gathering herself, working through the emotion

lines.text: Wait. One of the signatures I've been tracking... Arachne... That can't be a coincidence.
lines.note: An "a-ha" moment, thinking furiously

lines.text: And once A.T.H.E.N.A.'s dealt with... Maybe I'll finally feel whole.
lines.note: Hopeful, worried

topics.prompt: How are we doing, Commander? Me and you.

lines.text: This is going to take a while to adjust to... *sighs*
You're very kind to let me stay here with you, and I appreciate that. I don't feel like I know you very well yet, but no yellow flags yet.
lines.note: Oblivious to anything more than this. In other words, "There's nothing between us.

lines.text: I wouldn't say we're ready to try out for the Unstoppables quite yet, but... I could see it happening someday.
lines.note: We're friends, but... not like, great friends. But it could go in that direction.

lines.text: I just... I had hoped things would be different. We weren't great friends, or anything, but... we worked together for years.
They were very kind, always there for me. Emerson as well. I was so lucky to be a part of that mission... or so I thought, anyway.
If you hadn't found me after the crash, I would have probably either ended up like the rest of the crew... or Emerson would have taken me in.
lines.note: Pondering alternate paths. We're good friends.

lines.text: I'm not sure how that would have gone, really... but I like to think I lucked out immensely here.
lines.note: We're good friends.

lines.text: You, of course.
*laughs* Sorry, I had to say it.
lines.note: But she means it though.

lines.text: But seriously though.
lines.note: She dead serious.

topics.prompt: [Flirt] I should make a joke about you falling from heaven, right?

lines.text: What? Oh. Hah! I guess you could...
But if you do, I'll have to make a joke about granting your other two wishes, I guess.

topics.prompt: What do you think about the new outfit?

lines.text: I absolutely love everything about this! Thank you so much, I... I feel like an actual super hero. I feel like I need a name...
lines.note: Extremely excited. The player has given her a costume.

lines.text: Commander Cosmos?! Oh, buddy... that could work. I feel like I need a space pet now, though.

topics.prompt: Do you have any questions for me, Sofia?

lines.text: Sure, I suppose. But it needs to be a trade. I get to ask you a question too, deal?
I trust you. Completely.
lines.note: What she really means is... "I love you.

lines.text: Oh... huh. I never would have noticed. That could have caused some annoying feedback. Nice spot, thanks!
*laughs* I'm not sure how to take that. But... you're right. I had a pet turtle. I wonder if she's still alive. I guess there's a chance, right?
That makes some sense. He knew about them... and he told me how to find them. The first one I encountered wasn't hostile towards me, either...
You know you can call me Sofia by now, right? I should hope so, anyway. I'd like to consider us close enough for that.
lines.note: We're friends, but... not like, great friends. But it could go in that direction.

topics.prompt: I survived through Perception or Intelligence.

lines.text: Now you're speaking my language here. Observe, theorize, weigh the risks... learn from failures, adapt... I get it. I absolutely get it.
lines.note: She's really excited about this answer.

lines.text: When I figure out what's happening with the U.S.S.A., I can modify my scanner to continue finding historically significant things, resources...
lines.note: She's excited ot know that the player is a nerd.

lines.text: Things that will expand our knowledge of this world. You know? I'm suddenly more optimistic about this strange new world of ours.
lines.note: Genuinely excited to be exploring the world with another nerd.

lines.text: I can respect that. Calculate the risks then pass on anything that isn't reasonable. Safe and sound. It just makes sense.
lines.note: She appreciates this mindset.

lines.text: Later on, I'll modify my scanner to pick up on caches of armor and other helpful resources, tools, first aid, etc... not without risk, but worth it.
lines.note: Offering a glimpse of what she can do int he future for the player.

lines.text: So, the best way to survive is to use your environment to your advantage. Makes perfect sense.
lines.note: Not judging the character, definitely impressed and trying to learn.

lines.text: I bet down the road I can figure out a way to find more useful things for you. Scrap, weapons, armor... I can contribute to our survival that way.
lines.note: Not judging the character, definitely impressed and trying to learn.

topics.prompt: I survived through Luck.

lines.text: Just pure chance? Statistically possible, but... maybe there's more to it than you realize. I'm fascinated, regardless.
lines.note: She wants to study the player.

lines.text: Maybe it has and you're just doing better than you thought.
lines.note: Trying to boost the player's confidence a bit.

lines.text: When things cool down a bit for us, I'm going to reprogram the scanner to pick up a variety of signals. We'll see what you're good at, friend.
lines.note: Cheering the player up a bit

topics.prompt: I survived through Charisma.

lines.text: You know... that makes sense. In a world with so much death, the best way to live is to cling to other life. I get it.
lines.note: She's impressed with the player's resourcefulness.

lines.text: I know that I would have been lost without you, so that makes sense... and it's a relief, too. Society will continue. The world will continue.
When we have some down time, I'm going to rework this console to find supplies, help people... I think we can do some good for the world. Together.
lines.note: She's hopeful for the future.

lines.text: Makes sense. You can't rebuild society without the people, and if everyone is just out for themselves then what's the point?
lines.note: Thinking about what the player said.

lines.text: When everything is said and done, I've got some ideas for rebuilding society... gathering resources, helping people. We can do it.
lines.note: She's thinking about the future here. Hopeful.

topics.prompt: I don't honestly know. I just survived.

lines.text: Random chance, huh? It is what it is, I suppose. Takes the pressure off, I guess. It's a relief, isn't it? Out of your control. Just live.
lines.note: She's not judging, but is a bit relieved.

topics.prompt: Exploring, scavenging, killing. I do what is required of me.

lines.text: I can respect that. Every day seems like a fight... but you're learning something new about yourself, right? I'm glad I can be a part of that.
lines.note: Confidence building for the player

lines.text: I hope when everything settles down, I can reprogram this scanner to be helpful for you. Find more things to help you survive. We'll see.
lines.note: Explaining what her purpose will be in the future.

lines.text: I just crashed from space, the world that I know is gone, I have horrible headaches and... well... now there's someone flirting with me. I dunno.
lines.note: Trying to be kind about it. She just crashed! Come on!

lines.text: You're nice and all, but... slow your rockets. Just... for a bit, okay?
lines.note: Asking nicely

topics.prompt: We're in love.

lines.text: Same thing we do every day, my love. Enjoy ourselves.
I think we can figure it out as we go. We'll make the best of it.
No -- we did it. Together. We're a team.
I don't believe in fate, it's just cheesy.
But... I think about how we ended up together, and it boggles the mind. I mean... I could have died in space, in my pod.
I could have died on impact in the crash, like my crew.
I could have been shredded by mutants, or drowned in that old bunker. I could have died from the headaches alone.
But instead of any of those potentially more likely scenarios, I was found by somebody. Somebody decent and kind.
Someone who cares.
Waking up with each other, and exploring this world together. Wasn't that the dream all along?
Oh, and maybe also playing more holotape games together, starting up a new Unstoppables fan group, and maybe... just maybe...
lines.note: Considering the options

lines.text: Rebuilding Appalachia, side by side. Or... that's my short list of goals anyway.
lines.note: Said lovingly

lines.text: Explore Appalachia, build a new life for ourselves... forget about everything else that came before this. Just focus on us for a change.
And, you know, maybe see if I can find every issue published by Hubris Comics, and maybe every holotape game ever... you know, on the side.
A million things could have happened to me after I went to space. I never expected falling in love to be one of them.
I love you too. Oh. Wait, you were going to say that, right? Well. Either way, it's offered unconditionally.
lines.note: Said sincerely.

lines.text: Well, not all of them, perhaps...
Sure, I teamed up with someone to save my own life, unravel the mysteries of an evil experiment, and free a trapped robotic personality...
But there's still one thing on my list that's unchecked right now.

topics.prompt: Let's talk about the Finale.

lines.text: Then... I don't know. I really don't. Emerson would know, but he won't help.
I wish I knew what all this A.T.H.E.N.A. unit was collecting from my senses this whole time, but... I need this to end.
This is just wrong and cruel. We have to end it.
Dr. Lee commented that Earth just seemed so fragile out there -- so alone.
I watched the clouds spinning over our sparkling home dangling in the vast emptiness of space.
I thought... We are hardy little things, aren't we?
Yes... it's done. It's over. I wish we could have helped the A.T.H.E.N.A. unit. She was clearly in... distress. I just need to rest for a while.
lines.note: Sad about athena

lines.text: I don't know, but... I think that was the right thing to do. She was in pain this whole time also. I had no idea.
lines.note: Seems like it anyway.

topics.prompt: Anything for you.

lines.text: You're the best. And not just because we're in an apocalyptic wilderness and my options are heavily limited. I actually mean it.
I don't know what I'd do without you. Seriously. I don't. My retirement plan is just ruined so this is pretty much it for me.
Where would I be without you? Well. I'll tell you. I'd be dead in a waterlogged bunker covered with giant roaches. That's where. And thank you.
You always are. That's what I like about you. I know you'll always be back for me.
I'll be waiting with baited breath. And by that I mean stale sugar pops breath -- a little sugar, a little nuked grain, and a dash of chalk. Mmm.
You better.
I know I can.
Well, I don't know if they're still alive but... there's a good chance. That's about all I've got in terms of details.
This sort of thing happens from time to time, but... it would be good if we could also stop it from time to time.
I've heard a bunch of wild rumors about this case... what's true? I think that's something you've got to find out for yourself.

topics.prompt: What's my target here?

lines.text: There used to be several Anglers here, but now there's just one. Probably the meanest one of the bunch.
lines.note: Scared, a bit

lines.text: Scanner picked up an Angler, but there could be other things. It seemed to be sending off some sort of warning call.
lines.note: Or maybe not

lines.text: Not sure why, but there's an Angler here. Scanner seems pretty sure of it.
Tried to scan this signature and it reflected back onto the scanner. Almost certainly an Assaultron. Those things... are not messing around.
Scanner picked up on a bunch of Assaultrons recently. Most got picked off, but one remains. And that's what you're looking for.
Looks like another Assaultron. Could be a U.S.S.A. model, but I'm not sure.
Every so often, a gnarly Bloatfly with a particularly mean streak hatches. If it isn't killed quickly, it breeds. That's what I heard.
lines.note: Warning, kill it

lines.text: Scanner found a single Bloatfly here that seems unusually mean. You gotta check it out.
I've been tracking this Bloatfly for a while. It is responsible for personally infecting a dozen pack Brahmin recently. You know what to do.
lines.note: Warning, kill it

lines.text: Scanner picked up a couple of indistinct signals. I think one is a Wolf... not sure what the others are.
A wolf was seen being chased into this place by a pack of rabid squirrels. Scanner can't really pick up on the squirrels... too small. Be careful.
lines.note: amused, jokingly

lines.text: I heard there was a pack of Wolves here recently, then some hunters picked them off until just one remained. But it was a mean one.
Scanner indicated that some folks lived here recently... but it's just a Yao Guai now.
Scanner indicates that it's an unusually aggressive Yao Guai... take care, good luck with it.
I installed a special scanner upgrade unit to pick up on different kinds of creatures. This one is a Yao Guai. Seems like a mean one, too.
lines.note: Pausing for you to guess.

lines.text: I know one of those crazed Appalachian cults is behind this. I just know it.
lines.note: He doesn't really know it.

lines.text: There's gotta be more to it, but everybody's staying silent. You can't trust anything.
When I asked for more info, someone started chanting on the radio. Made my ears bleed. I couldn't shake it out of my mind for hours.
Scanner picked up on a ton of Bloodbugs, but only one remains here now. Probably the meanest one of them all.
lines.note: Warning, kill it

lines.text: Scanner found some Bloodbugs laying some eggs recently. One has remained behind to guard them. I think... you should check it out.
lines.note: Warning, kill it

lines.text: Got a lead on a Bloodbug that took a bite out of everybody in a whole family, then they all died in a day. You have to get rid of it.
lines.note: Warning, kill it

lines.text: Heard some traders talk about this Blood Eagle guy recently... might be worth your time. Sounds like a terrible person, honestly.
I never thought I'd be scanning Appalachia looking for murderers and thieves, but here we are. Found a Blood Eagle for you. Check it out?
lines.note: Sad about it, but kill them

lines.text: Grahm told me that this Blood Eagle smacked Chally so hard that Chally fell into a ditch and got stuck. He was just moo-mooing for days.
lines.note: Yeah, kill 'em!

lines.text: Took Grahm forever to dig him out. So upsetting...
So... I think you know what to do with this Blood Eagle.
There's one big Cave Cricket at the center of this scan. Find it and eradicate it before it comes after those Settlers nearby.
lines.note: Tongue twister

lines.text: Heard there was a Cave Cricket that cannibalized a creche of eggs. That's right. A cannibalistic creche-killing Cave Cricket. Kill it.
lines.note: Tongue twister

lines.text: At the center of this place there's one big mean Cave Cricket. Normally I'd say... avoid it, but I think you shoudl eradicate it before it breeds.
I've been tracking this beast for a while. This Deathclaw is wildly aggressive and... remembers. Waits. It needs to be destroyed.
lines.note: Warning, kill this thing.

lines.text: Scanner picked up on a Deathclaw. Not just any Deathclaw, mind you, but a really old one. Not sure if that means it's meaner or weaker though.
lines.note: Warning, kill this thing.

lines.text: Deathclaw sighted. Apparently it attacked Chally the Moo-Moo when Grahm was distracted. Chally will be okay... but this can't stand!
lines.note: Angry, everybody loves Chally (said like Charlie but without the R)

lines.text: Picked up on some old U.S.S.A. tech that was recycled into an Eyebot. Can you check it out? Destroy it, maybe?
lines.note: Warning, kill this thing. May as well.

lines.text: Pretty sure this Eyebot is a decommissioned U.S.S.A. Bot. Or parts of it are. Destroy it, will you?
lines.note: Warning, kill this thing. May as well.

lines.text: I'm fairly sure this Eyebot is an old U.S.S.A. model. Should probably destroy it while I've got its location locked.
lines.note: Warning, kill this thing. May as well.

lines.text: It's a Fog Crawler. I don't have any other information about it, though.
lines.note: Warning, kill this thing.

lines.text: I swear, I thought this Fog Crawler was dead for days. But then its signal started moving. Freaked me out.
lines.note: Warning, kill this thing.

lines.text: This Fog Crawler grew from a newborn size to a full adult size in half the time a regular one does. Kill it before it breeds!
lines.note: Warning, concerned. this could be a hard kill.

lines.text: A kind trader stopped by recently and asked me to find this Feral Ghoul and put it down. I think... he knew who it was, once. Be kind.
lines.note: Warning, concerned. this could be a hard kill.

lines.text: Saw this Feral Ghoul on the scanner for days. It's getting closer, so... may as well kill it.
lines.note: Warning, concerned. this could be a hard kill.

lines.text: This Feral Ghoul was released by one of the local Cults. Released. Why would they do that? Find it, kill it before... it does their bidding.
lines.note: Warning, concerned. this could be a hard kill.

lines.text: Ever hear of a Floater? Well. You're about to run right into one. Good luck, friend. You'll need it.
lines.note: Warning the player about a new monster.

lines.text: Floaters. That's what they're called. Weird things. Fortunately for you, I think there's only one. But the scanner has been wrong before.
lines.note: Warning the player about a new monster.

lines.text: Heard it's a Floater. How do you even kill those things? They freak me out.
lines.note: Warning the player about a new monster.

lines.text: Scanner picked up on the Grafton Monster at this location. Good luck... you'll need it.
lines.note: Warning, concerned. this could be a hard kill.

lines.text: Heard from a trader that there's a Grafton Monster here.
lines.note: Warning, concerned. this could be a hard kill.

lines.text: Apparently there's a Grafton Monster there that was being toyed with by the Blood Eagles. Put it out of its misery, will you?
lines.note: Warning, concerned. this could be a hard kill.

lines.text: Scanner wasn't able to identify this one exactly, but I think it's either a Gulper or a Rad Toad.
lines.note: Warning, concerned. this could be a hard kill.

lines.text: Couple traders stopped by here the other day. Said there was a Gulper there. Scanner didn't pick up on anything, though.
lines.note: Warning, concerned. this could be a hard kill.

lines.text: Scanner picked up on a weird Gulper. Very aggressive. I wish we had the ability to do some experiments on these things... maybe one day.
lines.note: Warning, concerned. this could be a hard kill.

lines.text: Scanner is jammed. It's gotta be a Honey Beast. Due to the nature of the bees, it really messes up the signals.
lines.note: Warning, concerned. this could be a hard kill.

lines.text: I've been tracking a cloud of bees lately, seems like a Honey Beast. Beware. Get it? Bee ware. Hah.
lines.note: Warning, concerned. this could be a hard kill.

lines.text: Scanner seems to indicate that this Honey Beast is actually from somewhere else and is going to corrupt our local Honey Beasts. May as well kill it.
lines.note: Warning, concerned. this could be a hard kill.

lines.text: It's definitely an Insect... but beyond that? Not sure.
lines.note: Warning, concerned. this could be a hard kill.

lines.text: Well, it's an Insect. That's the best I can do.
lines.note: Warning, concerned. this could be a hard kill.

lines.text: Scanner was able to determine that it's an Insect for sure. Looks like other Insects are approaching too. Probably good to squash it now.
lines.note: Warning, concerned. this could be a hard kill.

lines.text: It's a Liberator, but it has some U.S.S.A. signal attached to it. Scrap metal, maybe? Please destroy it, this is worrisome.
lines.note: Warning, concerned. This has been so annoying.

lines.text: This Liberator has been trying to access a bunch of U.S.S.A. data lately. Can you... destroy it?
lines.note: Warning, concerned. This has been so annoying.

lines.text: Apparently this Liberator has been raiding U.S.S.A. supply caches. Frankly, it has me worried. Destroy it, please?
lines.note: Warning, concerned. This has been so annoying.

lines.text: I sort of like Mega Sloths... but this one is really aggressive. Possibly diseased? Hard to tell. It needs to be put down.
lines.note: Friendly warning

lines.text: Hunter stopped by the other day and said he was being followed by a Megasloth. Anyway... the Megasloth is about a week behind him now.
Can you just.. find it and deal with it for him? It's making me laugh.
Turns out Megasloths are easy to track. Makes sense, right? According to the scanner, there's one here.
A trader stopped by recently and told me that he trapped a giant Mirelurk at this location... so that jives with the scanner data, too.
There's a Mirelurk there. Might be a King or Queen... not sure exactly. The scanner isn't really able to pin it down.
Heard there's a Mirelurk at this location from a Settler who was heading to Foundation.
Scanner indicated that there was a Mole Miner at this location recently but it's... hard to tell if it's still there. You know how they are.
lines.note: Warning, he's seen this before

lines.text: Mole Miner causing some trouble for the traders who are passing by that location. Be a good samaritan and take care of it, will you?
Not sure why, but I'm getting a U.S.S.A. signature off this Mole Miner. I wonder if it's carrying a piece of tagged scrap metal from my ship...
Some Settler stopped by here the other day and said there is a new Mothman Cult leader in this area. We need to stop that before it gets bad.
Scans were picking up on a gathering at this location. Given the shape of the signals, I think it's a Mothman Cultist. Take down the Leader, okay?
Scanner has noticed activity here that mimics some activity at another site. I think it's a Mothman Cultist outpost. Maybe a new chapter.
Signal coming from this location is very strange. Gotta be some interference. I'd guess it's a Mr. Gutsy type robot... aggressive, too.
There's a U.S.S.A. signal coming from a Mr. Gutsy at this location. I don't know what it means exactly, but destroy it. Please.
There's a Mr. Gutsy at this place. It's deliberately pinging the scanner. I think it knows I'm monitoring it.
lines.note: Warning, amused

lines.text: Not even sure what you'll find here. The scanner wasn't even that... precise. Some sort of mutated creature. That's the best I can do.
Scanner is sure it's a living thing. Seems mutated. Beyond that? I don't know.
This place is well known for its Mutation problem. Usually one shows up and does... whatever... and others follow suit.
There's an old U.S.S.A. Protectron model here. Destroy it, will you? We don't need it converting more.
Heard someone in Crater was tinkering around with a Protectron, flipped some switches, and the thing went haywire. Somehow ended up at this spot.
This is a reprogrammed U.S.S.A. Protectron. Could be carrying dangerous materials. Can you destroy it?
Heard a trader stopped here to eat her lunch and watched as a Rad Ant came out of no where. She barely returned to Foundation alive.
Scanner picked up a Rad Ant here, but not just any kind of Rad Ant. It's carrying ten times the amount of eggs as usual. Kill it, please?
A trader was bringing her herd of Brahmin head this way recently, but they got destroyed by a single, angry Rad Ant. Can you deal with it?
I've been tracking a really nasty Radscorpion lately. This one thing has killed a dozen Raiders and Settlers alike. Can you try to take it down?
Grahm told me that he saw a Radscorpion head over to this place a bit ago. I bet it's still there.
lines.note: Warning indirectly from Grahm

lines.text: Scanner confirmed: it's a Radscorpion. And it's aggressive and mean. So a regular Radscorpion...
I've never met anyone who was okay with Radroaches. Just your luck... there's a giant mean one at this location. Waiting for you.
lines.note: Grossed out

lines.text: It's a Radroach. The trader tried to claim there's just one there, but I certainly don't believe it.
lines.note: Grossed out

lines.text: There's a Radroach there. Please squash it and then do not tell me the gorey details. Thank you very much.
Scanner shows there's a Radrat nest here. Who knows how many Radrats could be here now though.
Apparently a trader carrying some cheese barely escaped with his life as he went by this place. Was almost shredded by a massive Radrat.
There used to be a herd of Radrats in this area, but only one is still on the scanner. I sort of think it ate the others. I don't know though.
Scanner is showing some Raider is at this location causing all sorts of chaos. Should probably clean that place up. You know?
lines.note: Amused, they're both Raiders

lines.text: So, this Raider stopped by here and threatened me. Then ran off into the distance. Been tracking the fool since... and finally got a good location.
lines.note: Emphasis on ex

lines.text: Scanner picked up on something pretty awful here. Some people got hurt. I think a Raider has remained behind... can you check it out?
lines.note: The speaker is a Raider so they have venom for this person

lines.text: This Robobrain reprogrammed my high scores on Red Menace. Deliberately. They're gone! Do you know how long that took?!
Please destroy it. It just makes me so angry... just... why would it do that? Why!?
This particular Robobrain destroyed my copies of a few holotape games that I just bought from a trader. So please. Destroy the Robobrain!
I'm not sure, but this Robobrain seems like an old U.S.S.A. model. Destroy it before it does something stupid. Please.
It's an old U.S.S.A. Robot, all right. I need you to destroy it. Okay?
Scanner picked up some unidentified U.S.S.A. Robots. Probably reprogrammed but... still. Destroy them, just in case?
It's a U.S.S.A. Robot, and I think it's trying to reprogram other Robots. Can you deal with it? Quickly?
Someone watched Scorchbeasts fighting there. One survived and is now nesting, we think.
I've been tracking this Scorchbeast on the scanner for a while. Is that something you can handle?
Scorchbeast. Giant, mean one. Is that something you can kill? I know they're tough.
I intercepted a signal from one Robobrain to a Sentry Bot. It was using U.S.S.A. encryption. Robobrain is missing. Sentry Bot is right here.
This Sentry Bot is definitely an active U.S.S.A. bot who is somehow scrubbing its signature from the scanner. I need you to destroy it. Fast.
Been tracking this Sentry Bot on the scanner. For some reason, it has gone to several U.S.S.A. caches. Can you just destroy it? Just in case.
Some Settler just snapped and... well... yeah. You gotta just take care of it.
lines.note: Warning the player about a new monster.

lines.text: Heard some Settler just... snapped. Hurt a bunch of people. Not worth going into details about it, honestly. Just take care of it.
lines.note: Warning the player about a new monster.

lines.text: I've been telling people forever that Settlers are just as messed up as anyone else. Looks like we got someone who's proving me right. Take 'em out.
lines.note: Warning the player about a new monster.

lines.text: Scanner picked up on something... really weird here. Seems like a Sheep? A big one. Part sheep, part... I don't even know what.
Heard a trader actually say that there's a Sheepsquatch there. I can't believe it. I just can't. But... can you check it out anyway?
I upgraded the scanner a while ago. I swear, it claims there's a Sheepsquatch here. I hope it's not broken.
lines.note: Warning, humorous

lines.text: Not sure why, but there were a bunch of Snallygasters here and then in a few minutes... there ws just one. Maybe it ate the others?
Scanner is indicating that it's a Snallygaster. I don't know where these things even come from.
It's a Snallygaster, I guess. Scanner was really hazy about it.
lines.note: Warning, laughing, he hates settlers

lines.text: It's one giant Stingwing. Gross, right? Scanner even said it's gross. Okay, it didn't... but... it should.
A trader saw Stingwing poo around this place, so could be one there.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: Where there's one Stingwing, there's many. Or just one. Honestly it isn't really a strong indicator of population. But anyway. There's one here.
Grahm confirmed that there's a Super Mutant here, and not a friendly one. In fact, it's one that has been causing problems for Grahm.
In my book, that means we gotta get rid of it. You know what I mean?
There were a ton of Super Mutants here only recently. Now there's one. Seems like it chased off the others. So it's... very aggressive.
Apparently there's one angry Super Mutant at this place, shouting at anybody who passed. It's starting to get violent. Can you deal with it?
I literally have no idea what this thing is. I'm sorry. Scanner can only tell that it isn't a Robot.
Hunters weren't sure what was here, scanner can't pick it up either. I'm sorry. It's not a robot but... that's all I can tell.
Scanner isn't able to get details on this thing. Sort of makes me nervous. I know it's not a robot but... it's aggressive though. That's all I know.
Scanner result is positive. It's a Tick. Sorry.
Trader stopped by just to tell me that there's a Tick at this place, and he had no interest in passing by our way again until it's dead. So.
lines.note: Grossed out

lines.text: There's a Tick here according to the scanner. Probably more than one, but... hard to tell.
Rad Toad. The signal on the scanner was absolutely clear.
I watched this Rad Toad hop from one end of West Virginia to the other, then back to this spot exactly. Twice. I think something odd is up with it.
Grahm told me there's a RadToad here, said he saw it from the road. Then he got sorta confused and called it a RoadTad.
lines.note: Awww cute

lines.text: Scanner indicates that one big, mean dog has shredded everything at this location and is still there.
lines.note: Just fyi

lines.text: Giant mean dog sighted at this location. A hunter warned me about it recently. We should just deal with it, right?
lines.note: Dog story

lines.text: Feels like such a bummer to hunt down dogs, but this one is particularly mean. We should put it down out of mercy.
lines.note: He doesn't get it

topics.prompt: I've come to think of you as more than a friend.

lines.text: R-Really? I was afraid you just thought of me as "that needy person" or "the one with all the headaches.
I sometimes feel like I've barely been myself through our time together.
It made me doubt what I was feeling, but now that you've said that... it must be real, right?
Oh, more? I hadn't... I mean, you've never... I... I don't know quite what to say.
With everything my head has been through, I hadn't even considered that you'd even think I was... dating material.
I come with my own set of matched luggage if you know what I mean.
Those are the words I wanted to hear.
I admit, I had the smallest fear that you'd think I wasn't ready.
ATHENA, sleeping pods... It's a lot to take in, and I've barely scratched the surface in this new world.

topics.prompt: I'd like to keep our relationship strictly professional.

lines.text: Of course. I... understand. *ahem* Professional it is!
The scanner is still picking up plenty of signals, and you're assistance is always invaluable.
Let's get back to it!
Of course. I... must have misunderstood, I mean, I understand. *ahem* Professional it is!
The scanner is still picking up plenty of signals, and you're assistance is always invaluable.
Let's get back to it!

topics.prompt: You're right. You need more time.

lines.text: Oh? *sigh* You're... right. And I know. I haven't even taken the time to redefine who I am in this world.
One minute I'm listening to soothing whale songs, thinking I'm doing my part, making my parents proud.
Next, I'm a recently freed experimental lab rat in a post apocalyptic world.
I guess it's time to let the soul searching begin, but still, I have you to thank for that.

topics.prompt: I love you, Sofia.

lines.text: Is it too sappy to say you've got my head spinning, but in a good way?
And I love you, if it wasn't obvious already.
Oh, not to mention share their priceless video games with you. And yes, I'm prepared to kick your butt any day.
lines.note: Second sentence is a playful, taunting challenge.

lines.text: Sure friends let you crash on their couch, but true friends take out killer robots and rescue sympathetic AIs.
Sure friends let you crash on their couch, but true friends take out killer robots and migraine causing AIs.

topics.prompt: Think of it more as a business arrangement.

lines.text: I deserve that. I mean, I have been a bit of a task manager. You've done quite a bit for me, and all I have to give is my gratitude.
lines.note: Slight disappointment and apologetic.

topics.prompt: I think you make a great room mate.

lines.text: Just like those good old college days, huh? Except, I guess I'm the one that never does the dishes...
lines.note: Joking. Her "dishes" joke is referencing how the player does all the work.

topics.prompt: I'd like you to think of this as your home, too.

lines.text: It feels good to hear you say that. It's been hard to have clarity since I... woke up.
I've spent so much time here, I never really stopped to think that this is your home, not mine.
Between the headaches and total collapse of modern civilization as I knew it, sometimes I'm not sure where certain feelings are coming from.
lines.note: She should say "total collapse of modern civilization" as if she's quoting it.

lines.text: Thanks to you, I'm finally beyond that.
And, given how life is even more unpredictable than ever these days... I just wanted you to know how much you've come to mean to me.

topics.prompt: Friends don't get any better than you and me.

lines.text: I won't argue with that.
I've been through so much, and I finally have a fresh start. I'm just happy that you're going to be a part of that.
But, in all honesty, you've given me my life back and asked for nothing in return.
lines.note: Being honest and sincere.

lines.text: Obviously, I've had misguided friendships in the past, but to me, you're the real deal.

topics.prompt: A lot of people would've helped you out.

lines.text: I mean, yes, you don't have the monopoly on being a decent human being.
But, being decent and being a one Vault Dweller army... Can you see my point? Miracle.

topics.prompt: Shutting down A.T.H.E.N.A. was the only sure way to heal you.

lines.text: You're right. I mean, she was just a program?
But she seemed so... sad. Is it wrong to feel sorry for basically code?

topics.prompt: After everything the USSA did, I didn't trust A.T.H.E.N.A. one bit.

lines.text: That makes a lot of sense. You know, making sure that all their lies and plans are over...
I buy it. See, you're still helping me out.

topics.prompt: So you feel good? No more headaches?

lines.text: I feel better than good. I feel like I could fly. Just feeling... normal, feels amazing.
Maybe a little guilt to go with that, though.
A.T.H.E.N.A... she was just as much of a tool as I was. A victim.
I can't help wonder, if what we did is right.

topics.prompt: I'm glad it all worked out.

lines.text: I have to say something, and I know it may sound corny. But hear me out.

topics.prompt: I still think we should've put a bullet in Emerson.

lines.text: *chuckle* Well, I wouldn't cry many tears if that had happened...
But it sounds like he's already paid for his crimes. The apocalypse hasn't been kind to him. Or anyone, really.
Him going through a bit of hell, though, I'm all right with that.

topics.prompt: So you feel good? No more headaches?

lines.text: It's more of nagging now? And when it fades I feel normal. Blissfully normal.

topics.prompt: Are you worried about A.T.H.E.N.A.?

lines.text: Logically and objectively, I think I should be. The scientist in me can't discount the possibility.
But... No, I'm really not. I feel a... connection, and not the creepy kind.
And, I think it may turn out to be a really good thing what we did.
But she was just as much of a victim as I. And now, I feel like I can really breathe again.
I fell to Earth, and literally anybody could've met me. Most people would've shived me for my suit alone.
So the greatest miracle of all of this... was finding you.
lines.note: This isn't romantic, it is appreciation - although I don't mind if the read could lead to something more (a romance can springboard off this)

topics.prompt: What are your plans now?

lines.text: Now that everything's over, where does that really leave us?
lines.note: Slightly nervous. Uncertain of the future, but being hopeful.

topics.prompt: What's done is done. Time to move on.

lines.text: I have to say something, and I know it may sound corny. But hear me out.

topics.prompt: Stop, I'm blushing.

Hello? Someone there?

lines.text: That said... anything else you wanted to talk about?
We'll just call that last time a test run. And now we're ready for the real deal.
I'm glad you changed your mind. I think we can give it a real shot this time.
It'll be good to get back to... "us." We make a pretty good team, you know.

topics.prompt: It was a stupid mistake. Forgive me?

lines.text: Forgiven completely. And, I have to say I agree. Stupid mistake, indeed.
lines.note: Joking with the player.

topics.prompt: Everything happened so fast, but now I'm ready.

lines.text: I understand. I often thought about that myself. The timing of it all.
I had my own fears that we may have rushed into things initially, so I understood when you ended things.

topics.prompt: I miss you. I didn't realize what we had.

lines.text: It's so good to hear you say that. I admit, I was pretty crushed to lose you, but oddly, I think the space apart did us both some good.
It made me realize that I'm not relying on you, and I've really had the chance to regain my identity again.

topics.prompt: Never mind. Can we talk about something else?

lines.text: Sure, what's on your mind?

topics.prompt: I made a mistake. Let's get back together.

lines.text: Wha-What? I mean, that's the last thing I expected you to say... Why the change of heart?
lines.note: Being cautious.

lines.text: I admit, I've been hoping you'd say something like that... but what changed?
lines.note: Being cautious.

lines.text: Are you sure this time? Not that I don't want to, it's just... what changed your mind?
lines.note: Being cautious.

topics.prompt: [Resume Romance] Sofia, I was wrong. Take me back, please?

lines.text: You're... serious, aren't you? That's just... so unexpected. Are you toying with me? Why would you do that?
*sighs* I know how this world can scramble our brains sometimes. Believe me. I'm here for you, I always will be.
lines.note: Glad she can be here for the player, will take them back, but is a bit hurt by all of this.

lines.text: Ok. Let's try again. But, well, I... need a moment to compose myself after this.
lines.note: Deep breath

lines.text: You know, I'll always appreciate everything you've done for me. And thanks to you, I know there's still hope in this world.
I know that sounds cheesy or something... but what I'm trying to say is, even if we're not together, you still mean a lot to me.
I have every intention of sticking around as a friend... if you'll let me.
lines.note: Slight sadness as the end.

lines.text: Now, let's get on with our lives before I take this sappiness to the next level.
lines.note: Clearing the throat or something at first. Recomposing herself. Then ending on a cheerful note.

lines.text: There's always that little voice that wants to doubt everything. It kept saying this was all too good to be true.
Of course I kept telling it to shut up, but sometimes... sometimes I should really learn to listen.
lines.note: Getting sad.

lines.text: If it means anything, you'll always have a special place in my heart... and after all you've done for me, I wouldn't have it any other way.
I was just thinking about how lucky I've been lately.
I survived a crash landing, I found you, who helped me find out the truth about Emerson, the U.S.S.A., and Athena...
Sooo lucky... that I knew that luck had to run out at some point.
But it was worth it. No regrets. And I hope you'll still consider us friends.

topics.prompt: Never mind. Let's talk about something else.

lines.text: Oh, ok.
lines.note: Friendly and upbeat.

topics.prompt: How do you feel about our relationship?

lines.text: Aside from the fact that the world is full of mutants creatures and we're constantly under threat... I'm glad that I have your love.
lines.note: Romance is on!

lines.text: I love you. You know that, right?
lines.note: Romance is on!

lines.text: I'll be ready to answer that in much more detail tonight, if you like...

lines.text: I love it. I hope you know that. The fact that you're asking kind of scares me, though.
Is there something I should be concerned about?
All thrusters are go, my love.
lines.note: Romance is on!

topics.prompt: I really enjoy being with you.

lines.text: You know I feel the same. I love what we have together, and wouldn't change a thing.
The U.S.S.A., Athena, the crushing headaches... I'd do it all again as long as I knew it led to you.
But... it worries me that you're asking... Was there something that you wanted to talk about?
lines.note: Slight fear the player may be breaking up with her.

topics.prompt: I think we should break up.

lines.text: Oh... Well, all good things come to an end, right? It was nice... while it lasted.

lines.text: *sigh* I had a feeling you were going to say something like that.
Somehow... I knew this was coming.
Call it, waiting for the other shoe to drop.
Expand your scanner to look for signatures at a constant speed. That should pick them up. They aren't that complicated.
lines.note: Genuine helpful tip, but also... holding something back.

lines.text: Maybe. I've heard a couple scavengers say that parts of the ship have already been scrapped... same goes for any other ship debris.
lines.note: He knows more than what he's saying.

lines.text: Best to just... move on. It's honestly shocking that you survived as it is. I'm serious.
lines.note: He really is shocked. Kind of annoyed, too.

lines.text: So you're staying at this uh... place? I guess you really decided to jump into modern Appalachian life, huh?
lines.note: Commenting on the player's camp which could be a mansion or a tiny junkpile.

lines.text: I don't even know what to say... I never expected to see you here.
lines.note: Shocked, really. It's just weird, too. What a huge coincidence.

lines.text: My ship crashed a while ago, and I was fortunate to find someone who took me in... been trying to find my crew, but I've had some horrible headaches.
lines.note: She's talking about the player helping her.

lines.text: Welcome... back to Earth, I guess. Welcome to Appalachia.
lines.note: He's almost sorry for her, in a way. But he's mostly surprised she's alive.

lines.text: ...Emerson? Dr. Emerson Hale? Is that... is that you?!
lines.note: She knows it's him, but she can't believe it. He's old now. What happened?

lines.text: Well, you look exactly the same. I never believed... *clucks tongue* I wondered who picked up my beacon... well, I'll be damned.
lines.note: He never believed he'd see her ALIVE because he tried to kill her in her sleep. He has regrets. She doesn't know any of this so he'll spin it.

lines.text: Who... who are you? You seem... so familiar.
lines.note: Strange man approaches her. Who is he? He seems familiar but she can't place him.

lines.text: I am too. So much has changed... I mean. You know better than most. Care to catch me up to speed?

lines.text: That's good. I'm glad you're making friends already, I suppose...
lines.note: Chuckling a bit. So much has changed in the world and she's making friends.

lines.text: My new friend here might be able to talk them out of attacking us. Ha! Well, worth a try, right?

lines.text: I'm sure we can deal with them. My friend here is a regular lucky rabbit's foot, really. I'm sure we'll figure it out.

lines.text: I think we can deal with that. My friend here is pretty clever, so I'm sure we can figure out a way to deal with them. Maybe permanently.

topics.prompt: It took me a while to get here, but I'm here now.

lines.note: Covering his ass.

topics.prompt: [Lie] I crashed from space! Wee!

lines.text: Oh hey, we've got ourselves a comedian here. They always said the roaches would survive, but I didn't know that included clowns.

topics.prompt: Some people arrived fairly recently.

lines.text: A lot of us have arrived lately, that's true. I came in with some regular folk, traders, that sort of thing. Safety in numbers, my friends.

topics.prompt: I'm from Vault 76. This is my home.

lines.text: Fascinating. Well, I worked here a long time ago but I only recently arrived again. Followed some folks out here.
lines.note: Basically true.

lines.text: Wanted to see if anything survived from the U.S.S.A. for old time's sake.
lines.note: Hiding a little bit more. Not overtly suspicious.

lines.text: Why did you come to Appalachia though?
lines.note: Genuinely curious. Not judgmental.

topics.prompt: It doesn't matter. That world is gone now.

lines.text: That's fair. A lot of people died. This is a new world with new problems.
lines.note: He agrees with the player.

lines.text: Anyway, look... I need to go. I'll be back another time and we can chat some more. Okay?
lines.note: He's cutting it short, he wants to eject.

lines.text: Hmm. Okay. I get that there were nukes... but... what happened? Was it... you know... a huge drawn-out war?
lines.note: She is concerned for the suffering of others.

lines.text: What about the rest of America? Or... the world? Did Communists do it?
lines.note: She cares genuinely about this.

lines.text: How did you all survive out here though? It must have been even worse than it is now.
lines.note: She is very sympathetic to their plight

topics.prompt: Bombs fell on Oct 23rd, 2077. It was fast and terrible.

lines.text: Succinct.
lines.note: He likes that.

lines.text: Mostly everything, anyway. Most cities... it's hard to know the extent of anything, really. Everything was just... gone.
Who did it? Ah, who knows now. The news was gone too, you know. Probably everybody had their fingers in that pie.
lines.note: Hedging his bets. He doesn't know, or doesn't want her to think he knows.

topics.prompt: Does it matter? A ton of people died.

lines.text: Cities were devastated. My family... was at home in D.C. We just bought that place. I was on the phone the day before arguing with the movers...
lines.note: Distant memories of a different time.

lines.text: I was in a secure place, but I knew they were gone. I figured... everyone was.
lines.note: This is true.

topics.prompt: Some people survived in Vaults.

lines.text: I know others survived in preservation shelters, underground buildings... caves even. But I'd guess most people just died.
lines.note: He knows more than he's letting on.

lines.text: Me, personally? I was inspecting a newly-built compound for a Monday report. Heh. I used to write... reports. How... strange?
lines.note: Thinking back to the time... amused that he did anything so mundane.

topics.prompt: Emerson can explain how other people survived.

lines.text: There are so many different answers to this. Some people hid in bunkers and scavenged, others moved around all the time... I don't know.
I stayed in the compound for a while with my coworkers, then we parted ways.
lines.note: They could be alive or dead. He doesn't care.

topics.prompt: The bombs killed many. Some of us survived in Vaults.

lines.text: That's right. You probably remember Vault-Tec building those things... I can hear my parents saying "I told you so" all these years later.
lines.note: Sort of annoyed.

lines.text: The Great War happened that October 23rd, 2077... and well, everyone outside of a Vault had to figure out other plans.
lines.note: It was a rough day for everyone, but he was safe.

topics.prompt: You're probably better answering this one, Emerson.

lines.text: It was a Saturday. October 23rd, 2077. It lasted... almost no time at all, but it felt like an eternity.
lines.note: This is true.

lines.text: I always figured the cities got bombed first, but it's hard to know. It was so fast, and so long ago...
lines.note: Remembering so long ago.

lines.text: Who did it? I dunno, kid. It's been forever and it's not like the news ever came back on television, you know.
They could have survived though, right?
lines.note: She's hopeful that this is true, but already not believing it.

lines.text: I see. Well, is there anything I can help with while I'm here? Supplies, medicines...? Questions, I guess?
lines.note: Speaking to the player and the astronaut. Skeptical of the player's motivations, but also doesn't care a lot. It's said for show.

topics.prompt: Why did her ship crash?

lines.text: My best guess? Probably ran out of fuel, and the auto-pilot guided it to the nearest U.S.S.A. facility. Oh, what does it matter? She lived! What a miracle!
lines.note: He's lying about why it crashed. He tries to change the subject.

topics.prompt: You know anything about that hostile U.S.S.A. robot?

lines.text: There's a bunch of them out there. Seems that their algorithms got scrambled or something. Who can say.
lines.note: He is hiding something, he doesn't walk to talk about this, and he thinks the player should mind their own business.

lines.text: They used to come after me, but it seems like they have a higher priority target now.
lines.note: Smirking. He knows more than he's saying. He has lead the robots to her camp, after all.

topics.prompt: Can you help with the Commander's headaches?

lines.text: We had some Emergence Kits back in the day. They were specifically designed to help people emerge from deep sleep specifically. I bet I can find some of those.
lines.note: Not Emergency -- "Emergence" like you are emerging from deep sleep.

lines.text: He has helped me out quite a lot already, actually. Brought back a U.S.S.A. Beacon and also took care of some hostile robot.
lines.note: Said a bit defensively because the player has done right by her. She's talking about the player. (There is a female version of this line.)

lines.text: She has helped me out quite a lot already, actually. Brought back a U.S.S.A. Beacon and also took care of some hostile robot.

lines.text: I hope your good samaritan here has helped you out with more than just a place to... uh... crash.

topics.prompt: Was that your beacon?

lines.text: Sure is. For a while I had hoped that I could contact somebody else to monitor the Deep Sleep mission until... we could figure something out.
lines.note: He's hiding something here. He was partially to blame for the crash.

topics.prompt: Very convenient that you're here in Appalachia.

lines.text: I suspect her escape ship's auto-pilot sent the ship on a trajectory to any known U.S.S.A. location using its... admittedly very old data.

topics.prompt: Can you help find the Commander's crew?

lines.text: They weren't in the escape capsule, I take it?
lines.note: He's hiding stuff. He knows they weren't.

lines.text: Well, that is unfortunate.
lines.note: Trying to cover up something, but not that obvious about it. He is relieved that they didn't survive though.

topics.prompt: You can leave anytime, pal.

lines.text: Honestly, I didn't even mean that as an insult. I find the creativity of the locals to be... impressive. I just live in an old military base, myself.
lines.note: A little condescending, but trying to make peace.

topics.prompt: Hey, come on. It's not much, but it's my home.

lines.text: No offense intended, friend. I live in an old military base, so I'm not one to talk about anybody's creativity here.
lines.note: He's sort of a jerk, but mostly just not a people person.

topics.prompt: I'm open to decorating suggestions, friend.

lines.text: I didn't mean to be offensive. Your home is, uh, fine. I'm not creative in that way... I mean, I squat in an old military base right now, personally.

lines.text: I simply cannot believe she's returned.
To have survived all she has... remarkable.
It's been... such a long time.
Is... is this a friend of yours?
lines.note: You just met someone who seems really familiar.

lines.text: We need to shut her down now. I figured the headaches were something else but... nothing like this. I never agreed to this in my contracts!
lines.note: She's determined to end this.

lines.text: This has to end. I never agreed to any of this in my contracts!
lines.note: Angered. Her head is killing her, she feels violated by the robot borrowing her eyes and ears.

lines.text: Well... *sighs* ...actually you did. The contracts were... very thorough. And extremely obtuse. You could have never known.
lines.note: He hates correcting her on this.

lines.text: I'll show you where you need to go. I'll shut down some of the internal power lines so A.T.H.E.N.A. can't detonate anything inside the facility...
lines.note: He's suddenly worried about revenge.

lines.text: In some sort of... I don't know. Revenge. It's a primitive robotic system. It drove the Robobrains insane, you know.
lines.note: Trying to be helpful, reminding them of the dangers.

lines.text: I know about A.T.H.E.N.A., Emerson. I know what you've done to me.
lines.note: Telling him is almost cathartic. She didn't need his help.

lines.text: You should know that her link to you isn't severed. I look into your eyes, Sofia, and she's there. Watching all of us.

lines.text: *sighs*

lines.text: I'll make this right. I promise.
lines.note: Telling her what he'll do.

lines.text: And... thank you, Sofia. I don't deserve it, but thank you.

lines.text: Hmm. Up to her then, I suppose.
I... I await your judgment.

topics.prompt: Emerson, you're pathetic. You better help us.

lines.text: I know... and I'm sorry. I know it doesn't sound real but... I have wandered around for decades thinking of what I did. Imagining them up there.
lines.note: He's serious.

topics.prompt: Thanks for your help, Emerson.

lines.text: I wish I could change the past. I'm... I'm sorry. We'll end this, okay? If it's the last thing I do. We'll end this.
lines.note: Genuinely sorry.

topics.prompt: You didn't tell us earlier because A.T.H.E.N.A. would hear?

lines.text: Yes... I couldn't tell Sofia, obviously, and I didn't know if I could trust you or if you would believe anything I said.
lines.note: He still isn't sure.

lines.text: I figured... if she started to suffer, I would do anything I could to help. Until then... I searched for Dr. Nowak's lab. Thought the kill switch would be there.
lines.note: annoyed that he failed.

topics.prompt: Can A.T.H.E.N.A. control Sofia at all?

lines.text: No... the neural pathways aren't compatible. It's a very simple robotic intelligence, designed to passively observe and collect.
lines.note: Informational only.

topics.prompt: What was A.T.H.E.N.A.'s purpose? We might need to know.

lines.text: It was a government contract. Supposed to keep the peace. Ensure societal tranquility. I don't know really, I just... authorized everything.
lines.note: He feels shame for phoning it all in.

lines.text: Who was I to stand up to all of them? I... should have though. I know that now.

topics.prompt: If we destroy A.T.H.E.N.A. will it hurt Sofia?

lines.text: Yes, it might hurt... a lot. Maybe permanent damage. But keeping that thing connected will kill Sofia.
lines.note: He thinks this is true anyway.

topics.prompt: Why did you come back to Appalachia, really?

lines.text: For a long time, I thought the old U.S.S.A. backup facilities here were gone. Heard a lot of rumors about it. Figured everyone was dead.
lines.note: He simply thought it was all over already.

lines.text: Then I heard people were coming back here. Decided... I should be sure it was over. Tagged along with some nobodies... made it here with one goal:
lines.note: Starting nervous but ending in a place of determination

lines.text: To blow up A.T.H.E.N.A.
lines.note: He says with vigor.

lines.text: But then... Sofia lived. And it was complicated, because I knew A.T.H.E.N.A. was holding her hostage, and I had to find another way.
lines.note: He feels tremendous guilt about all of this.

topics.prompt: Why did you force the scientists into pods too?

lines.text: *sighs* It was cheaper this way.
lines.note: Heavy sigh.

lines.text: After we achieved orbit, we were told that our program was getting cut entirely due to lack of results.
lines.note: Recalling the tale from 30 years ago.

lines.text: The scientists on the ship had exposed the program to the oversight board, and... we had deals with Arktos, RobCo, others... we were ruined.
lines.note: Spilling the beans.

lines.text: I was ruined.
lines.note: Heavy sigh. Guilt.

lines.text: Putting them in the pods gave us until 2080, when another crew was scheduled to take their place. We thought it was enough time.
lines.note: They were wrong.

lines.text: I resigned and paid a fine for some ethics violations. I was hired by RobCo afterwards for triple my salary... and that was that.
lines.note: Relieved to finally tell someone his shame.

topics.prompt: Did you cause the Deep Sleep's ship to crash?

lines.text: Exactly how could I do that? No. I didn't. The ship was supposed to switch to the secondary power cells a while ago.
lines.note: Sort of surprised that the player thought to ask this.

lines.text: When Dr. Lee was... unavailable... the ship's Pandora Bot initiated Blue Sunset, which landed the ship near the strongest active U.S.S.A. Beacon.
lines.note: He says "landed" with a bit of hesitency because it actually crashed. Also, he forced Dr. Lee into a pod, so he feels guilty about that.

topics.prompt: I have nothing more to say to you. We have Arachne. We're shutting Athena down.

lines.text: I had hoped that Dr. Nowak created some sort of shutdown routine for A.T.H.E.N.A., but almost everything was destroyed in the wreck.
lines.note: He's skeptical the program is real.

topics.prompt: [Intelligence 8+] The constant headaches weren't from the crash.

lines.text: No, they weren't. It's from the continued strain on your mind, Sofia. You could handle it when you were in Deep Sleep, but... not now.
lines.note: He's genuinely sorry. He's telling her that this won't get better.

lines.text: If we were ever friends, if any of that life before ever mattered, just... fix this.
lines.note: She's deeply disappointed with him. Suffering and sad. She wants to give him one last try.

topics.prompt: Before you go any further, take Arachne.

lines.text: Let me see...
So we can destroy A.T.H.E.N.A. With this.

topics.prompt: I have Arachne. You need to read it.

lines.text: Let me see...
So we can destroy A.T.H.E.N.A. With this.
Don't you understand? She's watching you, watching us, right now.
Your ship crashed here... Because A.T.H.E.N.A. is here. She's in a restricted section of Sugar Grove.
You need to find a way in. I lost my U.S.S.A. Keycard long ago. But surely you can find another?
That's all I can do. Sorry.
This... this is serious, isn't it?
lines.note: You feel like you're about to get yelled at.

lines.text: Sofia seemed to indicate she had something important to discuss. Speak to her.
lines.note: You feel like you're about to get yelled at.

lines.text: Whatever it is, I'm--I'm sure we can figure it out.
lines.note: You feel like you're about to get yelled at.

lines.text: Did... did it get hot all of a sudden? Must be the wind...
lines.note: You feel like you're about to get yelled at.

lines.text: A.T.H.E.N.A. A name I'd hoped to never hear again.
Quiet now. It could be listening.
lines.note: Looking over your shoulder. You think someone could be listening in on your conversation.

lines.text: Dealing with that system... you'll want to take extra caution.
lines.note: You feel like you're about to get yelled at.

lines.text: You're both here. Good.
lines.note: Serious. Down to business.

lines.text: Okay, that's enough for now. Emerson, could you please leave? Maybe... try to remember something helpful for next time.
lines.note: Pissed off at him. He better be useful next time.

lines.text: You just have to find the contract itself, I guess.
lines.note: He's annoyed, it's been so long and he wasn't to blame for all of this... just a little (in his mind)

lines.text: It wasn't decades ago to me.
lines.note: She mad. It was only days or weeks ago in her mind.

lines.text: What were they doing? Emerson. Tell me.
lines.note: She is looking over her medical records and becoming angry.

lines.text: Arktos Pharma and the U.S.S.A. made a deal to use some serum in the Deep Sleep project. They made it, but it didn't work, okay?
lines.note: He is hiding something, but he doesn't want to let on. This is a half truth. They did make the serum for the project, but it sort of worked.

lines.text: It was a bio-medical thing with Arktos. I don't know the details anymore. It was literally decades ago. You get that, right?
lines.note: Trying to remind her that it's been a long time, hoping it will make her sympathetic.

lines.text: *sighs* I knew... some of it. I was just a manager... I didn't really read the technical mumbo-jumbo.
lines.note: Long sigh. He knows he's backed into a corner now. He might be a bit relieved though.

lines.text: Emerson. What did you know about Dr. Bernard's Deep Sleeper Pods?
lines.note: She says this with a stern, almost hostile warning. An accusation is waiting... she already knows that he knew.

lines.text: Tell me you're not still chasing ghosts?
lines.note: Trying to be optimistic. He truly hopes she's not continuing down this path.

topics.prompt: [Charisma 8+] Emerson, you need to make things right. You owe Sofia that much, at least.

lines.text: You're... right. Okay. Listen...
lines.note: Worried, upset, does want to make things right but didn't actually want to do it.

topics.prompt: What did Arktos have to do with this?

lines.text: They're a pharmaceutical company, and they made the serum that we used in the experiment. Who cares? This is ancient news.
lines.note: Shrugs, he doesn't think it's a big deal.

topics.prompt: Bring her something for these headaches next time.

lines.text: Right. Fine. I will. I should. I meant to, I just... got distracted...

topics.prompt: [Strength 8+] Time to spill your guts, old man. One way or another.

lines.text: Okay, okay! Geez Louise.
lines.note: Gives up, is scared and annoyed.

topics.prompt: If it doesn't matter, just tell her.

lines.text: Look, my memory isn't reliable anymore. I've been nuked more times than I can remember. Literally.
lines.note: Nervous, irritated, he doesn't want to be here anymore.

topics.prompt: You heard her. Leave.

lines.text: I'll be back with something for those headaches later... I promise. I'm sorry about all this, I really am.

topics.prompt: [Charisma 8+] This is all recent to her, Emerson. You have to care.

lines.text: I do... I... I actually really do care. I didn't want her to stay up there so long... *sighs*
lines.note: Sighs as he's leaving.

lines.text: Arktos Pharma and the U.S.S.A. made a deal to create a serum... Serum K, maybe? It was going to help with the Deep Sleep Project.
lines.note: He is hiding something, but is relieved to let go of it a bit. This is a half truth. They did make the serum for the project, but it sort of worked.

lines.text: That's all I know. I wish... I could do more.
lines.note: Half truth - not completely obvious. Sincere about wishing he could help more.

lines.text: I hope you're both being cautious as you do your... exploring.
lines.note: You're concerned the player is snooping into business that'd be better left buried.

lines.text: You and Sofia seem to share a certain... boldness. That's for sure.
lines.note: You're concerned the player is snooping into business that'd be better left buried.

lines.text: I'm not sure I care for the direction your recent actions are taking.
lines.note: You're concerned the player is snooping into business that'd be better left buried.

lines.text: What exactly is it you two want here, I wonder.
lines.note: You're concerned the player is snooping into business that'd be better left buried.

lines.text: Sometimes I wonder if the past wouldn't be better left where it was...
lines.note: You're concerned the player is snooping into business that'd be better left buried.

lines.text: You're back. Just in time for the three of us to discuss what we found.
lines.note: A little stern. You're about to grill this person.

lines.text: There you are. Emerson and I were just about to discuss what we turned up.
lines.note: A bit sarcastic. You found out some troubling evidence about Emerson.

lines.text: There you are. Look what the cat dragged in.
lines.note: A little stern. You're about to grill this person.

lines.text: You're back. Emerson and I were just having a little talk. So... have you got something for me?
lines.note: A little amped up. You're excited to see the player, but you're in the middle of an argument with Emerson.

lines.text: You're back. Emerson and I were just having a little talk. How'd it go?
lines.note: A little amped up. You're excited to see the player, but you're in the middle of an argument with Emerson.

topics.prompt: Here's your medical records, Sofia.

lines.text: Transfer them to my console, please.
lines.note: She can check them out there.

lines.text: Transfer them to my console, please.
lines.note: She can check them out there. Same line as VOICE FILENAME 00000972_1

lines.text: Transfer the medical records to my console, please. I need to see.
lines.note: She's upset, but she already believes it.

lines.text: Thanks, friend. I can handle this myself.
lines.note: She's angry at Emerson.

lines.text: Tell me you're not still chasing ghosts?
lines.note: Trying to be optimistic. He truly hopes she's not continuing down this path.

lines.text: Emerson. What did you know about Dr. Bernard's Deep Sleeper Pods?
lines.note: She says this with a stern, almost hostile warning. An accusation is waiting... she already knows that he knew.

lines.text: *sighs* I knew... some of it. I was just a manager... I didn't really read the technical mumbo-jumbo.
lines.note: Long sigh. He knows he's backed into a corner now. He might be a bit relieved though.

lines.text: Entered home space. Success.
Running: adventure routines!
Have a day.
Input overload. Processing... processing. Formality selected: Hello.
I have more than zero items for trade. Appealing, correct?
Identifying: Human. Incrementing human count. Done.
I have already collected this data. Adding new data to additional storage structures. Redundant. Accepted.
Detecting inaudible lines of communication. Affirmative. Returning transmissions.
Inside private spaces, collecting items is not permitted.
Restarting human-facing speech routines...
These homespaces that you all have built are insecure, unstable, and potentially hazardous. However, they are... unique.
This object has not been catalogued. Scanning. Storing. Interesting... but why so small?
I seek the turtle for Sofia, do not worry. I can identify it by the scutes.
I spend caps on power sources. It is my vice. By vice I mean, I need it to continue. Surely that is a vice.
Fact: Not all robots respond positively to other robots.
I noted a small creature with enlarged ears on the way here. It did not respond to my query. I am certain that it heard me.
Fact: Rain does not damage this model of Assaultron. All U.S.S.A. robotics should be suitable for intense space or weather phenomena.
Tree permutations are varied, countless. Endless in number. In complexity, there is infinite. In infinite, there is thought.
Comment... overload existing function parameters to accommodate new situation. Commit.
Bird detected. Duplicated bird. Bird count will not be incremented.
The world is endless. But my capacity to carry goods is not.
Home saccharine home.
If customers, then trade. Else, leave.
Attention, humans. I have returned with objects of arbitrary value.
Grahm should come here sometime. I will tell him.
Assessing unfamiliar organic behavior.
Appropriate response generated.
Hey! How's it going? This weather sure is happening.
I'm tracking down some more of them with my contacts so I'll be back later. Stay out of trouble, please.
lines.note: He's hiding something, but also telling the truth. He means stay PUT and stop meddling.

lines.text: Thanks for the Emergence Kit, Emerson. Come back later, okay?
lines.note: Trying to emphasize the bond that they have.

lines.text: The robot's signature was a partial match for some other signals in the area, so I thought we might investigate those. It seems linked.
lines.note: This is a good idea and she knows it.

lines.text: Seems like a waste of time to me. You have your answers. Nowak, Lee, Bernard... they're all dead. Long dead.
lines.note: He actively doesn't want her to do this.

lines.text: You're not.
lines.note: Reminding her of something she knows, trying to be a slap in the face to wake up.

lines.text: Move on. Live your life. Build onto this... Appalachian uh... home... with your good samaritan friend here. Lie low.
lines.note: Warnings. Suggestions.

lines.text: There was almost nothing in the wreckage. They had no chance.
lines.note: Feels guilty.

lines.text: I just... why weren't they in the main emergency capsule with me? They would have been safe in there...
lines.note: Survivor's guilt.

lines.text: Maybe that's true. It's all in the past though.
Focus on things you can actually change. For example, those robots. Have you found any more?
lines.note: Trying to change the subject again.

lines.text: Glad to help... so. Last time we spoke, you both were tracking down the crew's signal. What did you find?
lines.note: Genuinely curious.

lines.text: You don't know how relieved I am to hear that. The headaches have been excruciating at times... I could barely think.
lines.note: The player did not give her a med kit earlier.

lines.text: Figured I would stop by and give you this Emergence Kit. It should help with your headaches for a little while.
lines.note: He's genuinely trying to help, but he is also hiding something in this conversation.

topics.prompt: Good advice. We'll talk about it.

lines.text: Okay... you should do that. Appalachia is dangerous, and these wild goose chases don't do anyone any good.
lines.note: Genuinely concerned.

topics.prompt: Do you know where U.S.S.A. holotapes could be stored?

lines.text: Not really... but back trace the program's signal that you picked up. Sofia can figure it out from there.
lines.note: Not sure if he should help.

topics.prompt: You should go.

lines.text: I was going to anyway. I'll be back though, because... Sofia is my friend. My very old friend.
lines.note: Emphasizing that she's not from this time or place.

topics.prompt: Why do you care?

lines.text: Just professional curiosity, really. These robots have come after me as well.
lines.note: Doesn't like the player. Is annoyed that he's being questioned.

topics.prompt: We found a Commander Gutsy and got an override program from it.

lines.text: Ah. See? I told you. Probably a rogue programmer. Some sort of hippy that wanted to cause chaos, I bet.

topics.prompt: I destroyed a robot. A Commander Gutsy.

lines.text: Interesting. That's a rather old U.S.S.A. model, not many were ever made.
lines.note: Wondering why it was on the hunt.

topics.prompt: There were no survivors.

lines.text: It was a long shot anyway. It's good that you checked, at least. But we already had one miracle when Sofia survived. More would be... pushing it.
lines.note: He had no doubt.

topics.prompt: Hard to say. There wasn't much left in the debris.

lines.text: I figured as much. Just found parts of their suit, I'm guessing? That's basically a body.
lines.note: He didn't think it was even worth investigating.

topics.prompt: None of your business.

lines.text: I knew them too, you know. I worked with them closely for years.
lines.note: Annoyed at the player.

lines.text: Hmm. I'm curious to know how you've fared in your explorations.
You seem to be making due under the circumstances.
I do hope you don't mind the visit.
Look who's back. And bearing gifts.
I just can't shake these nightmares. Floating in space forever... Just, why?
Surely this can't be what has become of humanity.
It only feels like a moment ago when I was on the Space Station, and now... this is my life.
Nothing in the Emergency Protocols Handbook covers this scenario.
Do you ever feel like you're being.... monitored?
I didn't go to Astronaut Camp for years to scavenge for scrap!
They blew it all up. Nobody thought those fools would actually do it... damn them.
I swear I heard strange voices as I was almost asleep last night. I just couldn't wake up!
I never had headaches like this before.
Why not? Dream big or don't dream at all... um. I gotta get back to... literally anything else now.
Chally isn't Moo-Moo for long! Soon Chally is MOON-MOON!
Er... well. I doubt that we could find a helmet ---
Oh! Greenies. Like Chally. SEE? Chally is ready for SPACE! Chally is going to the MOON!
What do Space people eat? You eat meat? Space meat?! MOON MEAT?
Moon... meat? No. I eat grains, plants, mushrooms... I don't eat meat. Wait... do you think the moon is made of meat?
Uh... I haven't been able to get in touch with the USSA ---
Can you take Chally to Space? Chally want to fly someday. Grahm okay with the ground. But Chally have dreams.
The Space Station, yes, but... before it crashed. All that is in the past though --
No doubt I'll probably start... stinking... soon though. Being in space kept me safe from a lot of things for a while.
SPACE?! You're from... the MOON?! Or... the SUN?! Or... the little TWINKLES?!
Oh, uh, well. Okay. Thanks? It's probably because I haven't been irradiated and soaked with all the despair yet.
You seem fresh. Not stinky. How so not stinky?
Hey. Hey you. You different than the other squishies.
Ugh, my head. I think I have a concussion. Where am I? Why do you look like that?
