lines.text: Of course, let's do that.

topics.prompt: Super Mutants. The big green guys.

lines.text: Very sad, but this is what happens to the youth of today when they drop out of college.
They can't string together a coherent sentence, and their lack of basic hygiene has made them sickly and green.
Oh, and their pets! One of their dogs almost bit me! Did I get an apology? No! Not until after I got through scolding him! Hmph.
lines.note: More annoyed than angry. Emphasis on "after

lines.text: Last time I go to Huntersville!
lines.note: More annoyed than angry.

topics.prompt: Mothman Cultists. The fanatics praying to a bug.

lines.text: You mean the University's Entomology students? Yes they're rather odd, but I guess that's just what their hazing is like these days.
lines.note: Pronounced "En-tuh-ma-luh-jee

lines.text: Oh that brings me back. Back when I was in school, if you wanted to pledge to a house you'd have to streak buck-naked through...
lines.note: Reminiscing about her younger days before realizing the topic isn't appropriate.

lines.text: Actually I'll tell you that story when you're older.

topics.prompt: Raiders. Those rough people wearing weird scraps of junk as outfits.

lines.text: Terribly rude. They were pushy and insisted that I stay the night but required I wear a gaudy necklace.
I managed to slip away but I would never recommend their accommodations to anyone.
lines.note: Like she's giving a review on a bad hotel.

topics.prompt: Responders. Those people helping out inside the Whitespring.

lines.text: I'm all for supporting a good cause, but did they have to make such a mess?
The Whitespring used to be a refined location. Now there's a man trading resources for stamps of all things!
Oh and their chef. Lovely stew, but it seems they could really use an assistant to prepare the ingredients.

topics.prompt: Scorched. The red people with green crystals.

lines.text: Oh dear, I've met them. More young minds rotten to the core. They can hardly speak and they are constantly jittery. Tsk tsk tsk.
lines.note: Concerned about the youth

lines.text: This is why winners don't use chems. And you're a winner to grandma, okay? Don't forget that.
lines.note: Like she's giving her child an anti-drug talk

topics.prompt: Settlers. The people with a place at Spruce Knob.

lines.text: Oh they're just darling, insisting I stay when I came to buy some groceries.
While it was tempting, I don't think I could stay somewhere that leaves cooking to a robot.
I wanted to try a sandwich, but instead it gave me some ravioli!

topics.prompt: Brotherhood of Steel. Those people walking around taking tech and wearing power armor.

lines.text: Ah yes, I remember them. They're the new local police force, yes?
I recall they had this sweet young thing with them... Odyssey... Odessa... something like that.
lines.note: Struggling to remember the name after the ellipses.

lines.text: She was a dear. Her rude friend was keen to leave, but she remained and was talking my ear off, asking about appliances of all things.

topics.prompt: Enclave. The secret agency that ran America right into the ground.

lines.text: Oh sweetie, I think you're confused.
The word you're looking for is "Government", and while they may run things, it's our votes that make all the difference.

topics.prompt: Let's talk about something else.

lines.text: Of course sweetie.
Have you learned how to apologize?

topics.prompt: Yes, I'm very sorry.

lines.text: I'm glad to hear it. Now then, where were we?

topics.prompt: Nope!

lines.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Oh look, "Sorry". See how easy it is?
Ah, I'm sure you'll find some manners eventually.
That's a shame. Well, I'll be here should you learn how to be a decent human being.

topics.prompt: I can cook my own food.

lines.text: Oh I've seen the sorry state of food you youngins are whipping up.
You'll get none of those college-styled instant meals from me, no siree.
Only the finest in grandmotherly cooking! Chock full of tender love and care.
lines.note: Proud of herself

topics.prompt: Sounds like that's just what I need.

lines.text: It's what everyone needs dearie.

topics.prompt: So you're useless for anything except cooking.

lines.text: Well I never! How dare you undercut the importance of a loving home-cooked meal!
lines.note: Annoyed and insulted.

lines.text: If you're going to be rude, you get to be rude all by yourself!
Let me know when you want to apologize.
lines.note: Says this as the final word in the conversation.

lines.text: But enough of that. Let grandma know when you're feeling peckish and I'll whip you up something special.

topics.prompt: That was delicious!

lines.text: Ah, yokatta!
lines.note: Pronounced "Yo-kat-ta

topics.prompt: Thanks for the grub granny!

lines.text: Of course sweetie. A full stomach leads to a full heart!

topics.prompt: [BURP!]

lines.text: Oh my! Hahaha. I'm... glad you liked it.

topics.prompt: I meant more in relation to the post-apocalyptic hellscape.

lines.text: That's also rude! I know Appalachia isn't for everyone, but no need to phrase it like that.

topics.prompt: Not that. How have you not been shot at by the more violent locals?

lines.text: Oh that's simple sweetie, I keep my nose out of other people's business.
If I stay uninvolved, I find most people pay me no mind.

topics.prompt: I mean the Great War.

lines.text: Honey, war is never great.
lines.note: Serious and a bit sad

lines.text: It's dark, depressing and isolating. At least I would assume so. I've been very fortunate in that regard.

topics.prompt: Ancient if I'm being quite honest.

lines.text: Well I never! Seems like someone is being cranky.
You have a nap and come back when you're ready to not be a brat.

drops.name: Recipe: Mirelurk Cake With Bloodleaf Aioli

items.description: Knock knock. Who's there? It's Joey Bello, wise cracking wise guy!
items.howToObtain: Claim from the Shoot for the Stars Scoreboard (Season 13)

lines: Claim from the Shoot for the Stars Scoreboard (Season 13)

topics.prompt: Who are you?

lines.text: Just a down-on-his-luck entertainer looking for a couch to crash on.
Appalachia, yah! Pleasure to be here. One of my favorite... States? Counties. What is this place? Ah, forget it. How you doing? You look great.
lines.note: Stage performance energy. Isn't sure what "Appalachia" is but doesn't let it throw off his groove

topics.prompt: Thanks. I'm doing fine. Welcome?

lines.text: Real nice C.A.M.P. you got here. Real classy. Just missing one little thing... Live Entertainment!
lines.note: Sales pitch. He's the "live entertainment

lines.text: But you are in luck, my friend! I'm here to spark a little life. A little laughter. Maybe even a little love, huh? Hahaha, ah forget about it.
lines.note: Tongue in cheek nod to "Live, laugh, love" with "love" being a little flirty before he laughs it all off as a joke.

topics.prompt: Back up, stranger. This is private property.

lines.text: Stranger? Woah, I barely knew 'er! Boom! Ah ha ha!
lines.note: He knows it's a groaner but he's committed.

lines.text: I kid, I kid, I kid! I'm harmless. No need for guns. I'm not packing.
lines.note: Said in good humor, but just in case the player is wanting to hurt him now after the previous bad joke

lines.text: The name's Joey. Joey Bello! Ya know, like a roar of laughter, only spelt different.
I saw the stage and thought you might have an opening?
Damn, I could really use another hit from that pipe. If I could just remember where it was...
What I wouldn't give for a tato pie.
No matter what happens, the show must go on.
lines.note: Self pep-talk

lines.text: Nah, no way Teddy's still following me.
lines.note: Quietly, to self.

lines.text: What do you think, Joey? Time for a little day trip?
lines.note: Said to self. Special emphasis on "day trip". Insinuating he's going to go take some Daytripper drugs.

lines.text: Go to Appalachia they said. "You'll have a blast" they said. Didn't realize they were literally still dropping nukes on themselves.
lines.note: To self.

lines.text: I don't mind when they throw tatos. It's the grenades I worry about.
What do stylish kangaroos wear? Jumpsuits. Ha... What the hell is a kangaroo?
lines.note: Trying out a new joke he's read but doesn't know what a kangaroo is so doesn't get the joke

lines.text: There once was a man from Nantucket, he... no wait how'd it go again? Nah, fuck it.
lines.note: Trying to remember the limerick. Coincidentally ends up rhyming.

lines.text: (Sigh) Mondays. Is it Monday? Feels like a Monday.
Hello, sunshine.
I heard there's some kind of dance party over at Point Pleasant. Might pop some Day Tripper, check it out later. I just hope it doesn't get weird.
By the way, how many moths does it take to screw in a lightbulb? Just two, but I don't know how they get 'em inside there. Haha!
Break a leg out there. Just not mine!
Geez! Hope you left the other guy lookin' worse.
Woo! Look at the pipes on you. Been working out?
Those tatos you got there? You better not be planning to chuck those at me later.
lines.note: Mock suspicion - it's a joke

lines.text: Geez, I heard you was bright but didn't realize they meant radioactive.
That a pipe gun in your pocket or you just happy to see me? Hey-oh!
We havin' fun yet?
Thinkin' hard, or hardly thinking?
Nice costume! Where's the party?
Got the party started without me, huh? Don't worry. I'll catch up.
Your mother know you're out dressed like that?
Damn. Eat something already. You're making me hungry!
lines.note: Emphasis on "me

lines.text: Good God! You okay? When they say break a leg they don't mean that literally you know?
I hear Grahm's hosting another cook-out. Meat for weeks. Make sure you don't skip it 'cause that would be a missed steak. I mean, come on!
lines.note: emphasis on "missed steak" (mistake)

lines.text: Did I take too many chems again or have you noticed a lot of, well...aliens lately? Wonder why they're invading Earth. Maybe the moon was full! HA!
Anyway, I hope the aliens aren't planning to blow up the Earth. 'Cause they're WAY too late!
Wow, somebody had a good time huh? A little hair of the dog will fix that right up.
Oh, I'm walkin' here!
lines.note: The classic NYC line

lines.text: If danger calls tell 'em I'm on the can.
Lookin' good!
Ring-a-ding-ding!
lines.note: Frank Sinatra shout-out. A line Joey picked up from lounge singers in Atlantic City

lines.text: Ouch! Who gave you the shiner?
You look like you could eat a fat sandwich. You find one you let me know!
Hey hey!
lines.note: As if starting a stage performance

lines.text: Hey chief!
Yeah, whatya want?
Heya boss!
What's the scuttlebutt?
What's good?
There's my favorite Appalachian!
How you doin'?
lines.note: the classic NJ line

lines.text: You lookin' for a put-down or a pick-me-up? Oh!
What's cookin', good-lookin'?
What's shakin', bacon?
How you doing?
lines.note: Not like Joey from Friends.

lines.text: Who loves ya, baby?

topics.prompt: What's the name of your act?

lines.text: Joey Bello Live! And I aim to keep it that way!
lines.note: Aims to stay alive (people who want him dead are after him)

topics.prompt: So... you tell jokes?

lines.text: Yeah, jokes! You know... Knock-knock. Why did the chicken cross the road? Youse got jokes here in Appalachia, right?
lines.note: Amused/joking around but he's new here and isn't sure what the "comedy scene" is like in Appalachia

lines.text: People pay caps to hear me crack wise and I help 'em forget about their miserable lives for a few minutes. Not rocket surgery, but it's a livin'!

topics.prompt: Okay, you can stay. But no funny business.

lines.text: Eyyy, look at you, huh? Guess I'm not the only comedian in this C.A.M.P.!
lines.note: Amused at the player's "no funny business" comment when his whole thing is being a comedian

topics.prompt: Welcome aboard Joey!

lines.text: You got it boss! Let me stash my stuff and I'll get right to work.
I tell jokes. I'm a traveling funny-man here all the way from exotic New Jersey. At your service.
lines.note: Says "Jersey" with a faux accent ("Joisey"). This and the next few lines are all part of a sales pitch to convince the player to let him stay

lines.text: Let me stick around and I'll lighten the mood. Maybe show you a few tricks of the trade. Thicken your skin. Teach you some "Comedian Resilience".
Yeah, who knows? Anything's possible with Joey Bello in your corner!

topics.prompt: You're looking for a job? What can you do?

lines.text: What can't I do? That's what you should be asking. But you want to know what I do do? You are filthy. I love it!
lines.note: What I do do is said like "doo-doo" and he's jokingly implying the player is asking about poop

topics.prompt: Are you some kind of comedian?

lines.text: What, like a clown? You think I'm here to make you laugh?
lines.note: Pretending to be offended

lines.text: Well honk my nose and slip me into some oversized shoes cause you nailed it, buddy!
lines.note: Happy performance mode

lines.text: Sticks and stones, my friend. Sticks and stones.
Oh! Forget about it!
Go get 'em Tiger!
C'mon, I'm just breakin' your balls.
lines.note: I'm just joking around

lines.text: Sure thing, boss.
You got it!
Anything else?
Heard Teddy the Toe Taker was after me but I doubt he'd track me this far.
What's on your mind?
Bada-bing, bada-boom!
Looking back, we really should have known Communism was going to be a problem for us given all the red flags.
What's the difference between a showman and a mobster? When a mobster says "break a leg" they usually mean someone else's. Oh!
I was never a big fan of mutations but after walking through that radiation zone I've gotta admit - they're growing on me!
Growing up I never did learn what the word "apocalypse" meant. Oh well, it's not like it's the end of the world.
I've taken so many chems I think they're affecting my memory. Not only that, I think they're affecting my memory!
They say if you want to make it in showbiz you gotta be funny! Aw but hey, looks aren't everything.
Someone close to me died recently. It really makes you think. If the bullet had been another foot to the right... that would've been me!
Last night I had to shoot a feral ghoul in my pajamas. How it got into my pajamas I'll never know.
I had this idea for a jokes-by-mail service right, but it didn't work out. The jokes were hilarious, but the delivery was terrible.
I borrowed this pair of shoes from my chem dealer. I don't know what they were laced with but I've been trippin' all day.
You ever get so hungry you try eating an alarm clock? It's better than starving but it sure is time consuming.
You ever explore any of the old skyscrapers around here? I don't trust the elevators. In fact, I take steps to avoid them.
I played this prank on this settler when I covered his door knob with adhesive. A week later and the guy's still furious. He just can't let it go!
You hear about the wedding they held at the old radio tower? The ceremony was only so-so but the reception was amazing!
You know I love ya!
You hear about that junkie that got addicted to soap? He's clean now. Woah!
Don't stop me if you've heard this one before.
Makes a lot of sense we use caps for our money, doesn't it? America has always been a cap-italist country. Cha-ching!
What's the worst thing a prison guard can find at a party? An open bar.
You hear the one about the drum set that fell off the roof? Badum-tss! Heh.
Hello, fellow Appalachian.
Say "hi" to my supply.

topics.prompt: Let's talk about your services.

lines.text: At your service, boss. What can Joey Bello do for you?

topics.prompt: What's your story, Joey?

lines.text: My life's an open book! Mostly a cautionary tale.
I didn't see nothin'! Who's asking, huh? Oh, whoops. Old habits die hard I guess. Just like me!
lines.note: A bit jokey - pretending the player is asking him to snitch on someone (which he's actually used to with dealing with the mafia)

topics.prompt: Have you met anyone interesting in Appalachia?

lines.text: I've made the rounds.
You digging up dirt on somebody?
Besides you? Yeah, I've met a new face or three.

topics.prompt: Got a joke for me?

lines.text: Oh, check it out.
Alright. Alright.

topics.prompt: Catch you later, Joey.

lines.text: Not if I see you first, Eh! Ha-ha!
Hate to see you got but I love to watch you walk away. Huh?
Catch you later, boss.
Break a leg!
Keep on keepin' on!

topics.prompt: Have you got anything good to trade?

lines.text: Ah, looking for a little a "pick-me-up"?
Well allow me to assist you with some uh...assistance.
First one's free! Wait, nope. Forget it, you didn't hear that.
Make yourself aware of my wares. Heh heh.
See anything you like?
Peruse away.
You break it, you buy it.
Don't low-ball me. I know what got here.

topics.prompt: You mentioned something about "comedian resilience" before?

lines.text: Say no more, say no more! Your pal Joey's gonna show you the ropes of showbiz.

topics.prompt: Roast me, Joey!

lines.text: Woah-ho, slow down there champ! Don't want you ending up in the burn ward.
lines.note: Said as if he's pretending to be a sports coach watching out for an athlete pushing themselves too hard

lines.text: You gotta recoup your self esteem before I lay into you like that again.
Okie-doke, but remember you asked for it!
Brace yourself.
Hope you got a salve ready cause you're about to get burned.
You're a glutton for punishment.
One roast, comin' right up!
Ever wonder how a comedian gets up on stage to suffer the slings and arrows of all them hecklin' asshats without even so much as breakin' a sweat?
lines.note: says "slings and arrows" in a mock Shakespearean actor tone

lines.text: Two words. Comedian. Resilience.
lines.note: Sales pitch.

lines.text: You don't owe those chucklefucks nothin'! Pardon my French. You're a star! Who the hell are they to boo you?
lines.note: Motivation speech

lines.text: See what you gotta do is flip their aggressive energy on them and make it yours.
Let their insults, or flying tatos, bounce off you like water off a radgull's back. Capeesh?

topics.prompt: Capeesh.

lines.text: Quick learner. I like that about you.

topics.prompt: What's a radgull?

lines.text: It's what you get when you cross a gull with a nuke. I dunno, I'm not a scientist.
lines.note: Brushing this off - player's question is not important

lines.text: So here's what happens next. I'm gonna roast you and you're just gonna laugh it off. After that nothing's gonna get under your skin.
It'll build up your resilience like firewalkers walkin' barefoot on hot coals. Mind over matter. It's like psychiatry or y'know some crap like that but it works!
You just give me the word when you're ready.

topics.prompt: Ouch. That really stung.

lines.text: Walk it off!
Too bad they don't make stimpaks for feelings, huh?

topics.prompt: Fuck you too!

lines.text: Whoa! The language on you.
lines.note: Faux shock. He's in on the joke

lines.text: Fuggedaboutit!
You kiss your mother with that mouth?

topics.prompt: Ha! Nice one, Joey!

lines.text: Now you're ready to take on the world.
Water off a radgull's back, baby!
Boom. Roasted.
Got 'em!
You want I should call the Responders to come treat that burn?
Badum-tss!
Zing!
Let me know if you need some ice for that burn.
You're so dumb when you were a baby your dad gave you an "I'm S.P.E.C.A.L." book. That's "special" without the I for intelligence, dummy.
lines.note: SPECAL pronounced "speckle

lines.text: You're so ugly you make me wanna quit drinking just in case I ever start seeing two of youse!
You're so fat when they need a new nuke code they just get you to hop on a scale. Ha-hoh! Boom!
You're so uncivilized the only culture you've got is mold.
Your family tree must have been a cactus 'cause you're a real prick.
You must have a real open mind, 'cause I can hear the wind whistling through your ears.
Yeesh, you're so ugly you could become ghoulified and no one would even notice.
How 'bout, your cranium called. It's got some space to rent. Haha!
You're so fat when you go camping the yao guai have to hide their food!
lines.note: Yao guai - Yao rhymes with "Ow!" and Guai rhymes with "eye

lines.text: You're so dumb when you play Russian Roulette you cheat and load an extra bullet. Lucky for you your aim's so bad even at that range you miss!
You're so ugly you don't need a Stealth Boy to be sneaky 'cause nobody ever wants to look at you.
Your aim's so bad when you throw rocks at the ground you miss!
If being ugly was a crime you'd be on the most wanted list. And given your looks it'd probably be the first time anybody's ever wanted you.
I never forget a face, but in your case I wish I could make an exception. Yours looks like it caught fire and someone put it out with a tire iron.
Your stench is so bad you make me wish I was a ghoul just so I didn't have a nose.
You're so stupid it takes you an entire hour to make Instamash.
I heard you was strong but I guess they were talking about your stench! Pee-yoo. Your breath would make onions cry!
You're so stupid when you heard it was chilly outside you grabbed a bowl and spoon.
You're so fat when you try to haul ass it takes you two trips!

topics.prompt: You use humor as a defense mechanism.

lines.text: Exactly! It turns out if you make 'em laugh then maybe they won't make you bleed. Keep 'em laughing and maybe they'll keep you alive.
Hell, tell 'em the occasional groaner and they might even toss a few tatos your way. Kid's gotta eat, right?

topics.prompt: You trade jokes in exchange for your life?

lines.text: Hey if you've got something they want and they can't take it from your corpse then you're more valuable to them alive than dead.
Everybody needs a good laugh and I provide 'em with the jokes!
And that's the story of how Joey Bello became a standup comedian. Course if I'm lucky enough to get a stool I happily become a sitdown one. Get it?
Don't worry. It's just a nickname.
Teddy's actually short for Theodore. Heh-heh.
lines.note: Joke here is that you'd think "Toe Taker" was the nickname, not that Teddy was the nickname. He really does take toes.

lines.text: Speaking of funny nicknames d'you know Dick is short for Richard? No kidding. Now you're probably asking yourself how do you get Dick from Richard.
You gotta ask him nice! Hey-oh!

topics.prompt: Do you have any family back home?

lines.text: Before the big one my family lived in a small town on the outskirts of New Jersey, back when I was just an ankle-biter.
lines.note: A bit casual. It was also a long time ago so he's not too broken up about it.

lines.text: After the bombs it was just me and ma left. We stuck it out there for awhile, ya know best we could, then made our way towards Atlantic City.

topics.prompt: Is your mom in Atlantic City?

lines.text: She tried her best but ma just wasn't cut out for life in the apocalypse. Her spirit died. Then her body joined it. I was, you know probably eleven?
lines.note: Said casually/joking but he is a bit sensitive about his mom

lines.text: Ma was always super supportive though! Even back then when I told her I wanted to be a comedian she'd just laugh so hard.
It took a few years and a few scars but I eventually made it to Atlantic City. I started small, scored some gigs on the pier, even earned some caps!
It's a hard-knock life, kid, but hey that's showbiz!

topics.prompt: What happened to your dad?

lines.text: Ma said dad was a hero. A firefighter. Lost him and my brothers in the aftermath of the bombs.
lines.note: Proud his dad was a hero even though he barely knew him. Also a bit bitter he died

lines.text: I barely remember my old man let alone my brothers. They were all bigger and older than me. Big enough to help out, old enough to get themselves killed.
lines.note: A bit bitter - he believes putting your neck out to help gets you killed and that cost him his family.

topics.prompt: What's New Jersey like?

lines.text: New Jersey? Oof, freakin' horrible. Poisonous chems on the streets, filth everywhere, people killin' each other over a can of beans...
lines.note: Exaggerated. This is a self-dig joke. He actually loves New Jersey

lines.text: And then the bombs dropped. Ah-ha, hey-oh!
lines.note: implying all the bad stuff existed before the bomb

topics.prompt: It's that bad?

lines.text: Nah, I'm just talkin' smack.

topics.prompt: New Jersey sucks. Noted.

lines.text: Whoa, watch your mouth! Huh? Ain't nobody earned the right to talk about New Jersey until you've called it home.
lines.note: Doesn't want the player making fun of New Jersey

lines.text: Truth is, it's not as bad as some places and helluva lot better than some others. Atlantic City's a real good time if you've got the caps.
I'd tell you to tell 'em Joey sent you if you ever find your way to AC, but it's probably a bad idea if you're a fan of havin' unbroken legs.

topics.prompt: Why not just get yourself a gun?

lines.text: 'Cause my aim ain't shit! Whoops, sorry ma. I couldn't hit water if I fell in a lake. Took me 16 years just to hit puberty.
lines.note: sorry cause he slipped up and swore

lines.text: Sure, I'll throw hands in a barroom brawl but when spit really hits the fan I get the hell outta Dodge.
I guess you could call me a "running joke"! Ha ha ha ha! Zing!

topics.prompt: How does telling jokes keep you alive?

lines.text: Look, life was hard out there for a kid. Guy like me crosses paths with a raider and all they see is a punching bag.
lines.note: Half serious but also laughing at himself a bit/self aware

lines.text: You know how they say when you got a hammer every problem looks like a nail? Well when you're a comedian all your problems look like punchlines.
So I crack wise. Tell a joke. Break the ice and then hope they don't break my bones.

topics.prompt: Why did you leave New Jersey?

lines.text: Short story short, I made a joke at a made man's expense and he wanted payback.
lines.note: This and the following lines are half truth, half a joke setup

lines.text: Thankfully I got tipped off by a pal on the inside. "Joey! You really crossed the line this time!" he says.
I know, I know! How much is it going to cost me to smooth things over? I ask. "Two caps", he says.
I'm thinking, "Two caps? That's nothing! What's the catch?
Turns out they wanted my knee caps!
I've grown real attached to my legs so I hoofed it outta town with just the clothes on my back and the caps in my pocket. Use 'em or lose 'em, right?

topics.prompt: Why did you become a comedian?

lines.text: 'Cause I dropped out of school and did a lot of chems.
lines.note: A joke at comedians' expense

lines.text: Nah, I'm just breakin' your balls. I never went to school!
The truth is it was a survival tactic. I was always a small fry. Ya know, runt of the litter. Easy pickings for gangs and raiders.
Comedy kept me alive.

topics.prompt: You're not from around here?

lines.text: What, am I not blending in with the local yokels? What gave it away? My cultural refinement and foreign charm?
lines.note: All said in jest. He's new to Appalachia and aware that New Jersey isn't known for its cultural refinement either

lines.text: Nah, I'm from back East. New Jersey born and raised.

topics.prompt: How to you come up with your jokes?

lines.text: Ya, when I was a kid I was obsessed with one-liners. Every joke I ever heard got committed to memory.
You used to be able to buy these packs of gum with a joke inside. I spent every cent of my allowance buyin' those packs and I don't even like gum!
I hate to admit it, but nearly every joke I know has been borrowed or jacked.
Truth is I'm just another scavenger doin' his best to survive. 'Course I'm standing in the spotlight getting an applause doin' it but eh, same thing.

topics.prompt: No, I'm just curious.

lines.text: I scavenge from old first-aid kits and bathroom cupboards when I can. That or I dip into the ole "swear jar" for caps and trade for 'em.

topics.prompt: Where do you get your chems from?

lines.text: Why, you lookin' to buy?

topics.prompt: I fucking love chems!

lines.text: Yeah, you do! Go get 'em Tiger!
lines.note: Hyping up the player, a fellow chem abuser

lines.text: They have this stuff back in Atlantic City that makes Psycho look like bubblegum.
Never tried it myself - ya know, way out of my class, but I hear that shit's on a whole 'nother level.
They say laughter's the best medicine but let's be real. You ever find me bleeding out just go ahead and jab me with every feel-good chem you got.

topics.prompt: That stuff will kill you.

lines.text: Yeah, I know but what doesn't? Way I see it everything we do might kill us. Might as well feel good doing it.
lines.note: Defensive/humored at the naive stance of the player. He's been using chems a long time and has heard this all before

lines.text: I knew this meatball back in Atlantic City. Wouldn't touch chems. Said they were too addictive.
This chucklehead was always drinking brake fluid instead. Claimed he could stop at any time! Ha ha ha!
lines.note: stop any time is a punchline (cause the guy was drinking brake fluid)

lines.text: Look, I know this crap ain't good for me but what's a guy gonna do? Quit? Ma never raised no quitter.
lines.note: Dismissive. Also tosses in a joke about not being a quitter as if the act of quitting is worse than doing chems

topics.prompt: You take a lot of chems?

lines.text: I guess it depends on your definition of "a lot" but yeah I'm something of a chem connoisseur. Started taking Daytripper when I was still a kid.
They say chems screw with your growth but I was always short for my age even before that.
In fact, I was so short that when I took Daytripper I didn't even get high. I got medium!

topics.prompt: Your act is shit. You're a terrible comedian.

lines.text: Woah-whoa hey! Fuck you, huh. I don't go to where you work and tell you how to eat a dick!
lines.note: More surprised than pure rage. He is angry but is masking it a bit with a snap comeback/insult

lines.text: Aw, fuck! Heh, you got me. Sorry ma, that's 10 caps for the swear jar. Shit. I mean spit! I mean ah-fu... ah sorry ma.
lines.note: Realizes he lost his cool and is embarrassed/disappointed

topics.prompt: Your act needs more pizzazz. Have you considered using props?

lines.text: What, like smashin' melons with a super sledge? Thanks for the advice but maybe leave the comedy routine to me, rookie?

topics.prompt: Keep it up! You're funny.

lines.text: You forgot handsome! But thanks, boss. Happy to be here.
Yeah, but looks aren't everything, am I right?

topics.prompt: I've got some feedback on your act.

lines.text: Lay it on me!
I once tried doing stand-up for a herd of brahmin but I got mooed off stage. Heh-ha!
Heard they're trying out a new strategy to keep the caravans hidden from raiders. They're calling it cow-moo-flage. Heh-ha-ha!
I asked 'em if they deliver chems but they told me they want to keep drugs away from the brahmin. Guess they're worried the steaks'll get too high. Come on!
When I'm ready to hit the road I might try hitching a ride with 'em West. I wonder if they could get me to Kentucky? Gotta save up some caps first.
I'm sure they mean well but with a name like "Foundation" you gotta expect people to walk all over you.
lines.note: Kind of shaking his head. He thinks "Foundation" is too nice for their own good

lines.text: Ward claims he's keepin' an eye on the "vital equipment" but it must be hard if he's gazin' through the bottom of a bottle as often as I think he is.
lines.note: Implying he thinks Ward is an alcoholic

lines.text: Those raiders up in Crater seem pretty decent Yeah, for raiders at least. I've certainly rubbed elbows with worse.
But if you ever end up drinking with 'em make sure you don't ever order a round of shots. Good way to trigger a massacre. Heh, God I kill me.
lines.note: Implying that ordering shots leads to a shootout

lines.text: Those Blood Eagles? You ever cross paths with them I suggest that you, uh, don't. Those rotters really make me think twice about doing chems.
lines.note: Blood Eagles are bad news. Even Joey doesn't want to have anything to do with them

lines.text: Of course thinking twice takes a lot of brainpower and then I want some Mentats.
lines.note: Joke/self-dig since he's a chem user

lines.text: But I'd rather try to get high sniffin' brahmin farts than deal with the Blood Eagles.
You hear this gal "Rose" on the radio? She sounds like a firecracker. Maybe I'll try to track her down and see if she wants to go day tripping.
The raiders out here should really think about getting in on the protection racket.
That's where you get people to pay you to protect them from what you'll do to them if they ever stop paying you.
You know if they're booking gigs? It might be nice to play a classy joint like The Whitespring once in a while, yeah if I stick around.
Oh, oh! What do you call a radstag on a stage? A deer in stage lights! Ha ha! Wocka-wocka!
lines.note: This is a joke commonly heard at the Whitespring and Joey is parroting/mocking it a bit cause he knows it's super cheesy.

lines.text: Seem like good people. Pretty stupid of 'em to put their necks out there but... ya know, sounds like the kinda outfit Dad would've signed up with.
lines.note: He's a bit bitter cause his dad died helping people but he also can't help but be a little impressed at people who help others

lines.text: More like the Brotherhood of Stealin', am I right?
Bet they'd like us to think they're named for the shiny Power Armor they wear but really it's 'cause they're always pinching everybody's stuff.
How many knights does it take to change a light bulb? Only one to screw it in but an entire squadron to take it from whoever owned it before that. Ha!
You meet these guys, "The Brotherhood of Steel"?
lines.note: Said like a late night comedian setup

lines.text: You meet those folks working out of the Whitespring Hotel? The Responders.
lines.note: Said like a late night comedian setup

lines.text: I've started picking up who's who when it comes to your local flavors of Raider.
You ever run into these Mothman Cultist whackadoos?
lines.note: Said like a late night comedian setup

lines.text: I'm guessing you've seen those "Super Mutants". How could you miss 'em, right?
lines.note: Said like a late night comedian setup

lines.text: What's the deal with robots?
lines.note: Said like a late night comedian setup

lines.text: There's this settlement calling themselves "Foundation".
lines.note: Said like a late night comedian setup

lines.text: You do any jobs with the Blue Ridge Caravan Company? The Brahmin drivers?
The other day I bumped into this "Insult-bot". Geez, they weren't kidding when they said the robots were coming for everybody's jobs were they?
But hey, funny is funny. I might just might have to "borrow" some of his material. Eyy-yoink.
I visited that Metal Dome place the other day. You know, the arena run by the Rust Eagles?
I placed bets on the kill-bots thinking there was no way robots programmed to do nothing but kill could possibly lose. But... zero won. Ha! Get it?
lines.note: Says "zero won" in a mock robot voice like "zero one

lines.text: I was poking around VTU and stumbled across this robot in a tattoo parlor. Bartender and drinking buddy all-in-one. Now that's my kind of robot!
You know, I once had a one night stand with a robot back in Atlantic City. I wanted to cuddle but it just wanted to screw, nut, and bolt! Hahahaha!
Come on! I'd heard Appalachia has its hillbillies but you're telling me there's really a whole group of rednecks out here worshipping a giant bug?
lines.note: Amused disbelief

lines.text: I mean sure, the Piney's back home have their Jersey Devil but at least you don't find 'em praying to it.
Growing up I never did learn what the word "apocalypse" meant. Oh well, it's not like it's the end of the world.
If you've got four drinks in one hand and another 3 in the other what have you got? Alcoholism. Badum-bump!
What has broken arms, broken legs, and lies at the bottom of a pier? People who tell jokes about the mafia. Ay-ay-ay!
lines.note: Ay-ay-ay is feigned worry. Like "I hope the mob didn't hear that".

lines.text: You know what we call a classy person back in New Jersey? A visitor.
You hear about the wise-guy that got a job workin' as a housekeeper? Yeah, he's a maid man. Oh, I'm cleanin' up here!
Makes a lot of sense we use caps for our money, doesn't it? America has always been a cap-italist country. Cha-ching!
What's a mobster's favorite game? Whack-the-mole. Ha ha!
You ever get so hungry you try eating an alarm clock? It's better than starving but it sure is time consuming.
I had this idea for a jokes-by-mail service but it didn't work out. The jokes were hilarious but the delivery was terrible.
I borrowed this pair of shoes from my chem dealer. I don't know what they were laced with but I've been trippin' all day.
You ever explore any of the old skyscrapers around here? I don't trust the elevators. In fact, I take steps to avoid them.
I was never a big fan of mutations but after walking through that radiation zone I've gotta admit - they're growing on me!
Why is breakfast cereal so bad at stand-up comedy? 'Cause Sugar Bombs! Get it? Sugar. Bombs. Yeah, all right, forget it.
I played this prank on this settler where I covered his door knob with adhesive. A week later and the guy's still furious. He just can't let it go!
What'd the redneck say to his girlfriend when they broke up? Let's just be cousins. Haha!
What's the worst thing a prison guard can find at a party? An open bar.
You hear that Santatron has a new comedy act? Yeah, it sleighs. Ho ho ho haha!
Why'd the snitch feel nervous around calendars? Cause his days were numbered. Bada-boom!
How does a mobster keep a clean conscience? Easy, they never use it.
You hear the one about the drum set that fell off the roof? Badum-tss! Heh.
You hear about the wedding they held at the old radio tower? The ceremony was only so-so but the reception was amazing!
You hear about that junkie that got addicted to soap? He's clean now.
A friend of mine stared selling fireworks, grenades, missiles, and TNT. Y'know he says business is booming.
Why'd the mafia put a hit out on the mime? He had to be silenced.
A blindfolded man walks into a bar. Then a table. Then a chair. Ha-ha, you see?
What do you call a mobster who's gotten too many rads? A gabaghoul!
lines.note: Gabagool = gaba-ghoul. Said with a strong fake Italian accent.

lines.text: Before I insult anyone I like to first walk a mile in their shoes. Yeah that way I'm a mile away and I got their shoes.
What'd the Vault-tec employee say when he saw the nukes dropping? Armageddon outta here!
I heard an old acquaintance of mine died the other day. We weren't that close, which is good, cause he stepped on a land mine.
How many mobsters does it take to throw a snitch off a cliff? None, he slipped and fell all by himself.
What do you get when you cross a mob boss and his right hand man? A bullet to the head.
You hear about that cool bachelor party they threw for the two-headed buck? It was a real rad radstag stag.
Why'd the robot cross the road? It was programmed to be a chicken. Baw-cawk!

topics.prompt: You can stay for now but don't get comfy.

lines.text: Got it. I'll keep my shoes on.
lines.note: A bit cold. Player might kick him out at any time and he knows it.

topics.prompt: You're welcome to stay for as long as you need.

lines.text: Thanks, boss. I appreciate it. I know I joke around a lot but I mean it.
lines.note: sincere. The player has been kind to him and he knows it

topics.prompt: Where would you go?

lines.text: Was thinking I'd head West. Save up some caps here telling jokes then see if I can hire the Blue Ridge Caravan Company to take me towards Kentucky.
I've heard rumors Vegas might still be standing. Maybe I'll head there eventually, or try for Reno. Who knows, might even make it to Hollywood!
Next time you see Joey Bello it could be in gorgeous PanaLuxe Color! Which I'm guessing is like real life, only better cause it's made in Hollywood.
lines.note: He know's this is an unrealistic dream but is selling it

topics.prompt: Are you planning to stay in Appalachia?

lines.text: Nah, not forever. Appalachia's nice, but I'm not sure if it's a fit, you know? I'll be here a while if you'll have me. Got to save up some caps.
There's this one, Grahm, eh he seems alright. Tried to sell me meat. I tried to teach him a joke, but he butchered it.
Everybody likes to hate on Super Mutants but y'know they're not all bad. It's just that 99% of them that give the rest a bad name.

topics.prompt: Sorry, Joey.  Maybe that was a little harsh.

lines.text: Yeah next time maybe just kick me in the balls instead, huh? Still, I guess I could take my own advice and grow a thicker skin.

topics.prompt: Geez. What happend to "water off a radgull's back"?

lines.text: Yeah I guess you ruffled this radgull's feathers huh? Maybe I'm gettin' soft, I wasn't expecting you to lay into me like that. Well criticism noted.
lines.note: Trying to act amused but he was rattled by the player being so mean

topics.prompt: Got any more gossip?

lines.text: Here's the scoop.
Alright, but you didn't hear it from me.

topics.prompt: That's enough jokes for now.

lines.text: Good idea. Better to let 'em air out a little bit.
Oh yeah, don't want to have too much fun, right?

topics.prompt: Haha! Tell me another one!

lines.text: I got you!
What, you think I'm made of jokes? Alright try this one on.
That's it. That's all the jokes I got. Nah! I'm kidding!
This one slayed 'em back home.

topics.prompt: Good one, Joey!

lines.text: Goodnight everybody!
lines.note: Mock sign off as if he just finished a stand up set

lines.text: Thanks, you've been a great audience.
lines.note: Said as if ending a show

lines.text: I'll be here all night. And day.

topics.prompt: What's with the jar on your stage?

lines.text: That? That's my swear jar. You know! My cuss pot, my curse can, my profanity pitcher. It's where I toss a few caps if I slip up and drop an F-bomb.

items.description: Reach for the stars with Katherine, an astronomer obsessed with the study of extraterrestrial life.
items.howToObtain: Can be purchased with certain bundles from the Atom Shop.

lines: Can be purchased with certain bundles from the Atom Shop.
Perception increased by 1. Energy weapon ammo weighs 50% less.

lines.text: All right, darling.
lines.note: In response to "Goodbye for now

lines.text: Understood.
lines.note: In response to "Goodbye for now

lines.text: Very well.
lines.note: In response to "Goodbye for now

lines.text: Of course.
lines.note: Response to "Let's talk about something else

lines.text: What else is on your mind?
lines.note: Response to "Let's talk about something else

lines.text: Oh? What is it?
lines.note: Response to "Let's talk about something else

lines.text: Certainly.
lines.note: Response to "Let's talk about something else

lines.text: I sometimes get a queasy feeling when thinking about abductions. Like I've eaten a pot of butterflies.
Stargazing is more than a hobby. For me, it's a career.
If only the nukes could target skyscrapers, and only skyscrapers, it might almost be a net gain.
A good scientist has a healthy curiosity and an open mind. Too many learned men turn to books assuming the answers are already known.
I don't mind sitting down and reading a comic book. I just hate the fact that Captain Cosmos always wins.
When studying the extraterrestrial, the few answers we do get always lead to more questions. But at least it means I'll always be employed.
When I'm stuck on a theory, I like to meditate. Meditation and exercise are good for the mind.
The apocalypse probably set us back a century in extraterrestrial relations. At least, I hope it did. God forbid they see it as a chance to invade.
It's important to read, but it's equally as important to experience. Finding the balance is key.
Constellations are funny things. Patterns we project upon things that predate us.
I love a good meteor shower. Watching the light streak across a canvas of stars is positively romantic.
If you get lost out there in the Wasteland, you can always use the sky as a map. Winds may change, but the north star will never lead you astray.
I drink red wine when I'm studying planets, because it reminds me of Mars. White wine is for the stars. When I'm doing both? A ros�.
When Maria Mitchell discovered her comet, she had to publish her discovery using her father's name. That's the boy's club at work for you.
The other day, some scavver called me "Toots." What does that even mean? I didn't even know how to respond.
I once had a gun that never jammed. Instead of selling it when I needed the caps, I should have married it. We all have our regrets, and that's mine.
One thing I'm sure an alien would never say is, "Take me to your leader." Rest assured, they don't need an escort.
I never understood the appeal of coffee. Tea is by far the superior of the two.
Cryptid hunters like Calvin van Lowe are the worst. To say he got what was coming to him is the understatement of the year.
As someone who takes their profession seriously, it is quite frustrating dealing with claims of extraterrestrial abduction.
Morning. People say it's a sunrise, but what they really mean is, the planet has made another spin.
Interviewing Mister Xerxo, which is obviously not his real name was, quite frankly, one of the most frustrating experiences of my career.
When walking the tightrope of life, never look down.
Do you have a favorite constellation? I've always been partial to Pegasus.
A clear sky bodes well for tonight.
Rain is so disappointing.
Hello there traveler, my name is Kat. I'm an astronomer.
lines.note: Pronounced "Cat".

lines.text: The earliest recorded abduction was in Salem, in 1697. There's a tape of a man who claims to have been swept up into a great spaceship in the sky.
You're not so bad, you know. You might even be swell.
Not even planets move in perfect circles. Their movements are elliptical; they bend and swerve. As do we.
Aristotle believed the universe was composed of four elements: earth, water, wind, and fire. He also listed a fifth element, to describe the heavens.
Ether. It's that fifth element, that unknown particle that stretches the cosmos, that is my calling.
It's good to keep a detailed plan of the near future. When I'm not charting the stars, I like to chart a course for the rest of my week.
If I were to ever make contact with alien life, I'm not sure what my reaction would be.
I like to think I'd boldly introduce myself, but my gut reaction might be to hide behind you.
Here on Earth, I've met my share of hare-brains and nincompoops. It'd be foolish to assume alien life doesn't have its fair share of the same.
I love classical music. It always puts me in a thinking mood. I save jazz for when I want my mind to dance.
lines.note: Relaxed at the thought

lines.text: Nothing more depressing than clouds. The stars are tucked away, and their light shines for no one.
Almost all unknown phenomena can be attributed to the extraterrestrial.
Witchcraft, paranormals, gray hairs that you're absolutely certain you plucked the day before... all of it can be attributed to alien interference.
One of my prize possessions is a Dollond refracting telescope.
It has three inches of aperture and a forty-six inch focal length, just like the one Maria Mitchell used to discover her comet.
That is one too many highs, and I don't even use chems. Still, a cursory examination of your body shows you are human.
Not that I've done anything more in depth, of course. That would be inappropriate.

topics.prompt: Tell me more about this ex of yours.

lines.text: If you have a few hours, I could probably tell you all about her. Suffice to say, thinking about the experience is difficult to stomach.
If I'm being perfectly honest, I only started dating her because I thought she was an alien.
So, my eventual disappointment was on several levels.

topics.prompt: You suspect your cat was an alien?

lines.text: Maybe. It would make sense for aliens to disguise themselves as felines, after all.
They come and go as they please, and yet are often adopted and cared for by humans, allowing for easy observation.

topics.prompt: You think I'm an alien?

lines.text: Well, that or you're just a highly productive, high performing, and high functioning individual.
lines.note: Player is male

lines.text: Well, that or you're just a highly productive, high performing, and highly attractive individual.
lines.note: Player is female

topics.prompt: Why would the Brotherhood of Steel be villains?

lines.text: My apologies darling, "villain" is the wrong word.
They are hoarders. And the natural inclination of a hoarder is not to share.
If they were to discover the body of an alien species and their technology, I don't think they'd be announcing their findings in the Watoga Times.
But I suppose they also wouldn't sell those ray guns to the local raider clans, so at least there's that.
I would almost prefer villains like Doctor Zorbo who laugh maniacally and wear their brains on their head.
Villains who look and talk like us are far more insidious.

topics.prompt: Any thoughts on the Brotherhood of Steel taking it over?

lines.text: They are an interesting lot, no doubt, but their motives leave me suspicious.
I realize you're a member, so I'll tread carefully, but the point still stands.
lines.note: She knows player is a member of the Brotherhood of Steel, so she comes down softer.

topics.prompt: I would love to get my hands on such a device.

lines.text: The way you said that, with the twisted smile and furrowed brow, doesn't give me confidence you'd use it responsibly.

topics.prompt: It's terrible that noble endeavors can be twisted like that.

lines.text: Yes, I imagine quite a bit of taxpayer money was used to fund the project. But those are concerns of a world we no longer inhabit.
I used to chide my ex for not paying more in taxes, but seeing the wars we funded, clearly the last laugh is hers.

topics.prompt: What, you don't like blizzards in August?

lines.text: Well, I do have plenty of fashionable winter wear, but it helps to have some measure of predictability.
Imagine diving into in the pool in your two piece bathing suit only to find the water half-frozen by the time you descend.
Even if I survived the fall, I'd still need to have my lawyers file a rather lengthy suit.

topics.prompt: Manipulating the weather isn't inherently evil. You can make rain for crops.

lines.text: Yes, but if that were your motive, you should advertise it plainly.
It's like when my ex told me she loved books, and I'd find her novels while I was on travel as a gift.
It would've saved us both a lot of trouble if she admitted she couldn't read.
Although I suppose the inability to read road signs was the first clue, but she was cute, so I believed her.

topics.prompt: You want to get abducted?

lines.text: I want to be invited. I want to travel to the furthest star and walk on worlds beyond.
But if I am abducted, I hope it's with someone like yourself by my side.
With my brains and your ingenuity, commandeering that spaceship would not be out of the realm of possibility.
And then we'd get to travel the galaxy on our own terms.
In any case, part of me is envious of our dear Colton. It makes me wonder what the criteria is for abduction, and why I can't seem to meet it.

topics.prompt: Do you think they wanted Colton to tell his story, to spread fear?

lines.text: The military aspect did cross my mind. Although again, from a tactical perpsective, I don't see the value in not abducting him blind.
If the perpetrator were indeed wearing a spacesuit, that would reveal a rather glaring weakness should they invade.

topics.prompt: It's not complicated. The aliens just wanted to experiment on him.

lines.text: Would that not seem rather inefficient? We have ample medical records, information that could be easily obtained at a local library.
Nor would I think a man who lives selling and consuming hot dogs to be a model representative of humankind.

topics.prompt: I think Colton made the whole thing up.

lines.text: That's always a possibility. But why bother with such an outlandish lie? There's no motive for it.
It would only reduce his standing in the community, and make him the subject of gossip.

topics.prompt: Maybe Colton wasn't abducted, he was invited.

lines.text: That is my theory. Although it doesn't explain why he'd make claims of experimentation.
Surely, if you were a party guest in my home, you'd leave with a more glowing endorsement. My explanation for that is simple: cultural differences.

topics.prompt: The aliens didn't want to kill him, so they just got him drunk.

lines.text: But not so drunk he forgot what happened. A simple cloth bag over the head would have also ensured he never caught view of his abductor.
And he did view him, in stunning detail. Gray skin, black eyes.

topics.prompt: What do you think happened to Colton?

lines.text: I believe he was telling the truth. But his truth. Or rather, the truth his abductors wanted us to know.
Keep in mind, our dear hot dog vendor did not have to be returned. He did not have to be contacted.
He could've easily been abducted and disappeared and no one would have bothered to look for his remains. The question I struggle with, is why?

topics.prompt: I believe you're referring to the Flatwoods Monster.

lines.text: Naturally. What some have described as a round, octopus-like head, I believe to be a space helmet.
Which, of course, only leads to more questions. Is our atmosphere toxic to their species? Or is it merely the composition?
If only I could speak with the man who was abducted, Mr. Colton Pickins, I would be able to do more than hunt and peck for clues.

topics.prompt: I have no idea what you're referring to.

lines.text: Surely you've been through Flatwoods, and heard of the monster that haunts the surrounding forest?
Well, it's my opinion that monster isn't a creature of this planet, but rather, contact from an alien life form.
Why it chose Mr. Colton Pickins as its emissary, however, is beyond me.

topics.prompt: That sounds scary and oddly delicious.

lines.text: While I'm contractually obligated to agree with your dining decisions, I do hope you reconsider that thought.
On the other hand, we've all had to consume much worse to survive, so who am I to judge Mr. Colton Pickins and his career choices.

topics.prompt: The aliens have discovered hot dog technology?

lines.text: That would be dreadful. I would hope an interstellar species would have evolved past the point of consuming mystery meat.
No, no, the hot dogs would be a reference to the workplace of one Colton Pickins, alien abductee.

topics.prompt: Your thoughts on Stella Skyfire?

lines.text: A character perfect for Hollywood. So thin you can barely make her out.
If the writers know their history, maybe her name's a reference to Annie Jump Cannon, the astronomer who discovered stellar spectra.
I just wish they gave her more lines so we could know for sure.

topics.prompt: What about Jangles the Moon Monkey?

lines.text: It's not implausible. After all, the first organism in space was not a man, but a Persian house cat named Mr. Pebbles.
We call ourselves brave explorers, and yet we've often had our pets do the dirty work that we are too cowardly to do.

topics.prompt: What do you think of Captain Cosmos?

lines.text: I find his portrayal to be more absurd than Dr. Zorbo, to be honest. But only because he's meant to be a mirror image of man.
And we delude ourselves into thinking we're better than we are. Especially, the men.

topics.prompt: You think Dr. Zorbo is real?

lines.text: I don't think it's impossible, no. It's no more ridiculous a mythology than any of our current religions.
Whether it's a vengeful god or an evil doctor with a death ray, the stories originate from somewhere.
Sometimes, that story is a complete fiction, born from the imagination. Other times, it only seems that way.

topics.prompt: I met a uniformed astronaut named Sofia Daguerre. Have you heard of her?

lines.text: Why no. An astronaut, in uniform? As in, she just fell from the sky? How is that even possible?
lines.note: Excitement and disbelief

topics.prompt: Have you heard about the Valiant-1 space station? It's been taken over by raiders.

lines.text: (Sigh) How does that bible verse go? Matthew 5:5. "Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.

topics.prompt: Have you ever met an extraterrestrial?

lines.text: None that have been confirmed, but many whom I've suspected.
There was the ex who pronounced "Sugar Bombs" with a long "S." Extremely suspicious, that one.
lines.note: Ssss, like a snake.

lines.text: There was my pet tabby cat, Herschel, named after Caroline, who seemingly teleported from place to place, although I never witnessed the act.
And of course, there's you, who I find unlike anyone I've ever met before.

topics.prompt: As an astronomer, have you been to the ATLAS Observatory?

lines.text: Yes, I have. Suffice to say I was quite disappointed with what I found, and I don't mean the army of hostile robots.
But I suppose it's not the first time scientific discovery has been used as a front for ulterior motives. In this case, weather manipulation.

topics.prompt: What do you know about alien activity in Appalachia?

lines.text: There is one tale that caught my interest. A story about flashing lights, floating octopi, and curiously, the smell of hot dogs.

topics.prompt: What are your thoughts on science fiction, like Dr. Zorbo and Captain Cosmos?

lines.text: I'm of two minds, really. On the one hand, any sort of scientific curiosity and interest in astronomy is a positive force.
On the other hand, if that information is presented in a scientifically inaccurate sideshow, some of that positivity goes to waste.
But to your question - do I believe in little green men, or that an evil green doctor is trying to thwart our attempts to travel through space?
Well, I've seen no evidence to support that. But I'm not ruling it out entirely.

topics.prompt: Where are your family now?

lines.text: They died shortly after the war, thank goodness. At the time, it was quite traumatic, but now I realize they were spared the worst of it.

topics.prompt: Did you ever have any concerns about your own mental health?

lines.text: Oh yes. When your passion is studying little green men in flying saucers, it does beg the question, "How far does the apple fall from the tree?
I even found an actual apple tree and shook it with every muscle in my body. It was my own little Newtonian experiment.
But in the midst of making a fool of myself, apples landing on my head, I realized I never had any reason to suspect my mother was ill.
It wasn't until she told me her history that the thought wormed its way into my head.

topics.prompt: How did she get out?

lines.text: A nail file in a cake? That's their version, at least. In reality, it was just university pressure.
My father worked at VTU, and was in need of mother's help for a paper he was working on. He tracked her down, pulled some strings, and got her out.
She stole a worker's uniform on the way out though, which always amused me.

topics.prompt: I like board games, but I don't have time to play, sadly.

lines.text: That sounds like an excuse, darling. You're your own boss, you can certainly make time for whatever recreation you need.
It's not always the world that needs saving, after all. Sometimes, it's friendships.

topics.prompt: I love board games! What's your favorite?

lines.text: Well, I'd be hard pressed to choose just one. But I suppose I'm partial to The Legendary Run, despite all its flaws.
We should definitely carve out some time to play together. Fair warning though, I can get quite competitive.

topics.prompt: Board games are for children.

lines.text: And wouldn't we all like to be children, once in a while?
Perhaps it's time for you to relax and rediscover that child-like joy you've so clearly repressed.
But I suppose doing adult things like murder and mayhem are just as therapeutic.
lines.note: A bit mocking.

topics.prompt: We should play a board game sometime.

lines.text: Yes, we can make an entire night of it! Blast Radius, The Legendary Run, they're all good choices.
As cliche as it might sound, the "Don't Be Bored Games Company" really does what it claims.
All the times I've played, I've never once been bored.
In any case, to answer your question, I like to drink wine and play board games, believe it or not. It's the perfect way to disengage.

topics.prompt: Not me. I've got all the free time in the world.

lines.text: That sounds like a recipe for boredom. Personally, I believe in a balance.
The stars in the sky are beautiful, no doubt, but without the empty space, the light would be blinding.
However, if all you had was the void, you would feel empty and alone.

topics.prompt: I don't have that problem. I never get tired of doing what I love.

lines.text: Is that so? Perhaps you're the extraterrestrial being I've been searching for all along. It would explain a lot.
But alas, the rest of us ordinary humans need breaks. Even from what we love.

topics.prompt: That makes it sound ominous.

lines.text: Yes, like the Sword of Damocles, but that's hardly the case. Astronomy is what I love, but even a loved one can suffocate you at times.
Science is the foundation for what we do, but not the foundation of why we do it.
Gazing up at the stars, I felt a passion I didn't have for other fields. That is not something I will soon forget.

topics.prompt: I'll never get those thirty seconds of my life back.

lines.text: You can darling, you just need to travel faster than the speed of light. If I smack you hard enough, you just might achieve it.
But regardless, I think the overall message still applies.

topics.prompt: Is that it? I'm kind of disappointed.

lines.text: Well, there's no accounting for taste, is there. Especially a palate as dull as yours. But, the message still applies.

topics.prompt: Not my thing, but I can see why it inspired you.

lines.text: Exactly, darling. I feel it applies to everyone, from the astronomers who study the sky to a Mole Miner burrowing tunnels on the ground.

topics.prompt: I like it.

lines.text: It's a good poem, but it also serves as an important reminder, whether you are a scientist or a scavenger.

topics.prompt: That's a beautiful poem.

lines.text: And a reminder of how one should live their life.

topics.prompt: Sure, I'd like to hear it.

lines.text: Very well. "When I Heard the Learn'd Astronomer", by Walt Whitman.
When I heard the learn'd astronomer, When the proofs, the figures, were ranged in columns before me,
When I was shown the charts and diagrams, to add, divide, and measure them,
When I sitting heard the astronomer where he lectured with much applause in the lecture-room,
How soon unaccountable I became tired and sick, Till rising and gliding out I wander'd off by myself,
In the mystical moist night-air, and from time to time, Look'd up in perfect silence at the stars.

topics.prompt: Maybe later, when I'm trying to sleep.

lines.text: Very well, but I assure you, it may invigorate you, as it did me.

topics.prompt: No thanks.

lines.text: Very well, I will refrain.
I will tell you though that when I read it, I looked up at the night sky and for the first time in my career, I knew I had found my calling.

topics.prompt: What changed?

lines.text: I read a poem. "When I Heard the Learn'd Astronomer". I can recite it for you, if you like.

topics.prompt: [Perception 4+] That tells me why humanity would want to study aliens. Not you.

lines.text: You're right, darling. I didn't answer your question. Not truthfully, anyhow.
The reality is, as a teenager I planned on majoring in one of the standard disciplines. Chemistry, physics, or biology.
But for whatever reason, I never felt fulfilled. It all seemed so mundane.

topics.prompt: I agree. Meeting other species would have a profound effect on us.

lines.text: Undoubtedly, it would provide us with a chance to change our fate.
Hopefully we can use that information to better effect this time around.

topics.prompt: Fair enough.

lines.text: You have inadvertently said something quite wise.
It is, after all, quite fair. Second chances are not something we're entitled to. It's best we don't squander it.
There's no denying that humanity is, more or less, a failed experiment. But it's an experiment that's been given a second roll of the dice.
An encounter with an advanced civilization would give us something to aspire to be, or at worst, give us an example of what not to become.
And that's why I believe it's important.

topics.prompt: I like discovering a bottle of whiskey when I raid an empty warehouse.

lines.text: If that's what invigorates you darling, I will not deny you that pleasure.
I personally would prefer a glass of red wine under a constellation of white hot stars.
But that's really the point, isn't it. In discovering others, we find out who we are.

topics.prompt: Finding out the answer to life's greatest question is thrilling.

lines.text: Yes. "Are we alone?" We most certainly are in the metaphorical sense, but in the literal? It's highly unlikely.
And meeting another species would not only offer us a chance to expand our sense of existence, but also offer a chance at self-reflection.

topics.prompt: But why aliens?

lines.text: Why indeed. I suppose like all discoveries, the point is to not only learn about others, but learn about yourself.

topics.prompt: Do you have any family?

lines.text: None I dare speak of publicly. My parents met under unusual circumstances, my mother being a former patient of Allegheny Asylum.
For years they told me she was a nurse. When the scandal broke, she decided to confess to the lesser crime of being a patient.

topics.prompt: What do you do in your free time?

lines.text: I don't know if I ever have a free moment. When your life's work literally hangs over your head, it's always on your mind.

topics.prompt: Why the interest in extraterrestrials?

lines.text: For me, the thrill of discovery is enough. And would it be cruel to say that terrestrials bore me?
Well, that's not entirely fair. I've never met an alien, after all. Who's to say they aren't dreadful conversation partners?

topics.prompt: Are you comfortable selling your research materials?

lines.text: Of course. One has to make a living, after all. In this world, we can hardly depend on wealthy benefactors and the kindness of strangers.
But rest assured, anything I sell to you has been thoroughly investigated, poked, prodded, and inquired.
In short, they have exhausted their scientific value, and must now enter their second phase of life, as a commodity.

topics.prompt: What other services do you offer?

lines.text: You mean besides my winsome personality? For one, I can help you use your scopes more effectively.
Whether you use that scope to gaze at the stars or target the head of a Blood Eagle is up to you.
Have you forgotten our session already, darling? It doesn't seem like your aim is off.
Then you shall have it.
Happy stargazing.

topics.prompt: Let's see what you've got for sale.

lines.text: There was a meteor shower the other day that led to some interesting discoveries. Take a look.
All the best in otherwordly goods.
You'll find my shop items to be out of this world.
From the stars in the sky to the pack on your back.

topics.prompt: I have questions about your work.

lines.text: As any curious mind should. What did you want to ask me?

topics.prompt: I want to know more about you.

lines.text: Of course, darling. What do you want to know?
Of course you do, my darling. Everyone that encounters my otherworldly charm assumes my story is as infinite as the cosmos.
But I assure you, no life is as interesting as the stars. Not even mine. Yet I will do my best to make it so. So go ahead, ask away.

topics.prompt: I'm in need of your services.

lines.text: Naturally, darling. What can I do for you?

topics.prompt: Nice to meet you.

lines.text: The pleasure is all mine, darling. I've never met a person so polite and well mannered. No human, anyway.

topics.prompt: Oh wow, can you read me my horoscope?

lines.text: No, that's astrology. Pseudo-scientific bunk. I'm an astronomer. I study the sky, and I don't tolerate idiocy.

topics.prompt: Studying the infinite cosmos is a noble pursuit.

lines.text: Oh, so you dabble in the sciences? Wonderful.
lines.note: Releaved that the player is not an idiot.

lines.text: Perhaps you'd like to be my assistant. Or, even better, my prot�g�.

topics.prompt: That's an interesting job to have, given the times.

lines.text: Of course. Just because the world isn't worth a nickel in a dime store doesn't mean the sky isn't still its illustrious self.
One only needs to look up to see what humanity can still discover.
Of course, I should mention, I'm not just any astronomer.
My study is specific to one particular field. Extraterrestrial life.

topics.prompt: So you're not a real scientist, but a crazy person. Understood.

lines.text: Well, that's rude. I'd slap you, but you're covered in filth of the wasteland, and I don't want to get my hands dirty.
But I digress. Copernicus was "crazy." Galileo, Newton, and countless others.

topics.prompt: You mean aliens? Do you worry people won't take you seriously?

lines.text: Not at all. Such a distinction would put me in good company. Galileo and Copernicus were deemed mentally unfit, and persecuted by lesser astronomers.

topics.prompt: It's a worthy field study. There's a lot out there we don't know.

lines.text: And that is what excites me so! We are frontiersman of a different kind.
We are braving the unknown, charting the uncharted, diving headfirst into the great expanse!
If that doesn't shake you to your core, then I would check your pulse and make sure you aren't already dead.

topics.prompt: That's all very intriguing, but how do you survive? Studying aliens doesn't put food on the table.

lines.text: Well yes, I don't deny my time is often limited by earthly considerations. But that is where people like yourself come in.
Benefactors who will gladly donate their time and resources in exchange for that which is priceless: knowledge.
I guess what I'm saying, darling, when you question my mental health, be sure you're not the one wearing a straitjacket.
Still, if you're concerned about the practicalities of having me in your employ, I can provide you with schematics and weapons relevant to my study.

topics.prompt: All right. I look forward to seeing what you uncover.

lines.text: As do I darling, as do I.

topics.prompt: Okay. We'll see how it goes.

lines.text: Yes, onwards we go and hopefully, upwards as well.

topics.prompt: Hopefully you'll get abducted by day's end.

lines.text: The abductions happen at night darling, but point taken.
I would like to speak with her one day, that would be an interesting conversation to be sure.

topics.prompt: Actually they were lucky to be part of a great experiment, linking their brains to an A.I.

lines.text: I think you and I have different understanding of the word "luck." But I'm glad Ms. Daguerre managed to find the ground in one piece.

topics.prompt: It gets worse. They were being experimented on, and had their brains linked to an A.I.

lines.text: That sounds like the ending to every sci-fi movie I've ever seen. In the end, the true monster is man. I'm glad she managed to survive his clutches.

topics.prompt: Because she's an alien.

lines.text: I have to admit, that was my first thought, but clearly you're being facetious.

topics.prompt: With strong determination, you can survive in space just by holding your breath.

lines.text: Maybe if you had green skin and vacuum-powered gills, but I assume the astronaut in question is human.

topics.prompt: She was put in suspended animation, as part of the Deep Sleep Project.

lines.text: Well, the deep sleep part sounds wonderfully relaxing. But I have to imagine that it was anything but.
Contrast that with true valor, like the brave astronauts who once inhabited that station, and it paints quite the portrait.

topics.prompt: I know, it's terrible. What has the world come to?

lines.text: I share your pain. But we shall endeavor to correct it, together.
If we happen to fall, we shall get back up again, and push aside any raiders that happened to move in in the meantime.

topics.prompt: [Strength 8+] Compared to me, everyone is puny.

lines.text: Even the Super Mutants, I imagine. Which is another group that is strong in muscle, meek in mind.

topics.prompt: Raiders talk a good game, but aren't all that dangerous.

lines.text: Well, I wasn't referring to their mouths. Those are quite loud. It's their minds that are meek, submissive, and easily swayed.

topics.prompt: Raiders are anything but meek.

lines.text: Oh but they are. Easily influenced, always submitting to their desires, and they have a conscience that is all but mute.

items.description: A Nuka-Cola company man through and through. Loyal to the end, and beyond.
items.howToObtain: Claim from the Nuka-World Scoreboard (Season 11)

lines.text: Greetings. Remember, don't hesitate to ask me for assistance.
I wish they played more Silver Shroud in Appalachia. Anyway, what's on your mind?
lines.note: Leo sighs before the line. Leo is annoyed that his favorite play does not play in this region. App-uh-latch-uh is the Pronunciation.

lines.text: A pleasure to see you again.
I can't help but wonder- is there any place out there untouched by war?
I tire of people shooting at me. Can't they tell I'm not feral?
lines.note: Leo genuinely sounds annoyed.

lines.text: Always keep a cool head out there. Brawns can get you far, but your brains will keep you 2 steps ahead.
lines.note: Leo lectures the player like a teacher but is not aggressive.

lines.text: Hello there.
You don't think I drink too- ah, never mind. What were you going to say?
lines.note: Leo takes back his question. He was going to ask if he drink's too much.

lines.text: Well, if it isn't my favorite Nuka dealer!
lines.note: Leo chuckles at the end of this line. He is excited to see his friend.

lines.text: Ahh, welcome back. Find any new discoveries, friend?
lines.note: Leo is glad to see his friend again.

lines.text: Hey partner, I just want to let you know I appreciate all you've done for me. But enough with that, let's get to businesses.
lines.note: Leo is grateful to the player, as they are one of Leo�s only friends and they provide him with shelter.

lines.text: You look exhausted. Don't push yourself too hard out there. You only have the one body.
lines.note: Leo is concerned for their new friend.

lines.text: Are you well? Oh, on second thought, those bloodstains don't look yours. How can I help?
lines.note: After confriming the player is okay, Leo's tone shifts from worried to Confident.

lines.text: To think no more Nuka-Cola flavors will be released. What a shame.
lines.note: Leo sounds slightly defeated.

lines.text: Welcome back! I am running low on Nuka-Cola again. if you don't mind.
lines.note: Leo really wants Nuka-Cola but does not want to appear desperate.

lines.text: I heard there was a company out east that refused to join the Nuka-Family. Can you imagine that? There could have been more flavors...
lines.note: Leo Sighs after this line.

topics.prompt: I'm in need of your services.

lines.text: Of course. How can I help?

topics.prompt: Nice Nuka-Cola jacket.

lines.text: Why thank you...I don't tend to receive compliments on my attire. Like myself, it's something of a relic of the past.
lines.note: Leo does not receive many compliments. This makes him feel better about himself.

topics.prompt: Woah! You snuck up on me!

lines.text: Ah, I still forget many Vault Dwellers are not accustomed to speaking to ghouls.
Your reputation proceeds you, Vault Dweller. But I forget my manners. My name is Leo. Leo Petrov. It's a pleasure.
lines.note: Leo sounds friendly but proper.

topics.prompt: Why do you love Nuka-Cola so much?

lines.text: I'm surprised you're asking that. Nuka-Cola is the number one drink of choice across America. It's difficult to find someone who *doesn't* like it.
lines.note: Leo is genuinely surprised you are asking this. It�s like someone is asking why you like sleep to him.

lines.text: Are you not fond of Nuka-Cola?
lines.note: Leo asks this with worry in his voice. He worries you do not like his favorite thing.

topics.prompt: What do you mean by "partnership"?

lines.text: Direct and to the point. Allow me to explain.
Here's my proposition: For the small price of Nuka-Cola beverages, I will offer you extra security here.
But of even more value, I can offer you words of "Nuka-Inspiration" specific to the variety you share.
Think of it as a sort of motivational "pep talk". I am confident it will make your day-to-day survival a bit easier.

topics.prompt: Are you from around here, Leo?

lines.text: No, I'm not. I originally came here on the job. After the bombs, I started wandering around, but I do return to Appalachia from time to time.

topics.prompt: I don't have a Nuka-Cola.

lines.text: What a shame. I was thirsty. Well, I'm sure you're wondering why I am here.

topics.prompt: What's with the Nuka-Cola getup?

lines.text: My get up...? Oh, but of course, you must mean my uniform. You see, I am, or, hmm, rather *was*...an employee of the Nuka-Cola Corporation.
lines.note: Leo sounds confused that his outfit was referred to as a "get up".

lines.text: To be blunt, I believe we can enter a partnership. As a former Security Officer for the Nuka-Cola Corporation, I'm sure you will find me useful.

topics.prompt: Wait, you've heard of me?

lines.text: Are you surprised? Locals tell me you are quite active here in Appalachia. Some even describe you as "exceptionally capable".

topics.prompt: [Perception 4+] I'm guessing you weren't just a security guard?

lines.text: Ah, you are a sharp one, as I expected. Yes, my career was much more.... colorful. Perhaps I'll tell you about it another time over a bottle of Nuka?

topics.prompt: Are you some sort of Nuka-Cola addict?

lines.text: I hope I don't give that impression. I will admit that, like the rest of America, I do consider Nuka-Cola to be the greatest beverage known to man.
I must ask, despite knowing it is strange to do so on a first meeting, but... do you happen to have a Nuka-Cola classic? I have run out.
lines.note: Make sure classic is said.

topics.prompt: Yes I have a Nuka Cola. Here.

lines.text: Much obliged! And I mean much. Walking around sure works up a thirst. But I'm sure you're wondering why I am here.

topics.prompt: Sounds like you were a bad husband.

lines.text: Perhaps, but I provided for my wife. I did not strike or scold my child, I couldn't say the same about my own father... at least there is that.
lines.note: Leo speaks with conviction. He believes he could have been a worse dad.

topics.prompt: [Endurance 8+] The past is in the past. Pick yourself up and carry on.

lines.text: Yes... yes, you are right. I miss them, but it is a new world out there now. I will probably never know their fate... I just hope they didn't suffer.
lines.note: Leo's first "yes" sounds depressed, but his second sounds more hopeful. The player helped Leo to move on a little more.

topics.prompt: I'm sorry. You've been through a lot.

lines.text: I appreciate it. It's difficult to talk about these things, but I'm glad I got that off my chest. Thank you for listening, friend.
lines.note: Leo is genuinely grateful.

topics.prompt: Do you think your family survived?
