lines.text: I... I'm not sure. My company benefits provided me and my family with space in a vault. But that was quite some time before we had parted ways.
lines.note: This topic is difficult for Leo to speak about. He should sound uncomfortable and/or sad.

lines.text: I was far from home when the bombs fell. I'd hoped, of course, that my family made it to a vault. But even if they did, how would I ever know?
lines.note: This topic is difficult for Leo to speak about. He should sound uncomfortable and/or sad.

lines.text: Forgive me, I can't bring myself to talk more about this right now.
lines.note: Leo should sound heartbroken. He does not know what happened to his family. Thinking about it hurts.

topics.prompt: You were married?

lines.text: A handsome devil like me? Of course, I was.
lines.note: Leo is making a self-deprecating joke. It helps him cope with being turned into a ghoul.

lines.text: The last time I spoke with my wife, she told me our marriage was over. "What good is a husband who is never home?" she said.
She told me she was taking our son and leaving for her mother's and accused me of being married to my job. I don't think she was wrong.

topics.prompt: [Charisma 4+] They live in your memory. Save them by surviving yourself.

lines.text: I suppose you're right. I can't change the past, but I can do right by them now by doing good where I can. Like helping you out, huh?
lines.note: Leo sounds more hopeful after talking to the player.

topics.prompt: She sounds like an asshole.

lines.text: No, she wasn't. She was quite lovely and she had good reason to act the way she did.
lines.note: Leo feels as like he needs to defend his wife. He knows he was the bad guy in the marriage.

lines.text: Even before the bombs, I'm not sure I could have ever repaired my relationship with my family, but I wish I had known how little time we had left.
lines.note: Leo sounds heavily regretful at the end.

topics.prompt: Sounds like you have regrets.

lines.text: Regrets? I suppose. But if I am truly honest with myself, were I to do it all again, would I have done anything differently? I sometimes wonder.

topics.prompt: It was a heavily alcoholic drink cooked up by some university students at VTU.

lines.text: University students had their hands on that? Nuka-Cola was, of course, aware of people's fondness for mixing their product with alcohol.
But frankly, this sounds problematic. Not to mention trademark infringement. Back in the day, I would have shut the whole operation down.
Wherever did you discover this? I can't imagine it was easy to find.

topics.prompt: Addiction is a disease and Nuka-Cola infected everyone. It's not your fault.

lines.text: I am very surprised I wasn't aware of this, but at least I know now, thanks to you.
I cannot imagine I could stop myself cold turkey, but perhaps I'll try to reduce my consumption as the years go by.
In the meantime, keep them coming I suppose.
lines.note: Leo *chuckles* after this line.

topics.prompt: I found a speakeasy in Big Al's Tattoo Parlor and a drink testing RoboBrain named "Biv".

lines.text: A speakeasy in a Tattoo Parlor? How curious! And a RoboBrain made for alcohol testing. In some ways, that is ingenious.
Maybe in the future, I'll run into this "Biv". I'm curious what kind of information I could pull from it. But then again, I'm no longer employed.
lines.note: Leo is curious about this alcoholic robot, but he does not have a good reason to look into it.

topics.prompt: Want to hear about how I cured the Scorched Plague with my blood?

lines.text: And this has something to do with Nuka-Cola? A fascinating tale, I'm sure. Do go on.
lines.note: Leo does not quite believe the player.

lines.text: This whole time I was thinking of nothing more than how flavorful our products were. I never seriously considered it... but am I truly an addict?

topics.prompt: It's the ultimate party drink! Really sends for a loop.

lines.text: If I had a bottle cap for every time I've heard that. To be honest, it sounds rather vile. I cannot recommend drinking unlicensed Nuka-Cola products.

topics.prompt: I have the recipe! Do you want it?

lines.text: I am going to pretend you didn't tell me this. I want nothing to do with your unlicensed Nuka-Cola contraband. Nuka-Cola Dark satisfies me just fine.

topics.prompt: The creator was a student named Lewis.

lines.text: Interesting. Never underestimate students. I'm sure this "Lewis" would have been a brilliant chemist at Nuka-Cola had things turned out differently.
Assuming the company didn't bury him in piles and piles of lawsuits, that is.

topics.prompt: There's something else I wanted to talk about.

lines.text: By all means, what's on your mind?

topics.prompt: Who cares if you're addicted to Nuka-Cola? It's not a big deal.

lines.text: Right. Right! I mean, it is just soft drinks at the end of the day. And who knows? As a ghoul, these chemicals may not even affect me!

topics.prompt: I think this explains your Nuka-Cola addiction.

lines.text: Preposterous. These experiments happened just before the bombs fell, did they not? I don't believe those chemicals ever hit the mass market.

topics.prompt: Don't worry. Probably just a few rogue employees, right?

lines.text: I love the company with all my heart, but I know it's had its fair share of corruption. I accepted that, but this... This is inhumane.

topics.prompt: That's a little anticlimactic. You could have just solved all this yourself.

lines.text: Perhaps. I would argue I didn't want to solve the case that badly. Maybe you were meant to solve this case all along?
I honestly could not have done this without you, friend. Having a cold case over me had really dampened my spirits.
This case wouldn't have been anything out of the ordinary if the world didn't end, but the fact is, you solved a mystery I was unable to.
For what it's worth, you would have been a great Nuka-Cola security officer. Solving crimes and helping people, well, it suits you.
In any case, I believe this information wraps up that particular mystery. At, least as far as I am concerned.

topics.prompt: You didn't buy that locker yourself, did you? Seems like something a Nuka-nerd would do.

lines.text: That's a good one! If only there was such a Nuka-Twist to this plot. I truly thank you for the laugh and providing me closure.
lines.note: Leo starts this line in a Light chuckle that turn into hysterical laughter at how preposterous the joke is.

topics.prompt: I used the Kanawha Nuka-Cola plant to manufacture a vaccine.

lines.text: Well that certainly would not fall within Nuka-Cola's safety standards, but I must admit it is an ingenious way to mass produce a vaccine.

topics.prompt: I made my own Nuka-Cola product. With my blood!

lines.text: Disgusting. I feel like I know you well enough to judge that you are not a complete psychopath. Can I assume you had a good reason for this act?

topics.prompt: It was the best way to get the vaccine out to survivors.

lines.text: Very impressive. Using Nuka-Cola facilities to manufacture and distribute a vaccine shows incredible ingenuity and resourcefulness.
Still, under different circumstances, I don't believe your "product" would have proven very successful in focus testing.

topics.prompt: I guess so. I was mostly just following directions.

lines.text: Well, while I can't approve of the *contamination* I do appreciate it was for a noble cause. The Scorched are truly a blight.
If this vaccine of yours works, it will save many lives.

topics.prompt: So that's it? Case closed?

lines.text: Yes. In this world, I would guess that is as close to the truth as we can get.

topics.prompt: Have you ever heard of Nukashine?

lines.text: Nukashine? That's certainly not an official Nuka-Cola product. What is it? Some sort of local cocktail?

topics.prompt: I found a bunker with plans for Nuka-Cola Quantum power armor paint.

lines.text: Really? A part of my investigation was to track down those plans. They were exclusive and meant to be used for upcoming Nuka-Cola events.
Just how did you gain access to this... locker?

topics.prompt: Actually, never mind.

lines.text: Sure.

topics.prompt: I found a secret bunker full of Nuka-Cola collector items.

lines.text: Fascinating! I had heard the company had a storage facility in the area. What a find! Perhaps I'll visit it sometime.

topics.prompt: I found evidence that Nuka-Cola was using chemicals to make their drinks addictive.

lines.text: Are you positive? This appears to be official, but I assure you I had no idea. I wonder if this was entirely local to the Kanawha plant?

topics.prompt: You had kids?

lines.text: Just the one. Roman. He was 10 years old when the bombs fell. He was a sweet boy but he was already becoming *angsty* as he approached his teens.
lines.note: Talking about his kid is difficult. But Leo finds comfort in remembering his son.

lines.text: The last time I was home I brought him a gift... My wife told me he wanted a leather jacket and a tin of pomade.
lines.note: Talking about his kid is difficult. But Leo finds comfort in remembering his son.

lines.text: I suppose I should have been concerned with his "greaser" obsession, but it's an old cliche that guilty fathers try to buy their children's love.
lines.note: Talking about his kid is difficult. But Leo finds comfort in remembering his son.

topics.prompt: Let's talk about something else.

lines.text: Of course.

topics.prompt: Can I ask about your family?

lines.text: I find it difficult to speak of them, but talking is supposed to help the mind heal. Maybe this is something an old ghoul needs to get off his chest.
What would you like to know?
No offense, but I believe it's best to keep personal matters separated from business. I hope you understand, partner.
lines.note: Leo is guarded about his family at this point. The player is still a new acquaintance.

topics.prompt: Where did you live before the bombs?

lines.text: I used to have a house in the capital. Must be long gone now. To be honest, I spent little time there.
lines.note: Leo is almost nostalgic about his old life.

lines.text: I'm sure it comes as no surprise to hear Nuka-Cola had enemies. It was my job to shut down internal leaks, catch corporate spies, etcetera.
I went where I was needed, inspecting factories and offices across the country. I practically lived on the road, and that left little personal time.

topics.prompt: I'm a fan, but you seem almost like an addict.

lines.text: No, I am not addicted. I'm no more an addict than the people who enjoyed a cup of coffee in the morning. It's just how I prefer to get my caffeine.
I try to restrict myself to only one a day, but then I do occasionally spoil myself from time to time.

topics.prompt: Can you tell me about your job at Nuka-Cola?

lines.text: Well that is a rather large topic. What would you like to know?

topics.prompt: You're right. You should give up.

lines.text: I am way ahead of you there, partner. I'm no longer an employee. There is no salary to be paid, nor benefits to collect. There is nothing to gain.
lines.note: Leo is pretending to not care and is also trying to convince the player that they do not care.

topics.prompt: You could still solve it!

lines.text: No, I don't think I will be doing that. What's to gain but peace of mind? I think I would much rather have half a crate of Nuka-Cherry.
lines.note: Leo is trying to convince himself that he does not care about his cold case.

topics.prompt: The Kanawha Nuka-Cola Factory?

lines.text: Indeed. Reports indicated suspicious patterns within Kanawha. I had barely arrived, and before I could conduct my investigation, the war began.
The trail went cold, buried in the rubble of the old world. That factory is very dangerous now. I recommend you steer clear.

topics.prompt: You never solved the case?

lines.text: No, I did not. The Great War destroyed my company, the face my mother gave me, and likely all the evidence needed to crack that case.
lines.note: Leo sounds disappointed in himself.

lines.text: So I say to hell with it! I've tried to put it from my mind, but even still... a mystery is a mystery.

topics.prompt: if I find something related to the case I'll bring it to you.

lines.text: I admire your drive, but I don't expect you'll find much, unfortunately. It's been too long and too much has been destroyed. I also won't stop you.
lines.note: Leo is somber. This case is almost hopeless.

lines.text: I must admit I would be interested in hearing about anything you find.

topics.prompt: Why would someone steal from their own company?

lines.text: Uncertain. It could be for any number of reasons. Many employees feel they are treated unfairly and start scheming to steal from their employer.
Half the time, it's simple greed. As for the other half... well, they should have found a better way.

topics.prompt: I can see that! Nuka-merch is so much fun!

lines.text: Yes! Incredible efforts were made to create a wonderful place for people to enjoy. You should have seen Nuka World in its prime!
lines.note: Leo is passionate and proud about this topic.

lines.text: On a hot summer day in the park, even the most hardened bruiser couldn't help but smile.

topics.prompt: I've never thought of it that way before.

lines.text: Nor did I at first. Sometimes it takes a quiet sit on a park bench with a cold Nuka Dark in your hand to put things into perspective.
lines.note: this topic has Leo in a reflective mood.

topics.prompt: I'm pretty sure Nuka-Cola only cared about the money.

lines.text: Well, any corporation will have corruption, but that does not paint the entire picture, nor does it reflect all the employees and their efforts.
Marketing may have focused on money, but what of the Nuka-World ride designers' passion to create pleasant experiences for the whole family?

topics.prompt: Tell me about the last case you were investigating.

lines.text: I can't divulge that. Ah, what am I saying... Sometimes I forget I'm no longer employed. Old habits die hard, I suppose.
lines.note: Leo has a habit of telling people he cant talk about his work. But he no longer works for Nuka-Cola so he is free to talk.

lines.text: I was here to investigate a large amount of funds that went missing through the Kanawha Plant here in Appalachia. Embezzlement was highly suspected.
It's not really something worth discussing. The trail went cold. I can't lie, I still think about it, but... never mind that. Let's carry on.

topics.prompt: Was Nuka-Cola a good company to work for?

lines.text: I must admit I rather enjoyed my work. My time at the company raised my appreciation of the brand and I realized something.
Nuka-Cola created more than drinks. We offered an escape from the looming threat of war and happiness to millions of children and adults alike.
Remembering the smiles... I know, despite our mistakes, we did some good in the end.
lines.note: This fact relieved Leo in the past. His company was corrupted, but he is proud of the good that was done.

lines.text: I suppose none of it matters now. After the bombs fell, my job ceased to exist. I tried to find my way home, but... let's speak of something else.
lines.note: This topic is hard for Leo. He does not want to share too much information and wants to change the subject.

topics.prompt: So you just travel around like a rogue investigator?

lines.text: Well, after the war, sure. My son used to believe I was something like that. But originally, I came here on an investigation Nuka-Cola assigned to me.

topics.prompt: On the job meaning Nuka-Cola business?

lines.text: Yes, I originally came here on a case.

topics.prompt: Nuka-Cola is liquid garbage.

lines.text: Garbage?! I'm... I'm shocked! Despite all our flavors? Nuka-Cherry? Nuka-Grape? Nuka-Cola Orange? Not even the Classic? Unbelievable!
lines.note: Leo sounds almost insulted. He took this personally but is trying not to show it.

lines.text: There are seventeen plus flavors. A flavor for everyone. I implore you, find yours...
lines.note: Leo is almost lecturing you about this.

topics.prompt: It's too unhealthy. I prefer water.

lines.text: Of course I've heard the concerns before, but I assure you they are fully unfounded.
lines.note: Leo is trying to reassure the player.

lines.text: No research or testing has ever found any conclusive evidence of any health risk. Nuka-Cola is safe for everyone to enjoy!
lines.note: Leo is trying to reassure the player.

topics.prompt: I love Nuka-Cola!

lines.text: Ha, I knew my intuition was right! My gut told me you could be trusted, and perhaps this is why. We just may be kindred spirits, you and I.
lines.note: Leo is happy he found a fellow Nuka-Cola fan. He chuckles after this line.

lines.text: Cheers to you, friend.

topics.prompt: Actually, I don't have any Nuka-Cola for you.

lines.text: Oh, that's quite a shame. Please do bring me some if you find any.

topics.prompt: Nukashine.

lines.text: Dear heavens! An unlicensed Nuka-Cola product? Give it here and I shall *dispose* of it at an appropriate time... Good god, that smell.
lines.note: Leo wants to act like he does not want this but secretly he does. Leo *Whispers* the "Good god, that smell." line

topics.prompt: Nuka-Twist.

lines.text: Turn your luck around and get blissed with Nuka-Twist! Ah, this was my son's favorite.

topics.prompt: Nuka-Cola Cranberry.

lines.text: Nuka Cranberry. "Made with 100% Appalachian cranberries, its light, and refreshing taste transforms how you experience life!

topics.prompt: Nuka-Grape.

lines.text: An underrated classic, if I do say so myself. "Let Nuka-Grape conquer your thirst, so *you* can focus on the action"!

topics.prompt: Nuka-Cherry.

lines.text: Nuka-Cherry! "Is daily life mundane and hard to endure? Don't fret! There is a cure! Nuka-Cherry is here to add some flavor to the day!

topics.prompt: Nuka-Cola Dark.

lines.text: I'm sure it's 5 o'clock somewhere. "Unwind with Nuka-Cola Dark. Have a glass and let the fun sneak up on you.

topics.prompt: Nuka-Orange.

lines.text: Nuka-Nuka-Cola Orange! Orange is the new...hmm? Uh, for when the heat is too much! I actually don't quite remember that one too well...
lines.note: Leo is trying to remember an old jingle for Nuka Orange but can't really remember it and is stumbling/muttering through it.

topics.prompt: Nuka-Cola Quantum.

lines.text: Take a leap... Enjoy a Quantum! There aren't many perks to being a ghoul, but drinking Quantum without worrying about side-effects is one of them.
I do wish it didn't make my urine glow, however.

topics.prompt: Nuka-Cola Wild.

lines.text: Give me a Nuka-Cola Wild any day. Never mind those cheap competitor drinks!

topics.prompt: A classic Nuka-Cola.

lines.text: The All-American Classic. "Share a Nuka-Cola with both new friends and old! Nuke your thirst"!

topics.prompt: That's all I needed.

lines.text: Of course. Don't hesitate to reach out if you need me again.

topics.prompt: I have a Nuka-Cola for you, Leo.

lines.text: My thanks, but I am still quenched from the last drink. Hold on to that bottle though. I am sure I will feel thirsty again soon.
Excellent! What did you bring me?
Thank heavens! I was feeling quite parched. What flavor do you have?
You do?! Pardon my, uh... enthusiasm. I am *not* addicted. What did you bring?
lines.note: Leo *clears his throat befoe pardon. Leo mutters before saying "I am *not* addicted.

topics.prompt: You mentioned you needed Nuka-Cola?

lines.text: I did indeed! I very much enjoy every Nuka-flavor and find each one uniquely inspiring.
For every Nuka-Cola drink you share with me, I will share that inspiration with you.
I realize that this sounds like fiction, but I can assure you, you will feel that "extra pep in your step!" Now then, let's see what you have.

topics.prompt: Let's see what you've got to trade.

lines.text: Certainly. Have a gander.
You're interested in what I have? Well here, here... let me show you.
It pains me to depart with some of these. But caps are caps.
Ah, I knew you couldn't stay away from my premium Nuka products.
Ah-ha! My favorite customer returns!
lines.note: Leo is happy to see his good friend again.

topics.prompt: I discovered something related to Nuka-Cola.

lines.text: My favorite topic. What's on your mind?

topics.prompt: Mind if I ask you some questions about yourself?

lines.text: I suppose you should get to know me if we're to be sharing a space together.
Perfect! Now if you excuse me, I'm parched. I'm going to see if I can dig up a Nuka-Cola somewhere.
Much obliged Vault Dweller. I'll have your back as long as I'm here.
Believe me, nothing malicious will happen on my account. I look forward to our future together.
Intriguing. TNT Dome #3 was the only Locker that belonged to Nuka-Cola as far as I knew.
I suspect an employee embezzled funds to purchase this locker and then used it to hide valuable and confidential items. In fact, I'm almost certain.
Am I to understand this contains your blood? Well, I hope it's mere trace amounts. Despite appearances, I'm a ghoul, not a vampire.
Sure.
lines.note: This did not make into the VO cut off.

topics.prompt: I had something else I wanted to talk about.

lines.text: Ask away! I'll do my best to have answers.

topics.prompt: See you around, Leo.

lines.text: I'm sure you will.
Don't look so gloomy friend, at least you don't look like a prune.
Don't you find it amusing how Nuka-Cola bottle caps are now used as currency? I never would have guessed it.
What is with your colleagues from the Vault? I saw one hopping around in a barbarian outfit of sorts? Strange... Amusing, but strange.
Close any cases lately?
I shouldn't have stayed up all night listening to radio plays...
lines.note: Leo Yawns before this line.

lines.text: Anything a tired old Ghoul can do for you?
Good to see you well.
Roman...I should have taken more vacation days...
lines.note: Leo feels regretful.

lines.text: I should really drink water...
Where the river's made of Quantum, hmmm-hmm -hmmhmm hmmm...
lines.note: Leo is humming a line of the Nuka-World song. Go to 9 secconds on https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7cHLPsEcWWA&ab_channel=CopilotMusic%2BSound-Topic

lines.text: I wonder if they made it into the Vault...
lines.note: Leo is reminiscing about his family. He hopes they made it safely into the Vault.

lines.text: I'm surprised how prejudiced people have become towards me since I turned into a ghoul. Definitely, a new experience that grants you perspective.
lines.note: Leo is reflecting on how becoming a ghoul helped him understand the troubles of being discriminated against.

lines.text: Brotherhood of Steel...Such odd sorts. How can you change anything if you are only focused on preserving a past that lead us to all of this?
lines.note: Leo is unimpressed with the Brotherhood of Steel and believes they could put their efforts to better use.

lines.text: Those Raiders are foul folk, but you cant help to admire how free they look.
In another life, I may have taken up photography... I don't believe people would take kindly to a ghoul snapping shots of them, however.
lines.note: Leo chuckles after the line.

lines.text: Have you ever been to Nuka-World? It was quite wonderful back in the day. I'm sure some ruffians have made it their home by now.
Bottle always rubbed me the wrong way... Not Cappy, though. He gives off a good impression but Bottle... Hmm, I don't know about that one.
lines.note: Leo is a little too suspicious of a Nuka-Cola mascot.

lines.text: My face may scare children away, but at least I don't have to use Rad-X anymore.
lines.note: Leo almost finds this fact funny.

lines.text: Nuka-Cola Quantum, what a drink! Twice the calories, twice the carbohydrates, twice the caffeine, and twice the taste!
lines.note: Leo is passionate about Nuka-Cola Quantum.

lines.text: It's a shame the Tunnel of Love wasn't open when I visited Nuka-World On Tour. Although I suppose I didn't have someone to bring anyways.
lines.note: Leo is heartbroken as he remembers he does not know if his wife is alive.

lines.text: The new people who run Nuka-World on Tour certainly got the spirit of Nuka-Cola nailed down.

topics.prompt: Did you hear that Nuka-World On Tour is here?

lines.text: Yes, I visited it before coming here. It was a splendid time, despite it not being an official event, that is.

topics.prompt: Get lost. I don't have caps for you.

lines.text: What? Do you think I'm a beggar? I was just here to greet you. Though I wouldn't turn down an ice-cold Nuka-Cola...
lines.note: Leo is confused on why he got mistaken for a beggar. He does want a Nuka-Cola as he is thirsty and it is his favorite.

topics.prompt: Nice to meet you, Leo.

lines.text: A pleasure to make your acquaintance. I must admit, it surprised me that you did not shoot this ghoul at first sight. Anyway...

topics.prompt: Let's change the topic.

lines.text: Sure.
lines.note: This did not make into the VO cut off.
