lines.text: You here for a tune-up, or just some friendly banter?
I used to eat a lot of Fancy Lads Snack Cakes. I thought it's what the celebrities ate. I was a pretty dumb kid.
lines.note: Self-deprecating, so light-hearted when calling himself "dumb

lines.text: I'm used to playing in front of petrified corpses. They're a pretty tough crowd.
How's it going boss? Hope you didn't pick up any new scars on the way home. Gotta protect that moneymaker.
I'm working on a new song, about an ex-girlfriend. It's part romance, part cautionary tale.
You know what I miss? Fresh laundry. Like, if I had a choice between a million caps and a pair of warm socks?
Well, I'd take the caps, but my cold ass feet would hate the decision.
To survive, you gotta do a lot of weird shit.
This one time, I had to eat an entire closet full of Cram, because all the regular food went bad and there was just nothing else.
I'm not sure I ever got that taste out of my mouth. I'm basically more Cram than human at this point.
I'd like to try fixing a car once. But I guess I'd need to fix the roads first.
Might be easier just to make a sled pulled by molerats.
I just had an idea. What if we had every door in your camp tied to a piano?
Then you could unlock them all with the uh ahem, right key?
lines.note: You realize the joke is terrible but you're trying to sell it anyway

lines.text: I'm a jack of trades with instruments too. Pianos, drums, banjos, I can play pretty much anything.
I once met a guy who was starting his own rock band. Had a voice like nails on a chalkboard, but he had the right look.
Sometimes that matters more.
lines.note: Pensive, as he's referring to his own lack of a rock star look

lines.text: I can fix just about anything. Well, other than a broken heart.
Unless that heart is in a robot. Then, maybe? Depends on the robot.
lines.note: Pensive, as he's referring to his own lack of a rock star look

lines.text: I've thought about it, and maybe I will learn how to fix a hair dryer. Might be useful next time you decide who you want to keep around.
Still working on that spaceship, boss. It's uh ... it's coming along. Might be ready for you sometime next millennium.
I was thinking about what you said, about how I'm good at adapting.
I may not be great at any one thing, but maybe being flexibile is its own kind of mastery.
I was thinking about what you said, about how lucky I am to be alive. And you're not wrong. But you're not entirely right. I put in work too.
Hey, my name's Sam. If you're looking for help on your settlement, I'm your guy.
Trying to stay agile here, boss. Mentally and physically, like you said. Got my head on a swivel.
Hey, I just got an idea! Protectrons with swiveling heads! Works for cameras, anyway.

topics.prompt: You're right. There's only room for one master here.

lines.text: And I won't forget it. Unless you get eaten by a yao guai or something.
At which point, it's probably fair to call the yao guai "master" instead. Rules are rules.

topics.prompt: Sounds good. Can you fix my gear?

lines.text: I think so! It's been a while, but you know what they say, it's just like riding a bike.
Just ignore the fact that I've never actually ridden one.
Metaphorically, I've done it a thousand times.

topics.prompt: I'm not entirely sure I need someone.

lines.text: But you haven't even heard my pitch? Crap, it's the eyebrows, isn't it.
lines.note: Sam has thick brows that make him look a bit angry, but in reality he's a bit of goof. Still, he thinks it's a feature.

lines.text: I've been told they're too intimidating. But I feel like they're important for my branding.

topics.prompt: [Low Intelligence] That's great. I'm not the brightest bulb in the ... place bulbs go.

lines.text: The shed! Bright bulbs go in the shed.
lines.note: Being helpful

lines.text: See? We're already complementing each other and finishing each other's sandwiches and everything!

topics.prompt: [Intelligence 8+] I'm already pretty good at fixing stuff.

lines.text: But do you know what you're not good at? Being at two places at once.
lines.note: Being helpful, not criticizing

lines.text: And that's where I come in. Hopefully.

topics.prompt: So you're a sycophant. Great.

lines.text: I don't know what that means, but it sounds like an elephant, and those are great!
But yeah, if you don't have a specific job for me, I can just work on repairing stuff at my shop here.
Maybe even compose a few tunes while I work.

topics.prompt: That didn't answer my question.

lines.text: Really? Sorry about that. I sometimes tend to talk in circles.
But you know what that makes me? A revolutionary! Get it? Because I talk in uh ... yeah, never mind.

topics.prompt: Never mind what you can do. What do you want to do?

lines.text: I'd love to just sit back and compose music. And I've heard it's best to do what you love.
Well, provided what you love isn't cracking your knuckles.
Something about that sound just ... (shudder).

topics.prompt: I could use a helping hand.

lines.text: And I've got two of them! Helping hands, helping feet, helping ... ears.
For, uh, you know, when you need a good listener! I've got everything you need.

topics.prompt: What do you do exactly?

lines.text: I'm a jack of all trades. And I know what you're thinking, that also means I'm a master of none.
lines.note: Trying to convince the Player but also fearful/nervous he'll get shot down.

lines.text: But what do you want a master for, anyway?
A person like that probably has a huge ego and spends all day letting everyone know about it.
Whereas me, I'm not just low maintenance. I am no maintenance. You won't even know I'm here.
Point is, I can help fix things, play things, and even tell a bad joke. You already know that much!

topics.prompt: I'm sorry, but who are you and how did you get past security?

lines.text: I'm Sam. And I kind of just walked in?
Although I guess "wandered in aimlessly while sweating buckets" is a more accurate answer.

topics.prompt: The more the merrier.

lines.text: And you can't go wrong with being merry. At least merry with an "e".
Getting married is another story. You kind of go wrong half the time. Statistically speaking.
Any other places catch your eye?
Anyways, I appreciate the story. Next time I play a song, I'm going to think twice about who's listening.

topics.prompt: Beats me. I just saw people partying, making music, and joined in.

lines.text: That's what I like about you. You're always diving in headfirst, like a bull in a china shop.
And that means a lot of broken shit you're gonna need me to fix.

topics.prompt: The Nightstalker is like any old person. They just want you noisy kids to be quiet and stay off their lawn.

lines.text: Ha, to be fair, that thing is probably really, really old.
Who knows how many gripes, and lawns, it's collected over the years.

topics.prompt: You didn't know? The Nightstalker is an Appalachian music critic. So be careful where you play.

lines.text: You're right. To be honest, these days I don't play for an audience.
But I don't think the Sons of Dane were either. Out here, sound travels.

topics.prompt: Apparently, constant partying from the Sons of Dane drove it insane.

lines.text: Damn, must have been one hell of a party. Or parties, plural. Or maybe it was just one party that never ended.
To be fair, I think that'd drive me nuts too.
Either way, there's one thing about it I don't get.
Why play music? Why did that draw it out?

topics.prompt: It was no big deal.

lines.text: Yeah, you're pretty good in a fight.
Now if it was an argument? My money's on the Nightstalker.
Yeah, you're pretty good in a fight.
Doesn't matter if it's a nightstalker or an argument, my money's on you to win.

topics.prompt: You wouldn't say that if you saw this thing. It was terrifying.

lines.text: Still, you conquered your fears and kicked its ass. Which is pretty cool.
That's one thing you can't do with a heckler. They're a paying customer after all.

topics.prompt: I'm sorry you had to go through that. Were you heckled often?

lines.text: Well, the funny thing is, it's usually before I start playing.
After? It kind of blows their mind that good music can come out of this body.
So it's pretty fun to shut people up that way.

topics.prompt: That's because you're soft.

lines.text: Wait, do we mean physically or emotionally? I've put on a few pounds, so I guess both.
But hey, I'm taking it in stride, aren't I?
You know what they say, Nightstalkers and deathclaws may break your bones, but hecklers can never hurt you.

topics.prompt: Not true. The Nightstalker I encountered said many hurtful things.

lines.text: Wait, they can talk? I thought creatures like that just growled.
Now I feel really bad for you. Hopefully you kicked its ass though.

topics.prompt: That's all.

lines.text: Nice! Photos are always a fun complement to a story.
Not that you can't paint a picture with words, but it's nice sometimes to let an actual picture do the work.

topics.prompt: Forget the camera, what the hell happened with the Floater?

lines.text: Oh, it wasn't that interesting of a story. It was a dead floater someone else killed.
Whoever killed it didn't have use for the crystal, or the pus. I did.

topics.prompt: Nothing that I bothered to remember.

lines.text: Well, that's what cameras are for right?
You take a picture, and it serves as a backup memory. Isn't technology great?

topics.prompt: The Harpers Ferry Armory courtyard.

lines.text: A lot of history in that place, from what I've heard. When you got to fight the power, it helps to have guns.
Oh, I've been there. Personally, I'd rather go to the waffle house on the other end of the building.
Because if I have the choice between a "House of Scares" and a "House of Waffles," I'm choosing the waffles, every time.
Even if they haven't served any in ages.
Oh yeah? That's kind of weird thing to put on your bucket list, if you ask me.
But that might be the artist in me talking. We don't usually write songs about monuments to capitalism.
In the Savage Divide, right? Oh man, when I heard about it, I thought the house was like, a giant pumpkin.
Nope, turns out it's an ordinary house. A lot of pumpkins around it though.
Oh yeah, wilderness hikes are always a good way to relax.
I'd like to rent a cabin one day, and finish a whole record. Sigh, someday.
lines.note: Wistful, imagining it in his head.

lines.text: Ha, no bigger trap for tourists and teenagers than a Pre-War shopping center.
Why visit a historic landmark when you can browse the Men's Wear section at Big Steve's Sporting Goods?
No, I'm kidding. I love malls. It's like a junkyard, with more organization.
Castles are always fun. In another life, maybe I'd be a bard.

topics.prompt: [One Violent Night] I formed a band to draw out the Nightstalker.

lines.text: Oh my god, I heard about that! That was you?

topics.prompt: [Bucket List] I fixed up a ProSnap Camera and helped finish a tourist's bucket list.

lines.text: Oh shit, I love that camera! Funny story, I once made a night vision lens out of crystal I got from a Floater Freezer's pus sac.
I didn't have much use for the pus though.
Anyways, that took a weird detour. What pictures did you take with that camera? Anything interesting?

topics.prompt: [Agility +8] I've learned it's helpful to be agile, both mentally and physically.

lines.text: Yeah, I like to think I've got the mental part down. The physical? I'm working on it.
Although endurance is probably more helpful when you're fixing pipes and not, dodging bullets.

topics.prompt: It's a miracle you're still alive. Formal training is important.

lines.text: Well, then I guess I'm just lucky. But better lucky than dead, right?

topics.prompt: That kind of adaptability is good. You'll do well in the Wasteland.

topics.prompt: Why did you come to Appalachia?

lines.text: My Ma and I used to move around a lot. We never had a place we called home.

Well, let's see... how do you feel about giant mutant ants? Sound dangerous enough?
Those big, disgusting Rad Ants, for one thing. There's said to be a bunch of them out that way.
That place is a rat's nest for sure. And I don't just mean regular rats, I mean Rad Rats.
Rad Rat meat has never been my taste, but some people like it, and those who do often go there to hunt for the little scamps.
There was some chatter about a Rad Rat infestation in that area. Nasty things, those.
One Radroach is disgusting, so how do I even start to describe a whole bunch of them? A nightmare, that's how.
I can't believe some people actually eat Radroach meat, but if you're one of those, you can find a bunch of them where you're headed.
That whole place crawls. Radroaches all over, from what I've heard.
Definitely. There are reports of multiple Radscorpions in the area, and if you ask me, just one of those is dangerous enough. Be careful.
I was talking to another scavenger who was checking out that area. She said that she spotted a couple of Radscorpions and decided to move on.
There are some who call that area the Radscorpion death zone, which is why I try to avoid the place.
Apparently, it's become a Raider hangout. I doubt they'll be happy to see you.
Rumor has it that some particularly violent and dangerous Raiders have moved in. Don't expect a warm welcome.
I overheard some Raiders talking to each other on the radio about that area, and how some of them had claimed it as their turf.
Not sure how accurate the rumor is, but I did hear that some Radtoads have laid claim to the place as a spawning ground.
The last scavenger I talked to who'd been in that area said she saw a bunch of Radtoad eggs. Drawn your own conclusions.
I'm not sure if they're still there, but there were sightings of multiple Radtoads in the vicinity not that long ago.
Only some lethal mechanical killing machines with organic brains. Other than that, nothing dangerous at all.
Dangerous and disturbing, yeah. You know those robots with actual organic brains on top? Robobrains? There are a few of them patrolling that area.
Multiple Robobrains were seen there just a few days ago. They're attacking everything they come across.
A passing trader did mention that he had to run when some robots started shooting at him. They were too far off to tell what kind, though.
I knew a guy named Pete who was looking for some scrap out there. The last anyone heard from him was a frantic radio message about robots.
I hope you can avenge him by dismantling whatever probably killed Pete.
There was a vague mention on the radio a few days ago about robots taking over that area. Didn't say what kind of robots, though.
Got a tip that some military-spec robots are up to something out there.
Judging by the mechanical sounds, gunfire and laser blasts described to me by another scavenger, I'd guess some military robots are out there.
Robots. But not just any robots. The worst ones. Military spec. Not sure what type or how many, but the info comes from a reliable source.
You know that awful disease the Scorchbeasts spread? Word is, it's affected a bunch of stuff in that area.
In a word, yes, and that word is Scorched
There's a lot of Scorched out there, if the rumors are to be believed.
Sentry Bots were seen roaming around in that area. If I were you, I'd avoid them. No need to tangle with that kind of firepower.
One of my scavenger buddies was checking out that area when some Sentry Bots rolled in.
Poor guy spent ten long hours in hiding before there was finally an opening to get away.
Oh, definitely. If you were to ask me what the deadliest kind of robot is, I'd say Sentry Bots. Care to guess what's patrolling that area right now?
I did hear something, but I'm not sure it's reliable. A trader on the radio was going on and on about seeing Sheepsquatches there.
I'm not sure he was all there. He sounded a little off-kilter, if you know what I mean.
Weird story about that. One of my old scavenger friends was out there and said she saw hoof prints like a sheep, but much bigger.
She was convinced it was the Sheepsquatch, but the tracks were confusing, like maybe there was more than one of them. Creepy.
There was a guy on the radio saying he'd been in that area recently and found clues that suggests the presence of a Sheepsquatch.
It might even have been more than one, but he never actually laid eyes on any. He got out of there pretty quick once he realized what he was seeing.
Some of those nasty Snallygasters are out there, based on word going around among the other scavengers.
There's been chatter on the airwaves about a trader who had a run-in with a Snallygaster. Then another one showed up. She got away, thankfully.
As a matter of fact, there have been multiple Snallygasters seen at that location. Those things are about as foul as any creature in Appalachia.
Stingwings are nesting in that area. You'll know them by the loud buzzing sound.
A scavenger I know was chased from that area by a pack of Stingwings. Keep your eyes open, those things come at you quick.
Those flying terrors called Stingwings are known to aggressively guard their territory out there.
Without a doubt. Super Mutants have staked out that area as their own, and they're not looking to take prisoners, if you know what I mean.
Last I heard, the place was being used by a group of Super Mutants as a base or camp or whatever.
I know another scavenger who was all set to go looking for spoils out there when he heard Super Mutants talking close by. He got out quick.
I was having some drinks with a couple of fellow scavengers, and they told me that place was now home to some swamp creatures.
I heard that area has become overridden with swamp creatures.
Someone on the radio was saying that area is full of swamp creatures, so stay alert.
It's a nest of damn ticks. They'll bleed you dry if you let them.
Oh yeah, that place is crawling with ticks. I hate those things. Burn 'em all with fire, I say.
Depends on whether you consider oversized ticks to be dangerous, I guess.
I heard a pretty gruesome story about a scavenger who got mauled by dogs out there.
It's pretty sad, actually. He had a pet dog that died not long ago, so when he saw these wild dogs, he tried to befriend them.
When he tried to offer them food, well... he ended up as the food.
Yeah, there's apparently a pack of wild dogs preying on other creatures that enter that area, including people. Man's best friend, my ass.
I met with an old friend who was out there recently, and he saw a pack of wild dogs take on a Yao Guai. The dogs won, so they're probably still there.
Hell yeah there is. A pack of Wendigos is on a blood hunt in that area. Might be better to just avoid them, if you can.
Absolutely. There are Wendigos. Several of them, by the sound of it. That's a whole lot of sharp teeth and claws coming at you if you're spotted.
Most of us scavengers know to stay far away from that place. The Wendigos who stalk that area aren't exactly what I'd call hospitable.
Rumor has it a big pack of wolves has marked out that place for a hunting ground.
Lately there's been this eerie howling sound coming from there, mostly at night. It's safe to assume that wolves have moved into the area.
I don't think... oh, wait. I just remembered hearing about a pack of wolves that was seen out that way. Might be led by a big alpha, I'm not sure.
What do you call it when there's more than one Yao Guai? A pack? A den? Anyway, whatever it's called, that's what out there.
I'm afraid so. Some hungry Yao Guai have decided to get together out there and hunt pretty much everything that moves.
I've seen pictures in books of what Grizzly bears look like, and they're pretty scary.
With that being said, I still don't think they're as scary as Yao Guai, several of which are known to be hunting in that area.
All I know is that some kind of trouble's waiting for you out there. But isn't it always?
I tried to find out, but nobody seemed to know anything other than people try to avoid that place.
I know a trader who said he lost a friend there to some kind of creature, but he didn't want to talk about it. Guess he's still hurting.
Some of those floating gas bag creatures were spotted in the area. Best to bring a long-range weapon.
You know those disgusting floating jellyfish creatures? The ones that explode? Rumor has it some of those were spotted out that way.
Well, I did heard word that some Floaters were seen out in that area. Those things are revolting.
Just some of those Foundation settlers. I wouldn't call them dangerous, unless you've made an enemy of them.
Heard there were some Foundation folk in that area. Are they dangerous? I guess that depends on you.
There was a group of settlers out there the other day. Might still be around.

topics.prompt: Where am I going?

lines.text: A cabin was mentioned. I usually prefer to look in the big towns for salvage, so I rarely bother with isolated small buildings like that.
There was mention of a cabin, I know that much.
Sounded like it was in, or maybe near, a cabin.
You're looking for a camp, probably not very big.
It's a camp, so keep your eyes open. Those can be hard to spot in the wilds.
The info suggests that the location is a camp, but I'm not sure how old.
As luck would have it, you're heading for a cave. I'm glad it you that's going and not me.
The details included something about a cave. That's not the kind of place a scavenger pokes their nose into, so I couldn't say much more than that.
The area that was described to me has a cave nearby, so I'm guessing that's where you'll want to start.
It was pretty brief, but I did hear something about a building. Not sure whether it's in a town or off by itself.
I didn't come away with a real clear sense of that, other than something about a building being involved.
Inside of some kind of building. At least I think that's what it was. I didn't catch what kind of building, though.
It's an old communications building. Not a bad place for salvage.
A communications building, or least I assume that's what it was. I've searched through it for components a while back.
It's a building with some old machines inside. I think it was used for communications. Radio, maybe?
The person I heard from wasn't sure what kind of place it was, but I knew right away when they described it. It's a military compound.
I'm going to assume that weapons and ammo are of interest to you, so you'll be pleased to learn that the location is a military compound.
Where is it? A scavenger's paradise, my friend. An old military compound. You can find some real good stuff in there, oh yes.
Funny story, that. When my buddy said "dam", I thought he was swearing. Then it finally dawned on me he meant a dam to block water.
You're looking for a dam as your point of reference. Should be somewhere near that.
Definitely near a dam. Whether it's in, on or next to the dam, I don't know. Just look for the dam and start your search there.
You'll love this. Apparently the location is an old factory. For a scavenger, that's like Christmas.
It's one of those old factories that used to make who-knows-what before the war. Maybe you can figure that out while you're there.
You, my friend, are in for a treat. You know those old factories that used to mass-produce stuff before the war? It's one of those.
You can find so much good salvage in places like that, I get excited just thinking about it.
There's chatter among the other scavengers about a farm with something interesting. That seems like a good place to start.
It's at a farm. I don't usually spend a lot of time searching through places like that, but sometimes you can get lucky.
Sounds like an old farm. Don't step on anything sharp.
It's a house that you're heading for. I've spent more than my fair share of days scavenging in places like that.
One of the countless abandoned homes you can find around here. Hopefully it'll be clear which one when you get there.
The report described an old house. Who knows, maybe you'll find some good salvage while you're there.
It's one of those lookout towers, like you see all over the forest. Careful on the steps, some of those towers are in pretty rough shape.
You know the real tall lookout towers that give a good view of everything around? You're headed for one of those.
I hope you're not scared of heights, because your destination is on of those big lookout towers.
It's a medical facility, which his pretty good news if you're a scavenger like me.
Sounded to me like a medical building, maybe a hospital.
My source mentioned a building with beds, life support equipment and offices. Probably some kind of old medical building.
They said it was like a cave but with wooden supports and digging tools. Guess they've never been in a mine before.
You're not claustrophobic, are you? If so, you're not going to like this, but the location appears to be a mine.
What's dark, dusty and dangerous all over? The answer is the place you're going. Yep, it's a mine.
You're heading for what used to be called a power substation. It's basically a bunch of machines and fences.
Back before the war, everyone had electricity that came from these places called power substations. That's where you're going.
Try not to be shocked when I say this, but you're heading for a power substation. Get it? Shocked? Okay, yeah, that was terrible.
Up for a little rest and relaxation? The info I got described a park, which is a place people used to go to relax. Go and enjoy yourself!
You're off to a park. Hey, why not pack a lunch and have a little picnic while you're there?
There's a park where some of us scavengers used to meet up to swap salvage. That's your destination.
If science and technology are your thing, then you'll be pleased to know that the location is an old research facility of some kind.
I had to dig a little to get that particular piece of information. Turns out it's a research facility, maybe a lab of some kind.
Good question. All I know is that it's some kind of research facility. You can usually find some interesting stuff in those places if you look carefully.
What was it I read in that magazine? "You've won an all-expenses-paid vacation to one of our fabulous local resorts!
Back before the war, they had places called luxury resorts. There's a few here in Appalachia, and you're going to be visiting what's left of one.
Oh, I'm glad you asked! You're going to one of those great old resorts where people used to relax. Wish I could have seen one in its prime, you know?
The area of interest is a school. As scavenging opportunities go, it's not bad.
You're never too old to learn, right? Seems appropriate given that you're about to go to school.
Well, I'm not sure how you feel about this, but the location you're heading for is a school. Me, I just keep thinking about all those poor kids.
What's pretty much every scavenger's favorite place? I'll tell you. It's a store. Happy looting!
You're going to love this. The location they described matches an old store I used to frequent. Those are some of the best places for salvage.
lines.note: explaining a mission/favor you are asking the player to do

lines.text: Some of us scavengers have a code word for "store", because we don't want to let everyone else know where all the good salvage is.
But I trust you, so I don't mind saying that you're headed to just such a place.
Intel was a little light this time around. All I can say is that it's a town.
All that my source could tell me was that he was in one of the local towns. I think he must be new to the area.
I had a bad signal, and the second half of the conversation was pretty garbled. I definitely caught something about a town, though.
It's pretty hard to mistake a trainyard for any other place, so even though the description was a little vague, I'm confident that's where you're going.
My friend said it was the place all the trains are sleeping, so that would be a trainyard. She's always had an interesting way of putting things.
Only place it could be is a trainyard.
Does a dark, creepy tunnel scare you away? Yeah, I didn't think so.
There was mention of a big, dark tunnel, but the person I talked to didn't want to go in there. I wouldn't either.
They seemed to say it was in a tunnel. You've got that Pip-Boy light, so you should be fine in there.
Soup's on, my friend. You're headed for a restaurant.
By all accounts, it's a pre-war restaurant. I'd ask you to bring me back something, but I've already eaten.
Was that a little rumble I heard from your stomach? You're in luck, because the location is a restaurant.
Out in the wilds. That's what my source told me, so that's what I'm telling you.
This is one of those times where I didn't get the most detailed info. All I can say it that it was a wilderness area, and the general direction.
The signal broke up right when I asked that. I heard the general area and the word "wilderness", but not much else. I hope that's enough.
I wish I could say. All I can really do is point you to the general area.
lines.note: sincere, trying to be helpful, but you really don't know much

lines.text: That part, I'm not sure about. What I heard was pretty light on specifics regarding the location, but I can tell you the general area.
lines.note: sincere, trying to be helpful, but you really don't know much

lines.text: I can point it out on the map, but I'm not real familiar with that area, so I can't give you much more help than that.
lines.note: sincere, trying to be helpful, but you really don't know much

lines.text: You know those people who make their home at Foundation? It's one of them.
Aside from someone who needs rescuing, I really couldn't say.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: There was something the person being tied up, but outside of that, I'm not sure.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: I really wish I knew, but I didn't get a lot of details. All I can say for sure is that someone's in trouble.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: Unfortunately, I didn't get any additional information beyond what I just said. I guess just look for the most dangerous thing and put an end to it.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: The description I got was, well... I didn't really get one. Just be ready for anything. I guess. I know that's not real helpful.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: I wish I could be more helpful, but I wasn't told much. The only thing I can say for certain is that you should be ready for a fight.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: Sounded to me like an Angler.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: Based on the description, I'm guessing you'll find an Angler on the prowl.

lines.text: I'm pretty sure there's an Angler involved.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: There was something about a woman's and a glowing red eye, so I'm going to say an Assaultron's involved.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: Well, you're getting this second-hand, of course, but it sure sounded to me like there's an Assaultron in the area.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: Whatever you've got that's good for killing robots, you'd better bring with you, because you'll be going up against an Assaultron.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: Thankfully it's just a Bloatfly. They're annoying, sure, but far from the scariest thing out there.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: I'll give you a hint. It's fat, disgusting, feeds on death things and flies. If you guessed a Bloatfly, you'd be correct.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: I wasn't there to see it myself, obviously, but based on what I heard, I'm willing to bet you're going to be hunting a Bloatfly.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: Judging by what I heard, I think it's safe to assume you'll find at least one Bloodbug.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: You might want to wear long sleeves, because it sounds like one of those big blood-sucking bugs awaits you.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: Probably a Bloodbug, given the description I heard. Nasty things, those.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: You know that gang of raiders called the Blood Eagles? Sounds like one of them is going to be your target.
Your mark is a Blood Eagle. Even by raider standards, they're pretty nasty.
If hunting violent psychopaths is your favorite pastime, then I have good news. You're going up against a member of the Blood Eagles.
Nothing too scary. Just a cave cricket, by the sound of it,
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: Judging by the info I got, it's probably one of those Cave Cricket things. I really hate giant bugs.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: I'm thinking a Cave Cricket, and that's fine with me, because even one less Cave Cricket in the world makes it a better place.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: I'm glad you asked, because this is one you're going to want to prepare for carefully. It's a Deathclaw.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: It's a Deathclaw for sure. Make sure you stock up on stimpaks before you go after it.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: You're not going to like the answer, but it's a Deathclaw. If I were you, I'd make sure my best armor and weapons were fully repaired.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: Sounds like a rogue Eyebot on the loose. Watch out for those lasers.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: There was mention of a hovering mechanical orb, so that's got to be an Eyebot. Good salvage on those things.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: It's one of those defective Eyebots. Every good scavenger knows that you can pull some pretty useful stuff off of them.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: I'm not sure if there's going to be any fog there, but I'm pretty confident you'll see a Fog Crawler.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: A Fog Crawler, no doubt about it. they're pretty tough, but it's a nice change of pace to eat seafood, right?
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: Sure sounded like a Fog Crawler to me. Tough shells on those things, and nasty claws, too. Should be fun, right?
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: Sounds like one of those Feral Ghouls is skulking around in the area.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: Likely a Feral Ghoul, if my instincts are right. You rarely find those things alone, so watch your back.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: A Feral Ghoul. I'd bet my last bobblehead on it. We scavengers run into those things all the time, and let me tell you, they're a damn nuisance.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: By all accounts, a Grafton Monster has claimed the area as its territory.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: It's one of those creatures they call a Grafton Monster. Probably my least favorite of all the cryptids.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: From what I gather, you'll be killing a Grafton Monster.
lines.note: I'd put good odds on it being a Grafton Monster. Those things really unnerve me, you know? How can it not have a face? It's unnatural.

lines.text: You know what a Gulper is? It's one of those. Got to be one of the strangest creatures I've ever seen.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: It's a Gulper for sure. I had one chase me out of an abandoned raider camp a while back. Lost a whole day's haul, too.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: Gulper. No doubt about it. If you ask me, those things are every bit as disgusting as they are dangerous.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: You should bring an empty jar, because I'm confident that a Honeybeast is your target. Kill the beast, collect the honey.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: If I were a betting man, I'd say a Honeybeast. Unless, of course, it was another kind of giant crawling bee monster being described to me.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: A Honeybeast. You know, that giant mutant killer bee surrounded by an angry swarm of regular-sized bees. Basically, two nightmares rolled into one.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: All I know is that there's a giant bug of some kind causing problems.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: You're off to kill a giant bug of some kind. Transparently much all I know.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: There was something a giant insect, which only narrows it down to something like 10 possible creatures. Not real helpful, I know.

lines.text: You can expect to find a walking, talking tin can, otherwise known as a Liberator Bot.
lines.note: friendly, sincere, sharing the intel you have with the player so they are informed about the favor/mission you are sending them on

lines.text: Judging by the mechanical Chinese shouting that was described to me, I think you can expect to find a Liberator Bot.

lines.text: Probably a pesky little Liberator Bot. They make great targets for scavengers, because you can get quality scarp at a minimum risk.

lines.text: I'll venture a guess and say it's a Megasloth, since the description was that of a giant sloth.

lines.text: The only thing that makes sense given what I know would be a Mirelurk.

lines.text: Mirelurk. Can't say what kind, exactly, but I'm sure you know the drill. Attack the soft parts. dodge the claws.

lines.text: Got be a Mirelurk. Someone's dining on seafood tonight!

lines.text: A Mole Miner, mostly likely. Damn diggers come up out of nowhere.

Probably worth looking into, anyway.

A good friend of mine ran into someone dangerous and barely got away. You'd be doing everyone a favor if you took out that menace.

lines.text: Poor kids these days. Then again, maybe it's... just better this way?
lines.note: Could be better in the apocalypse, things weren't all that great before.

lines.text: I should write about her sometime.
lines.note: Reflecting on his life.

lines.text: Libraries! That's what the world needs again, dang it. That's where we went wrong.
lines.note: He realizes suddenly

lines.text: Oh. Pardon me.
lines.note: He tooted.

lines.text: *humming*
lines.note: folksy old song, anything

lines.text: Interesting. I should write that down...
lines.note: Thought of something.

lines.text: Someone said, never wear black and brown together. After a full apocalypse and nearly 70 years on this earth, I can say... do what you want. Heh.
Don't live by rules just to live by them.
Had a dream the other night about the old days. I don't miss it much. Seems like I should, but I don't.
lines.note: He's happy with his new freedom

lines.text: Best things in life aren't always free, but... sometimes you can get a discount.
You're never too old to make new friends. I promise... I promise.
*coughing* Excuse me.
lines.note: He's got a persistent cough.

lines.text: I should be scared, but I'm not.
lines.note: Place got nuked.

lines.text: This too shall pass, so they say.
lines.note: Place got nuked.

lines.text: We've been through worse. Hang in there.
lines.note: Place got nuked.

lines.text: You get used to anything given enough time.
lines.note: Place got nuked.

lines.text: This was not the future that we wanted. But we will take it. And we will run with it.
lines.note: Place got nuked.

lines.text: By the way... you can call me Gramps, if you like. Everybody who knows me does anyway.
lines.note: He's happy with the nickname anyway

topics.prompt: Hard pass. Bye.

lines.text: I get it. I get it. Not everybody's got a decent place ready for guests...
lines.note: Quick Insult

topics.prompt: You can stay with me.

lines.text: I think I just might. Maybe just for a short while... enough to catch a breath and rest my bones.
Set out a comfy chair for me, will you? I need to pick up some of my things, and I'll be there soon...
lines.note: He's happy he found somebody.

lines.text: Ever since the war, I've been sort of scrabbling along thinking of my books, making the best of it.
lines.note: Tells you the tale

lines.text: I have enough time to write some more, and that's exactly what I aim to do. But... in order to do that, I need a place to stay for a bit.
And... if you have a place, well... I would be happy to watch it for you. To tell you some stories. I'm a wealth of practical knowledge, kid.
lines.note: Amazing offer!

topics.prompt: [Luck 8+] Uh. You're a... famous... author?

lines.text: Was that a guess? What the heck? Hmm, maybe you have a deep-seated memory of me, buried within your psyche. Okay, I love it, let's go with that.
lines.note: Convincing himself that he loves it.

topics.prompt: [Charisma 3+] I apologize for my ignorance, but I would like to know who you are.

lines.text: Oh my. We've got ourselves quite a talker here. Well. That was very kind of you. I shouldn't expect everybody to know who I am, after all.

topics.prompt: I don't know. Maybe?

lines.text: Well... that's unfortunate. *sighs* Run along now, I suppose. Kids these days...

topics.prompt: Uh. Nope. Not even slightly. Sorry.

lines.text: That's... okay. You are pretty young. Oh well.
I know, I know. You're thinking... "I've seen you before!" Right? You recognize this mug, don't ya?
lines.note: He knows you have no clue what he's talking about

lines.text: Shoulda built that house long ago.
lines.note: Sad for himself

lines.text: My dang knee! Again! Every blasted time... dang it all to heck.
lines.note: Sad for himself

lines.text: I just need to rest my eyes for a bit... that's all.
Nevermind that... where was I? Huh.
lines.note: Lost his train of thought

lines.text: Always wanted to retire in the forest somewhere.
*whistling*
lines.note: Any old tune.

lines.text: Oh! Drat. What was your name again? Wait. Maybe we haven't met.
lines.note: A little embarrassed

lines.text: We all gotta toot. It's normal, kid!
lines.note: It is what it is

lines.text: I'd gladly walk up a hill in the snow if it means not eating from a garbage can again!
lines.note: It is what it is

lines.text: Hey kid, pull my finger. Hah! Too late!
lines.note: It is what it is

lines.text: You seem like somebody who appreciates resourcefulness.
lines.note: This NPC's for hire and going to hard sell.

lines.text: I've been living in several different areas of the country since the war, you know... and... I know how to live off the land now. You know?
lines.note: This NPC's for hire and going to hard sell.

lines.text: Tell me, kid, you ever think about what retirement might be like in this world? This is it. You find someone to take care of you. Done.
lines.note: This NPC's for hire and going to hard sell.

lines.text: I know all the best garbage piles in this whole area... but! I also know some of the best junkpiles, too.
lines.note: This NPC's for hire and going to hard sell.

lines.text: Listen, kiddo. The world's a cruel place. Pick up some family where you can, it helps.
lines.note: This NPC's for hire and going to hard sell.

lines.text: Always be kind to others when you can. Don't cost anything at all.
lines.note: Friendly advice

lines.text: Good to see you too, squirt! Gramps is busy right now. Okay?
lines.note: Is he your gramps?!

lines.text: Hush. Not now, okay, kiddo?
lines.note: Is he your gramps?!

lines.text: I'll talk to you later, okay?
lines.note: Is he your gramps?!

lines.text: I know, I know. Hush.
lines.note: Is he your gramps?!

topics.prompt: [Intelligence 8+] Oh! You're that author! I saw your book cover!

lines.text: Bingo! We have a winner here, kids! Will you look at that. Someone knows me! I knew it would happen.
lines.note: Excited, kicking heels with joy

items.howToObtain: Companion Quest

lines: Gain Resistances and AP Regen based on your CHA while not on a team.
When adventuring alone, take 15% less damage and gain 20% AP regen.
When adventuring alone, take 20% less damage and gain 30% AP regen.

lines.text: It's a tough world out there, so take it slow and be safe.
Appalachia's a lot to take in, so play it safe and smart.
Make sure you got food, water, and maybe some Stimpaks. Never know when you'll need them.
Good luck. I'm rooting for you!
Keep an eye out and don't get in over your head and I'm sure you'll be fine. Probably.
I'd say I wish you well or something, but I figure there's nothing you can't handle at this point. So, have fun?
Time for you to do that crazy thing you do. In style.
I guess this is goodbye. For now. You'll be back? I kinda get stir crazy around here sometimes.
You know what needs doing so, uh, do... it? Really smooth, I know.
I have some leads on something for tomorrow. Maybe getting ahead of myself, but I figure you got this in the bag.
You take care of business, and I'll make sure you get your reward. Deal? Good.
You know, I'm not going to worry about it. You got this.
You keep knocking them over, and I'll keep lining them up for you.
And so it's go team time! Well, mostly you. Really, all you. Hey, sometimes I kill Mole Rats when you're gone.
You know the drill. So, uh, yeah. We're good? Yeah, we're good.

topics.prompt: Maybe later.

lines.text: Gotcha. I'm in the middle of deciphering a code from some mothman hunters anyway.
I've got to keep monitoring the chatter anyway, see ya.
No problem. I'm pretty busy myself. I'm the safety contact right now for someone who is tracking down strange lights in the sky.
Understood, I've got to be monitoring the chatter now anyway. Lots to do.
You gotta do what you gotta do.
I knew it. I knew you'd be interested. Best of luck.
lines.note: pleased the player is doing your favor/quest

lines.text: Who brings you the intel on the cool weapons? Me, that's who. Knock them dead. I guess, literally.
I hope it's the best Flamer, Gauss Rifle, or... uhh... machete ever. In history.
Excellent. Go forth and armor up. That sounds so medieval, right?
lines.note: pleased the player is doing your favor/quest

lines.text: There's no offense like a good defense. Wait. That makes no sense any more.
I hope this lead pans out. I mean it will. Armor here we come.
So kill all the things and bask in our collective gratitude.
lines.note: pleased the player is doing your favor/quest

lines.text: Boy, I'd hate to be on the opposite side of this mission. Good luck.
Time for some violence. Hopefully the nice and one-sided kind.
I'd wish you luck, but I don't think you'll really need it.
Have fun out there. And I will absolutely not be hosting a big party when you're gone. At all.
Good luck out there. I'll keep the kettle on. Hey, you know, I actually could do that.
lines.note: pleased the player is doing your favor/quest

topics.prompt: How do you know about this?

lines.text: I found out via my sparkly personality. I'm good that way.
I heard it from a friend. More an acquaintance, really. Maybe a little on the stranger side, but you get the idea.
I have my sources. And my ways.
All I'll say, is even in the wastelands it pays to be friendly. A kind word and the well-placed cap can do wonders.
Give a traveler some hooch and you'd be amazed, and often disgusted, at what you'll hear.
I don't know what it is about weapons, but people love talking about them. On and on and on.
The amount of chatter about this weapon and that. I mean, I pay attention for you. For me, I'd rather take a nap.
People gossip. Especially about firepower or the latest and greatest deadly instrument of death. It passes the time.
I... forgot. Uhm. A trader? An eyebot? Literally drawing a blank here.
I was told on the condition of anonymity. And as a professional busy-body, I protect my sources.
A junk merchant of all things. Who knew they were interested in random piles of garbage?
Some junk trader. It was a trove he couldn't hit, so he's hoping someone gets lucky. Nice guy.
It's kind of a drunken haze. I want to say a... giant gecko. That's the image I have. Yay, alcohol.
My junk contacts. Kind of sad that I have those. But there you go.
People passing by. I mean, you can place your camp literally anywhere and I swear at least one lookey-loo would pass by.

topics.prompt: Is there anything dangerous nearby that I should know about?

lines.text: Would you believe... Snallygasters? And lots of them. Oh so much fun.
Well, just a few... vicious, creepy and just all around no fun Snallygasters.
From the stories and rumors I pieced together, it's full of Snallygasters. Or Pioneer Scouts. Stories get weird sometimes.
Keep calm. Even breathing. So Yao Guai. Just a couple, several, a lot... of them.
The best info I've got points to... Yao Guai. Lots of them. So... surprise? I don't have a cake. I should've softened the blow with cake.
You'll appreciate this, this is good. Yao Guai. Because that makes this job sooo easy.
A hunter friend said there's wolves in that area. So vicious pack hunters.
Wolves. On the scale of things, not the worst. But no push overs, either. OK, maybe a little.
People have heard wolf howls around there. So expect them.
A pack of Vicious Dogs. Because putting down dogs is great. Thanks for that, Appalachia.
Couple of buddies ran into a pack of vicious dogs around here a while back. Could still be there. Fun times.
Lots of vicious dogs are in that area. So, don't be surprised if you see some.
A bunch of Radtoads. Creepy, creepy Radtoads.
There are those yucky eggs all over that area. Which means toads. With all the googly eyed goodness that comes with them.
Giant toads have been spotted near there. My favorite. I'm being sarcastic.
It's full of those giant ticks. Don't you just love it when they're full of your blood. That's a treat.
Be warned... this place is crawling with Ticks. Loads and loads of them.
It's full of bloodsuckers. And only in Appalachia do you get to say, "Be more specific." Giant Ticks.
No one knows for certain what's there. Some swamp creatures...? Just guessing.
My money's on swamp creatures of some flavor. And that's not an invitation to lick one of them. Because, yuck.
Sane people kind of avoid that area. So best guess: something swampy.
A lot of those big bruisers, your pals and mine, Super Mutants.
Glad you asked, because Super Mutants have been spotted over there. So be careful. Or better yet, stay here and we can play some tunes.
Everyone says there's Super Mutants over there. OK, not everyone. Scorched mainly say, "One of us" but everyone I asked.
Stingwing nests have been spotted around there. So lots of them is my guess.
So the junk trader, and if you think I'm funny - he's a real hoot, a national treasure, really... Anyway, Stingwings. Sorry.
Lots of flying bugs have been spotted over there. My caps are on Stingwings.
Two people have said it's a "Sheepsquatch." Maybe more than one. I mean, how gullible do I look?
I fully expect you to laugh, but people "say" there are Sheepsquatches there. I know, haha.
A tracker came by, you know the "I never smile even at the birth of my daughter type" and he said look out for Sheepsquatch. Those... aren't real, right?
Oh, you know, nothing. Just some building destroying Sentry Bots. That's all, though.
I'm glad you asked. At least one Sentry Bot was spotted near there. And that's a whole mess of bad news.
My best intelligence, and hey don't laugh, I'm intelligent... Anyway, Sentry Bots. So be very, very careful.
Radscorpions. That's all I'll say. Unless you ask me more questions.
People have seen Radscorpions in the area. With their nasty poisonous tails and hide that just brushes off bullets. *groan*
Soo.... Radscorpions are in that area. So stay here, instead. You aren't staying, are you?
There's usually Scorched in the area. Such a shame.
You can expect Scorched. They're everywhere. Which is really, really depressing when you think about it.
The area is crawling with Scorched. OK, not literally crawling. Because they walk. I'm going to stop talking now.
Robots of some kind. That's all I got.
It's pretty common knowledge that there are a lot of robots over there.
Would you believe robots? Well, you should. Because they're there... and all over.
So lots of military robots. I'm so glad we built all those to protect us from communists. I feel so protected right now.
My ex says it's full of top-of-the-line military robots. So happy hunting?
He lost them in this place, but I bet you they're still there, waiting.
Everyone says its full of military robots and to stay away. Which for you, I imagine is an engraved invitation.
It's full of Robobrains. Another of humanity's finest ideas.
There have been Robobrains spotted in that area. And poison ivy. I'll let you be the judge about what to worry about.
You can expect Robobrains. Seriously, who thought that was a good idea? I would find them and I would... have strong words with them.
A literal rat's nest. That's what's there. Well, Radrats. But still.
Everyone says there are Radrats there. They looked at me like, "How can you not know that?" Do I look like an encyclopedia?
Major rat infestation. So, good times ahead. And possibly rabies.
Lots of Raiders in that area. So be careful.
A whole squad, team... Listen, I don't know how many... but Raiders.
That's Raider territory. So expect them. A lot of them.
So good news: not the big a threat, really. Bad news: radroaches. A whole nest of them.
This place is utterly infested with radroaches. And there goes my appetite.
A skittering mass of delightful radroaches. Man, sometimes I don't envy your job.
So... Radants. Because one of those quick little guys isn't bad enough. Surprise, friends!
This place is teeming with ants. Of the big and hungry variety.
Ants. I used to feel a little bad for squishing them, if I could go back I'd buy a bulldozer and show them who's boss.
A lot of RobCo's finest. Protectrons. That's what's there.
So a lot of Protectrons are in the area. I wonder what you should call a pack of them? A herd? A flamboyance? An annoyance? Hmm.
Robots have been spotted there. Specifically Protectrons.
Some sort of... mutated thingies? Listen, that's all I got.
The talk I've heard runs all over the map. Some sort of mutated scary thing. So yeah, could be anything.
Some sort of mutated monstrosities which, of course, we've grown to love.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: You'll find Mr. Gutsies. As in plural. Because one isn't enough to ruin your day.
There are a lot of Mr. Gutsies there. And I know Assaultrons and Sentry Bots are scary, but Gutsies cut down people just as bad. Maybe worse.
So some programmer back in the day thought it would be just swell if the fall back pathing code sent our favorite Mr. Gutsies to patrol where you're going.
You hear that scurrying sound? And the barge reeeah. That's a Mole Rat. Expect lots of that.
lines.note: Barge reeah is him trying to make the sound of a mole rat bursting from the ground and going, "raarrr.

lines.text: A happy little colony of Mole Rats live there. And they will most certainly not try to eat your face. Oh wait, they will.
Expect Mole Rats. Lots of them.
Mole Miners have been spotted over there. So expect them in all their wonderful miner claw glory.
Mole Miners. That's what you'll find. So take cover and try to draw them out one at a time. That's what my hunter friend said.
You'll find Mole Miners there. Why? Who knows? No seriously, who knows?
From the oh so wonderful seaside smells, Mirelurks. In all their stomach churning glory.
You can expect a colony of Mirelurks. Hopefully they won't be expecting you.
Mirelurks. So take it slow and easy and aim for the head... Wait, were you the one who told me that advice? Whoops.
A Mega Sloth has been seen around there. They are mean.
Expect a Mega Sloth. I know people that think they are just precious. Crazy, right?
The radio chatter says there's at least one Mega Sloth there. It shouldn't be hard to spot.
Lots of little commie bots. Your favorite, my favorite... Liberators.
I was drinking with some fellow wanderers, they said the place is swarming with Liberator Bots. Before they passed out.
Liberators have been spotted there. Why would communists would want to capture that spot? No idea.
lines.note: warning player about enemies at mission location (you assume the player can handle themselves, but you want them prepared)

lines.text: You can expect bugs. What type, who can keep track of them all? I mean, who would want to.
So many skittering chittering sounds to be heard. Bugs are there.
Just be aware that this place tends to attract giant insects of all kinds. I know, I love Appalachia, too, right?
Honey Beasts. They give me the creeps. I mean, bees that shoot more bees. That's just sick.
I heard that that is a Honey Beast breeding ground. Which is gross on so many levels.
Our friendly sweet pals, the Honey Beasts, they're there. Of course they are.
I heard there are Gulpers there. Not Swallowers. Not Breathers. Gulpers. Yeah.
So "gulpers" are there. Whatever those area.
So Tim, he's one of my drinking buddies, swear there are Gulpers there. And he described them. And they sound scary. And made up.
So expect a big hulking Grafton Monster. Seriously, they have no head. Why isn't anyone else freaking out about that?
One of my personal favorite nightmares may be there. The. Grafton. Monster. *shudder*
There's a Grafton Monster that is sometimes in the area. And I say, we should just fence it off and let him own it.
You're seriously still doing this, aren't you?
That place is overflowing with ferals. Who knows how many and where they all come from.
Lots of Feral Ghouls have been spotted around there. It just makes me sick.
Loads of ferals have been seen over there. So, you've been warned.
So, you want to into a whole mess of Fog Crawlers? Because me? I definitely don't.
The word is that Fog Crawlers nest there. Which is more than a word. And it's a not a good word.
Massive slimy Fog Crawlers. That's what the magic eight ball predicts for your future.
It's not so bad this time. Eyebots. I mean they can and will kill you. Just slower than most the things around here.
Some of those floating eyebots around. That's it. So a nice quick assignment.
Lots of eyebots have been spotted around there. They make for good target practice.
So you want to know what's there? Isn't it great weather we're having? Heard any good jokes? I... uhh...
Deathclaws. That's what there. Right.
At least one, possibly many... Deathclaws. It's not too late to back out.
There are... terrifying tales about that place. And the Deathclaws that live there.
Cave Crickets. There was a time where that wouldn't make me terrified. That time was many years ago.
If not, well, you're in for a treat! This place is currently bursting at the seams with them.
A lot of hopping chittering Cave Crickets. So you're in for a lot of good times.
Do you like Cave Crickets? If so, boy, you are in luck.
A lot of zippy annoying Bloodbugs. Those guys are the worst. Except for Deathclaws. Oh and Mirelurk Queens. Or...
OK, they aren't the worst - but they're so not good.
The place is infested with Bloodbugs. My gift to you. I know, I shouldn't have.
Bloodbugs. Flying oh so hard to nail with a pipe pistol, blood bugs.
Good news: easy assignment. Bad news: Bloatflies. Disgusting little beasts.
So there are Bloatflies over there. Not so bad as things go, but, still... gross.
Bloatflies. This one is all you, my friend.
This place has some serious resistance. At least one Assaultron. *shudder*
Just one of the deadliest robots around: the Assaultron. Probably more than one. The things we do.
Everyone says there's assaultrons over there. Nobody's actually seen one up close, because you know laser beam and then the aahhhh death.
Something called Anglers live there. And I assume they aren't the fly fishing kindly old gentleman kind. Although that would be so welcomed.
You can expect Anglers there. That's bad, right? They made it sound bad.
Maybe just the obvious: a "run-they're-aggressive-and-going-to-shred-us" of Anglers would suffice.
A bunch of Anglers. Apparently they have this floaty bit? Are they pulling my leg with this?
Word is there are Blood Eagles in that area. That's really, really not a good word then.
A lot of Blood Eagles are know to be around there. So be careful. Those guys are no joke.
Oh, just a few Blood Eagles. Because that's what Appalachia needs more of.
You get the joy of fighting Mothman Cultists. Make sure you bring your tinfoil hat.
What do you say to Mothman Cultists? And you probably say, "Yes." Because you're just the right sort of crazy to do that.
Expect some of Mothman Cultists. Because around here that is a thing.
A bunch of happy Floaters. It'll be fun, right? No?
There have been Floaters sighted around there. And often that means Super Mutants. But maybe you'll get lucky?
Who am I kidding?
Your favorite, my favorite: Floaters. Especially the blue ones. They are the.... worst!
I know you're going to love this. Expect the unexpected. Because everyone I ask has no idea.
I did my homework. I hobnobbed, I kvetched, I even insinuated once. And I got... nothing. Zilch.
I asked everybody. No one knows. It's a genuine mystery. Excited?

topics.prompt: Where am I going?

lines.text: It's over... Well, by the... Just let me put it on your map.
lines.note: sincere, trying to be helpful, but you really don't know much

lines.text: I think I can tell you how to get there... but otherwise, you're on your own.
lines.note: sincere, trying to be helpful, but you really don't know much

lines.text: Sometimes even I come up a little short. I can give you the coordinates, but that's about as helpful as I can be.
lines.note: sincere, trying to be helpful, but you really don't know much

lines.text: From what I can tell, you have to go to some sort of camp. God, I hope not here.
Some sort of camp site or campground is the destination.
It's time to go camping. Well, not here. Out there. It's at a camp. That's all I got.
I believe it's at a store or shopping center. If you see any marshmallows, grab some. S'more time, right?
You get to go to a store. Which is a lot more exciting and deadly than it used to be. Except for Black Friday. Right?
lines.note: explaining a mission/favor you are asking the player to do

lines.text: Some sort of store. Once a temple to commerce, now full of irradiated who-knows-what.
It's in one of the local towns. I know, super helpful, right?
A... town, hamlet, burg... You get the idea.
Somewhere in a town. Hey, it's better than saying somewhere in Appalachia.
Head to this trainyard. It'll be there. Probably. Hey, I'm just the messenger.
I asked a buddy who asked an old hunter friend, who asked a former solider she knows, who asked a farmer that just arrived from the east...
And the farmer said that she heard a trader say that he saw someone in this exact trainyard with that stuff. So, that's what I got.
It's definitely a trainyard. No question about it. Except the one you just asked. And that is answered.
It's in a tunnel. A dark, oh so cheery tunnel. I bet your camp is sounding really good right now.
I know the tunnel to go to. Because dark creepy tunnels equal fun.
The target location is a tunnel. So there you go. You ask, and I answer. Teamwork.
Some sort of civic building. Listen, I'm not from here, I'm doing my best.
Some sort of old government building. I think. Listen, I know where it is. Exactly what it was Pre-War...
So the job's at a civic building. Well, a building for sure. Alright, I can point to it on your map.
It's at a communications building. In and out, and no one is the wiser. Except us. Because it's a life experience.
I've narrowed it down to this area. It's a building. And my oh so helpful friend said "the communication kind.
This is the compound to go to. Definitely. If you believe the drunken ramblings of friends. Which I do.
Head over to this compound. It's probably military. That makes sense, right?
It's in a military compound, I think. So, sure, should be as easy as... well, not at all.
You get to go to one of the picturesque local dams. Fun.
So the target location is a dam. Which means trouble. The dams around here are loads of good times.
So head to this marked dam and take care of business. That's it.
It's at a factory. So bring your hard hat, punch in, and get it done.
You're headed to one of the many local hubs of manufacturing and production. Appalachia is lousy with factories.
Head to this factory. The intel seems solid.
So it's some sort of farm. That's where it is. The details were a little vague. Sorry.
Time to go to a farm. Agriculture. Gets me every time.
Some sort of... farm? Field? Ag Center? It's something. And I'll point to it on a map. Because that's what I do.
It's at a house. Really, that's it. Hopefully no big deal.
Go to this house. I love it when they get that specific. Instead of, "It's in Peru." It's "403 Baker Street.
I'd check out this house. They were pretty certain that's where to go.
You aren't afraid of heights, right? You know those lookout towers? Well, that's where you're going.
It's at a lookout tower. Have you ever been to the top of those? Quite the view, good for scouting. I'm serious.
Go to this lookout tower and you'll be in business. The business of looking out. That sounded better in my head.
So it's at a medical facility. So you can get your annual checkup at the same time.
It's at a hospital or medical facility or pharmacy... OK, I don't know exactly what this building is. But I can point to it on a map.
Some sort of... medical facility? Yeah, that's what I'm going with.
So it's in a mine. A mine in Appalachia. It's not a cliche. They're out there.
I talked with some other friends, we narrowed it down to this mine. Be careful, mines around here... not to be trifled with.
So you get to go to a mine. Your life, I swear, never boring.
Get out your picnic basket, it's a Park. Hey, they can't all be gems.
So the target's in one of the local parks. All that wide open space, with who knows what watching...
Try this park. Me and my friends are pretty certain that's where it's at.
Check out this power substation. Maybe circle it first, all that equipment can hide who knows what inside the fence.
So one of the local power substations. That's where you need to go.
So I got a tip from my old girlfriend, and that is a story let me tell you... This one time... Right, sorry. It's a power substation.
The odds are super good, it's at this research facility. Or it's in Pennsylvania. But my caps are on here.
So I asked around, did some digging - and the consensus is it's at this research facility.

lines.text: Weapons aren't really my gig, but I got a lead on one... If you're interested.
Weapon stash any interest to you? If so, today's your lucky day.
Guns, blades, and whatever. Kinda makes the world go 'round now. *sigh* I got a lead on one, if you like.
Armor, right? You're into that, right? I got a lead for you.
The amount of lead you take, ain't healthy. Heard of some armor that might help. Maybe? You think?
One day, I'm going to write a ballad. About the new knights. In shiny armor. Oh right, I know of some armor out there. You in?
I've seen all the crazy shit you do with... well, garbage. It's kind of amazing. And well, uh, gross. I know where you can get more junk.
Who knew junk piles would be so... exciting. But I heard of a stash of components...?
You like good old fashion junk, right? If that's making the inner you go "Yay" then I have something for you.
Probably worth looking into, anyway.
I don't say it lightly, but there's a real real problem out there. And they need to be taken out. Like... OK, killed. I said it.
I hate to ask you to do... Well, the thing you do as far as I can tell all the time... You know, bad guy. Action. Dead bad guy?

lines.text: I got a bit of violence for you. Total bad guy, or girl, or whatever. Point is, it's an equation that needs my dear friend. That's, uh, you by the way.
Some friends say there's something baaad out there. And it needs a you-sized solution.
So, OK, bad things are out there. Most sane people run for the hills. But you, you, my friend, that's where you come in.
A friend needs some world-class extermination. And I told, I know just who to talk to.
I got a real job. A friend-of-a-friend is in a real bind. Needs the whole Adventure Hour rescue.
Ready to get on a white horse and leap to the rescue? If so, I know someone that needs it. Like... soon.
I heave it for you. The rescue. Our hero, er, you, barges in... Whoosh, boom. Everyone cheers. Oh, this is real. Someone's in trouble.
Someone stopped by earlier... heard me singing. We talked a bit... heard about something that sounded perfect for you.

lines.text: So, I was doing my thing and a gig landed in my lap and I thought of you.
lines.note: Going to offer a quest.

lines.text: I had the craziest day. And in the middle of all of that, I found something. Something you might like.
lines.note: Going to offer a quest.

lines.text: I walked around, did the talky talk, and listen listen. Guess what I picked up?
lines.note: Going to offer a quest.

lines.text: So I've been doing what I do, talking, being social and blam. Something you might like.
lines.note: Going to offer a quest.

lines.text: Heard about something from a trader who happened across my path. It's odd how these things work out, isn't it?
Would you look at that. You got it! Good for you, but better for me.
You found it? I spent most of the time you were away having an internal debate about whether or not you'd die trying to get this.
I guess you proved me half-wrong and half-right at the same time.
Made in back in one piece, huh? Well I'll just take that pretty little thing right off your hands, thank you very much.
Well, this is a pleasant surprise. Now I've just to figure out where to stow this thing.
Back with my little prize? I've had dogs that didn't fetch half as well as you do. I'd offer you a bone, but I'm afraid I'm out at the moment.
I should walk more... It pays to stay in shape. Just not very much.

lines.text: Nothing new dropped in my lap yet. Which is good. For my lap.

lines.note: Sorry she has no quests.
