items.description: Xerxo is an alien from the proud Zebulon Empire. At least, that's what he thinks.
items.howToObtain: Can be purchased with certain bundles from the Atom Shop.

lines: Can be purchased with certain bundles from the Atom Shop.
You pay 50% fewer Caps when Fast Traveling.

lines.text: You know that comic about the Unstoppables visiting the Ux-Ron galaxy? Complete fabrication.
They visited the Ux-Ray galaxy, and it wasn't the Unstoppables, it was the Immovables. Tell your historians to get it right next time.
Zebulonians used to molt, much like your snakes. But now we simply discard the skin and hang it in our closets as a memory of our youth.
Greetings Earthling. I am Xerxo, son of Xarlax, captain of the starship Voxthaltha of the Zebulon Empire.
The Zebulonians weren't the first to develop advanced probing technology, but we definitely are the ones who perfected it.
We've got machines that can probe 100,000 organisms per second, and serve you ice cream when you're done.
What you call food on this planet is a disgrace. But the alcohol? Well, let's just say I'll be filing a Zebulonian copyright for all your drinks very soon.
If you need any help relaxing, I can show you an ancient Zebulonian meditation technique. It involves heavy drinking and vomiting out negative energies.
The gravity on this planet is so weird. My xer-joints, or what you humans call knees, they hurt so much when I have to stand for long hours.
There are 10,000 starships in the Zebulonian fleet, each one equipped with the latest in interstellar missile technology and a dozen private chefs.
I'll have you know the moonshine on this planet is its only redeeming quality.
There's eighty other planets I'd rather be on than this one. However, it still has its perks.
I have family on Zebulon. We communicate daily via telepathy. The long distance charges are out of this world, but it's certainly worth it.
I'm going to miss a lot of my childrens' milestones. When they play their first Zorxball game. When they fire their first ray gun. Prom.
Doing an audit of an entire planet is incredibly hard. You never know when one of you might blow it up again.
Space travel isn't very difficult. Time travel, even easier. But this "walking" these Earthlings are so fond of? It's killing me!
I've met a few people on this planet that I mistook for Zebulonians. But apparently they're something called "ghouls".
Until they sent me here, I was going to retire and live on a beach on the planet Ur-Vox. Just me, the sand, the ocean, and those rings of color just like a rainbow.
Oy vey, one of my backs is killing me.
I'll have you know I've flipped no less than ten planets in the last year alone. I'm not just a starship captain, I'm a renowned intergalactic realtor.
Sometimes I look at your sunsets and think to myself, oh, this planet is going to look fabulous when it's furnished. I really should remember to factor that into the price.
Every doctor in the Zebulon Empire learns to probe their first species by the age of ten. It's part of their rite of passage.
As a starship captain, I've seen my share of abductions. Super Mutants, Sheepsquatches... we've studied them all.
Our studies show the most intelligent being on this planet is actually a Mole Miner. Yet they want me to bargain with humans instead.
We Zebulonians have long since evolved past the need for skin. Our insides aren't so weak that they need to be covered.
My superiors are mostly hands off, but tentacles on. Tentacles tend to stick better, and keep you working.
Twenty days until retirement and I get tasked with flipping this shitshow of a planet. Can you believe my luck?
Earthling.
When you have 47 stomachs, it's hard to tell which one has indigestion.
The air here is toxic to three of my lungs. Good thing I can shed them easily.
Vaya con Dios, Earthling.
Until our next encounter.
So long.
All Zebulonian technology is delivered through one's face holes. It provides the most impact.
lines.note: Gentle, almost apologetic, but doctor-like "It is what it is" tone

lines.text: It's simple. The shot from my ray gun will rewrite your particles with that of a kangaroo and the DNA of an Olympic gold medalist in the long jump.
The effects will be temporary, but should be felt almost immediately. Just try it, and you'll see.
Of course, Earthling.
What remains to be discussed?
If we must.
What a day. I could use a xartini. Ooo... or better yet, Earth whiskey.

topics.prompt: Welcome to our planet, Xerxo.

lines.text: Thank you. You know, many Earthlings are hostile to our kind. They call us names like "ghoul," or "crazy person," or "stop, thief!
lines.note: Appreciative, warming up

lines.text: But me, I ignore all of these taunts, for the sake of my mission: the invasion and complete subjugation of your planet.
lines.note: Tone shifts to something matter-of-fact and somewhat sinister

topics.prompt: Nice to meet you. Shall I take you to our leader?

lines.text: There is no need, Earthling. I have already met him and eaten him, as is required by Zebulon law.
lines.note: Appreciative and matter-of-fact

lines.text: Before digesting him in one of my 47 stomachs, I made sure to slather plenty of barbecue sauce on his forehead, just the way you humans like it.
We're not barbarians, after all. We may plan on invading and subjugating your entire species, but we do respect your customs.
lines.note: Genuine and earnest

topics.prompt: I don't think you're any of the things you just said.

lines.text: That was your first mistake. Thinking. But please rest assured, you won't have to think any longer, once we invade and subjugate your people.
In fact, thinking will likely be made a crime punishable by death, followed of course by having to watch a series of instructional videos.
Given that there are 1,757 stages of hell in the Zebulon afterlife, you will have ample time to watch these videos and reflect on your mistakes.

topics.prompt: Oh boy, this is going to be fun.

lines.text: Maybe for you. But I take no joy in the complete domination of your species.
lines.note: Earnest, matter-of-fact.

lines.text: I am simply required by intergalactic law to read you the terms and conditions of your surrender.
If not for that, we would not be having this conversation, because I would be drinking a xartini and you would be a pile of goo.

topics.prompt: [Charisma 4+] You're invading our planet? At least buy us dinner first.

lines.text: That may be how it works in your culture, but Zebulonians do not engage in your primitive rituals of dinner, movies, and inane small talk.
When we see something we want, we form an exploratory committee on the 25th of Dexember, to summon the God of War, Xanta.
Xanta then creates a list of planets that have been naughty, and nice. The naughty ones we invade. And your planet has been... so naughty.

topics.prompt: Why are you taking over our planet?

lines.text: Should we wait until you screw it up even more?
lines.note: Bemused, aloof

lines.text: Relax, Earthling. We don't plan on staying long. Your planet is what they call in the intergalactic market, a "fixer upper.
We plan on cleaning it, renovating it, and then flipping it to the Martians at twice the cost.

topics.prompt: You're reselling our planet for profit? Didn't you say Zebulon was an empire?

lines.text: Yes. A real estate empire. What kind of empire were you imagining? No doubt one that reflects your failings as a species.

topics.prompt: Do the Martians even have that kind of capital?

lines.text: Oh yes. Martian sand is quite valuable in the Andromeda Galaxy. It is the source of the Empire's early wealth. They use our sand in hourglasses, you know.
They say using Martian sand is more precise than an atomic clock. Of course, it's all just a scam. Anyone with 19 brains knows that time isn't real.

topics.prompt: What if I bought the planet off you? I have the caps.

lines.text: Don't make me laugh. Your currency is no good on the intergalactic market. We don't use inefficient, primitive methods of exchange like bottlecaps.
All of our transactions are performed using ions, transferred via clouds of gas we exhale using specialized glands.

topics.prompt: I'm not even going to dignify that nonsense with a response.

lines.text: There's no need for you to respond. At least, not unless you've been chosen as Supreme Leader, at which point I will need you to formally surrender.

topics.prompt: No one can own the planet. You can't sell it.

lines.text: What's the matter with you, are you some kind of communist? You Earthlings should know that everything can be bought and sold, even this conversation.
I'm actually recording this on a holotape right now, and will be putting it up for auction this very evening.
Hopefully you don't say anything idiotic and tank the value.

topics.prompt: Well, in any case, enjoy your stay.

lines.text: I will do my best, but this is hardly a vacation. Once the Zebulon fleet arrives, you'll see.

topics.prompt: I, for one, welcome our new Zebulonian overlords.

lines.text: Good. I'm glad you're able to see the forest for the trees, even though you burned half of them down.

topics.prompt: All right, whatever. Just don't touch my things.

lines.text: Don't worry, I would never touch anything you Earthlings have put your sausage-like tentacles on.
lines.note: Aloof, mildly disgusted at the thought

lines.text: Anyway, there's still some paperwork I need to file for closing escrow on the planet, so if you need me, I'll be on my spaceship.

topics.prompt: I'm in need of your services.

lines.text: All right, Earthling. What do you need?
Normally I don't do this, but in exchange for letting me park my spaceship here, I'm willing to rewrite the rules.
I know intergalactic parking fees can be exorbitant, so don't think I don't appreciate your gesture.
And if you want to learn the secrets of intergalactic space flight, I can help with that too.
lines.note: Hints of pride

topics.prompt: I'd like to know more about you.

lines.text: Very well. Proceed with your inquiry, Earthling.

topics.prompt: Have you discovered anything interesting about our planet?

lines.text: Besides the marshmallow center?
Besides the caramel-filled crust?
Besides the mole people living in the clouds?
Besides the odd noise it makes when it rotates?
Besides the fact that it's an intergalactic tax haven?
You mean, aside from the strange smells emanating from the occupants?

topics.prompt: Let's see what you've got for sale.

lines.text: Premium Zebulonian wares, at premium prices.
This transaction is classified, you understand me?
Everything you see here, as long as it's visible.
The very best in Zebulonian technology.

topics.prompt: How will you help me understand space flight?

lines.text: Simple. By shooting you in the face.
Your memory's failing you Earthling. You've already got your gamma ray shot.
One burst of gamma rays, coming right up.
Then you'll get it. Right in the puddum.
Just remember to watch your landings.
Close your eyes and I'll count to three. One...

topics.prompt: Sure, sounds like a plan. I'll let you know when I need a blast.

lines.text: Very well, Earthling. I'll be sure to calibrate my weapon to your flesh settings.

topics.prompt: [Charisma 8+] The face? But that's my moneymaker!

lines.text: Oh, I wouldn't worry. By intergalactic standards, you're about two million xorbits below the poverty line. It really doesn't get much worse than that.
lines.note: Pronounced "zor-bits".

topics.prompt: On second thought, I think I'll pass.

lines.text: Fine, but there's nothing dangerous about it.
lines.note: Gently persuasive, disarming

lines.text: Perhaps I should explain further.

topics.prompt: Why does your suit say "Blast?

lines.text: It does not say "Blast." The symbols merely resemble your language, and it's confusing you.
What appears to you as letters are in fact ancient Zebulonian runes that spell the name "Xerxo.

topics.prompt: Why have you come to Earth? Why not just invade?

lines.text: Before we begin the invasion and close escrow on your planet, some reconnaissance and an appraisal needs to be done.
I am here studying your people, and perhaps, if the opportunity avails itself, mate with them.

topics.prompt: Is there anything you want to discuss with me?

lines.text: Yes, Earthling. For allowing me to stay at your camp, I have decided to generously give you our most distinguished award: the Zebulonian Medal of Honor. Here.

topics.prompt: I don't know. Maybe you were an astronaut named Blast, and simply forgot.

lines.text: Zebulonians do not forget. We have 38 brains, each one working independently to remember the time you didn't pay your fair share for dinner.
Mary chipped in, and she barely ate. But you! You ate half the food, and conveniently "forgot" your wallet at home.
lines.note: His mask slips, begins to reference his past life

lines.text: Everyone else may have forgot that minor transgression, but little brain number 36 didn't.
lines.note: Back to his Xerxo self

topics.prompt: I think you stole that suit from someone named Blast.

lines.text: Well, that is an understandable deduction for a species that uses their own clothing as a napkin.
But make no mistake. My suit says Xerxo, just like your clothes scream out, "wash me.

topics.prompt: You probably picked up that suit somewhere while scavenging.

lines.text: An understandable deduction for a species that collects trash and then displays it in their museums as art.
But make no mistake, my suit says Xerxo. You're just having trouble telling the difference.

topics.prompt: It might not be a name. Maybe it means "blast off?

lines.text: An understandable deduction for someone that can only think using Earthling languages.
But no, it doesn't. My suit says Xerxo, just as your clothes clearly say, "hardly working.

topics.prompt: [Intelligence 4+] The name Elliot Manfield mean anything to you? You know, the actor that played Blast Hannigan in "Invaders from Beyond Our Galaxy"?

lines.text: Well, the other day, I did have something you Earthlings call, a "dream.
I had switched my brain organs to sleep mode when I was suddenly bombarded by a strange visual.
It was of a tall man in a spacesuit, walking on a stage. And in the background, there was a voice that said, "Elliot, break a leg.
lines.note: Xerxo's mask begins to slip

lines.text: And perhaps this Elliot is a real person - a shell of himself, trying to find a way to cope in a world he simply does not understand.
lines.note: Xerxo's mask slips further.

lines.text: But given that my name is Xerxo, and I've never broken either of my legs, my dream was clearly about someone else.
lines.note: Back to Xerxo, straightens up, but rattled by the conversation

topics.prompt: The name Blast does sound familiar, but I can't place where.

lines.text: I've never heard of it, and no one has ever referred to me as a verb of any kind.
I told the writers it was a stupid name, but do they listen to old Elliot? No. They tell him, "you do your job, and we'll do ours.
lines.note: Xerxo's mask slips, becomes Elliot momentarily

lines.text: Well, now I'm doing the job of invading this backwater planet, so the joke's on them.
lines.note: Back to Xerxo, straightens up.

topics.prompt: That's disgusting, Xerxo.

lines.text: Do you think I take pleasure in this mission? I simply do what I must, for the sake of the Empire.
If that means performing the ancient Zebulonian love dance with one of your high ranking diplomats, so be it.

topics.prompt: I'm probably going to regret this. Fine, let's do this.

lines.text: Well, as flattered as I am by the proposition, I'm only allowed to perform the ancient Zebulonian love dance with high ranking government officials.
If you would like, however, we can stand near each other, and exchange nearby gases. I understand that is what qualifies as intimacy among your species.
lines.note: In a "want to grab a cup of coffee?" type of casual tone

topics.prompt: Why would you need to mate with an Earthling?

lines.text: Because that is how you Earthlings reveal your secrets. By being seduced, letting your guard down, and then whispering them in your sleep.
lines.note: Confused at the question. A sort of "duh, of course" tone.

lines.text: I've studied enough of your primitive spy cartridges to know of this fact.

topics.prompt: What if the opportunity never presents itself?

lines.text: Then I will continue as I have. Studying, appraising, and reading your amazing romance literature.
Just because I am not participating in your primitive mating rituals doesn't mean I shouldn't be well prepared for the scenario.

topics.prompt: This is a roll of toilet paper.

lines.text: No, it only looks like that to your untrained eye.
lines.note: Like an enthusiastic professor

lines.text: Now, while it is similar to your toilet paper in look, feel, and two-ply softness, I assure you, it is made of authentic Zebulonian eagle feathers.
lines.note: Beaming with pride

topics.prompt: Thank you. I'll wear it with pride.

lines.text: You should. It's only been given to a non-Zebulonian on two occasions. One to a Zambonian who stopped the Ice Insurrection on the Planet Hockeystick.
And the second, to the Scorchbeast Queen that ravaged your planet and helped reduce the asking price.

topics.prompt: Great, I'm always looking for more scrap.

lines.text: What you do with the medal is your own business. Usually while sitting, with the door closed. But either way, it's an honor well deserved.
Now go on, before I get all misty-eyed.
Yes, a few things. But perhaps you can tell me more.

topics.prompt: Do you know about Dr. Zorbo and the Legendary Run?

lines.text: Of course! I know all about Dr. Zornhole and his infamous jog.

topics.prompt: Have you heard of the film "Invaders from Beyond Our Galaxy?

lines.text: Do you think that just because I'm a space captain, brilliant military tactician, and devilishly handsome, that I am not also a student of history?
I know all about that piece of Earthist propaganda.

topics.prompt: Close enough.

lines.text: Yes. Almost... too close.

topics.prompt: It's Dr. Zorbo, actually.

lines.text: That's what I said.

topics.prompt: It's the Legendary Run.

lines.text: You cannot correct me. I am a Zebulonian, and you are not. That makes me right, and you wrong.

topics.prompt: It wasn't a run, but a jog?

lines.text: I so hate to disappoint you, but your hero is a fraud.
He'd like you to think it was a run. But if you look at the tape, you'll see that he's actually jogging and the tape has simply been sped up.

topics.prompt: How is it propaganda?

lines.text: It depicts the Zebulon Empire as evil, the Neptunians as Earth slaves, and worst of all, Blast Hannigan as a hero.

topics.prompt: What's the real story?

lines.text: Well for one, Blast Hannigan isn't a real name. It can't be. What kind of monster would name their child "Blast?
Only a Hollywood director could conceive of such cruelty.
The rest is more or less true to reality, except we were liberators, and the colonists were from Uranus. They always are.
Meanwhile, Earthlings had nothing to do with the incident, and yet they still plaster their names all over the credits. Typical.

topics.prompt: Blast Hannigan isn't a hero?

lines.text: Blast Hannigan doesn't even exist. He's an Earthling creation, through and through.
lines.note: Letting the player down softly

topics.prompt: How do you think they even knew about the war?

lines.text: The simplest explanation is quite often the right one. The Neptunian media probably leaked it to your press.

topics.prompt: I've never seen the movie myself.

lines.text: Good. And trust me, it's not worth watching. The acting is atrocious.

topics.prompt: The name on your suit says "Blast." Are you sure you aren't him?

lines.text: The Zebulonian runes on my suit spell "Xerxo". They're the same runes you'll find on my intergalactic pilot's license.

topics.prompt: That's all the questions I had on the film.

lines.text: A change of subject would be most welcome.

items.description: Don't be shy, try her latest creation! Yasmin is a Chef that makes your C.A.M.P. feel like home.
items.howToObtain: Can be purchased with certain bundles from the Atom Shop.

lines: Can be purchased with certain bundles from the Atom Shop.

lines.text: Tried any new foods lately?
lines.note: Friendly and curious

lines.text: Don't forget to stock up if you're heading out again.
Hello.
Hi there.
How are you doing?
I collected some new recipes on my latest outing.
Crambuger? I'm not sure that recipe can be rescued.
lines.note: Skeptical about this recipe and a little disgusted

lines.text: Don't eat just anything you find out there.
lines.note: Friendly concern

lines.text: I should visit that giant teapot next time I go out. We'll see how robot tea stacks up.
lines.note: Thoughtful, excited by the idea of visiting this landmark

lines.text: Swamp tofu? That needs a new name and a marketing campaign.
lines.note: Skeptical and amused by this food.

lines.text: I need to visit Flatwoods again sometime soon.
lines.note: Thinking, no real sense of urgency

lines.text: I really need to find a way to bring back water ice.
lines.note: Thinking about a favorite treat from her childhood

lines.text: Project Cheesesteak is officially on hold until I have a way to make cheese.
lines.note: Frustrated and disappointed

lines.text: I used to say I'd try anything once... now I'm not so sure.
lines.note: Reflecting on how she's changed over the years

lines.text: I found a box of Sugar Bombs. A little Brahmin milk and I'll be ready to go. Don't you dare tell anyone about my guilty pleasure!
Wish I had some fresh cranberries. I really want to try out this relish recipe.
I really should start my own garden.
lines.note: Thinking this is something she should have done already

lines.text: I wonder what those stuffy old cooking shows from before the war would say about Wasteland cuisine.
lines.note: Amused, but really wonders what the reaction would be

lines.text: Time to make a fresh pot of sweet tato stew.
I don't know how Brain Bombs got their name, but I'm going to make a batch.
lines.note: A little put off by the name, but confident they'll taste good

lines.text: Eighty-six glowing meat steaks. Time to go hunting again.
lines.note: Matter-of-fact, using a term she hasn't heard since the early days of her restaurant career

lines.text: I found some recipes at a place called Toxic Larry's Meat n' Go. But I won't be eating any of the�food I found there.
I wonder if mutations change your food preferences. Not that I'd want to find out�personally, mind you.
lines.note: Genuinely curious

lines.text: What do they feed you in a Vault, anyway?
Just say something if you're hungry.
lines.note: Friendly and caring

lines.text: Don't forget to stock up if you're heading out again.
Good to see you again, my friend.
lines.note: Friendly and warm

lines.text: Thank you again for giving me a place to work.
Welcome home.
There's a fresh batch of corn pone in the oven.
lines.note: Pleased with her efforts and happy to see the player again

lines.text: I have something I'd like you to sample.
lines.note: Friendly, genuinely interested in the player's opinion

lines.text: Don't be shy, try my latest creation!
lines.note: Friendly and confident

lines.text: You look famished, have you eaten recently?
You're just in time. I want you to try something that's been simmering on the stove.
lines.note: Excited and friendly

lines.text: A hearty meal and some rest will fix you right up.
lines.note: Confident she knows just what her friend needs after a long day

lines.text: You look like you could use a good meal. I know just the thing to help!
lines.note: Helpful and confident

lines.text: I'm working on something... unique, but I haven't worked up the courage to ask you to sample it yet.
lines.note: Amused and conspiratorial

lines.text: Pleased to meet you. My name's Yasmin, and I'm a traveling chef making my way through Appalachia.
lines.note: Warm and friendly, has a proposal she thinks will benefit her and the player.

lines.text: I always have something cooking.
lines.note: Friendly and in her element

lines.text: I brought back some beautiful produce from my latest trip.
lines.note: Pleased with the results of her foraging

lines.text: There are times when I miss a real kitchen, but there's pride in making do with what you've got.
lines.note: Thoughtful at first, but transitions to satisfied toward the end

lines.text: I've found some promising recipes. Don't worry, I won't sell you anything I haven't made - and tried - myself.
lines.note: Happy and transitions into a shared joke between friends.

lines.text: I gave a cooking lesson to some scavengers today. You should've seen their, uh, creative squirrel bits appetizer.
lines.note: Starts off pleased and later becomes amused by the results of her students' efforts.

lines.text: I meant to make mud cookies today, but I didn't get around to it. Anyway, how can I help?
lines.note: Lost in thought, slightly disappointed. Snaps back to the current moment at the end.

lines.text: Pull up a chair and tell me about your latest adventure.
lines.note: Friendly and welcoming

lines.text: I've met a lot of resourceful Wasteland cooks in my travels. I've also seen my share of crimes against food.
lines.note: Recalling fond memories at the beginning, then amused by thoughts of sillier things she's seen.

lines.text: The Wayward is the only real restaurant I've seen out here and I'm not in a hurry to apply to be their cook. Is there something you need?
I like the spot you chose here. Lots of opportunities to gather ingredients for my projects.
lines.note: Grateful, happy.

lines.text: I just pulled a fresh batch of blackberry honey crisp out of the oven.
lines.note: Happy and willing to share

lines.text: I would've liked to visit Big Fred's BBQ Shack before the war. Sorry, what's on your mind?
lines.note: Thoughtful, comes back to the current moment at the end.

topics.prompt: Let's change the topic.

lines.text: What do you want to talk about?

topics.prompt: It's not for a special occaison, but you need to try pepperoni rolls.

lines.text: You know, I met a trader who told me the same thing.
lines.note: Thinking back

lines.text: He said something about an old family recipe that's since been lost.
lines.note: Thinking back to a story she heard

lines.text: Of course, now that means I have to get my hands on it. If I can track it down, that is.

topics.prompt: You've got to see Meat Week. It's a giant cookout.

lines.text: That's exactly the kind of thing I'm looking for!
lines.note: Excited and grateful

lines.text: I just hope the grillmaster will share their secrets with me.
lines.note: Hopeful, conspiratorial

topics.prompt: Check out Fasnacht in Helvetia. They have a masked parade and donuts!

lines.text: Helvetia? I think I've traveled through there, but now I'll definitely have to visit again.
lines.note: Trying to remember whether she's been there or not, determined to visit

lines.text: Fasnacht goes back a long way, doesn't it? It's wonderful to see people keeping the tradition alive with food and festivities!
lines.note: Happy and excited

topics.prompt: I want to talk about something else.

lines.text: What do you want to discuss?

topics.prompt: What have you learned in your time here?

lines.text: I've gathered dozens of recipes for everything from a pot of Appalachili to a hearty Yao Guai roast.
lines.note: Proud of her accomplishments

lines.text: I want to learn more about Appalachia's celebrations and the foods that go with them.

topics.prompt: What happened to the other survivors?

lines.text: That's just it... I-I don't know.
We only had time to say a short goodbye and decided it was best to separate.
lines.note: Sad, regretful

lines.text: It was harder for the Raiders to follow us that way, but it meant I might never see my friends again either.
lines.note: Sad, speaking about a painful choice

lines.text: No... no, they weren't just my friends. They were my second family. I keep thinking maybe I'll find them in the next settlement if I just keep on going.
lines.note: Starts out sad, realizing this is the second time she's lost all the people close to her. Becomes a determined and a little hopeful at the end.

topics.prompt: Give me the short version.

lines.text: Well, Raiders attacked the settlement I'd built with other survivors.
Some of us managed to escape, most weren't so lucky.
I had my notes and stories from travelers about Appalachian cuisine, so I set out.
lines.note: Tone is more conversational here, confident she made the right choice about where to go

topics.prompt: I've got time, and I'd like to know.

lines.text: After the war, I joined a group of survivors building a settlement in the ruins of an old resort in the Poconos.
lines.note: Speaking fondly of old friends

lines.text: We built my kitchen first. It was the center of town, the place you'd go for a warm meal and the company of friends after a long day.
lines.note: Warm, sharing her favorite memories of life after the war

lines.text: We had fifteen good years before the Raiders came. They destroyed the town and scattered those of us they didn't kill.
lines.note: Becomes quieter and more somber

lines.text: I escaped with my notes and just headed toward Appalachia.
lines.note: Somber and determined

lines.text: But then I remembered the stories I had heard about the recipes locals like Delbert Winters had created.
lines.note: Matter-of-fact, an aside to help the player understand why she chose Appalachia.

lines.text: So I set out to learn more about Appalachian cooking traditions, new and old.
lines.note: Determined, confident

topics.prompt: I want to ask about something else.

lines.text: What's on your mind?

topics.prompt: The Wasteland is full of dangerous creatures.

lines.text: And I've field dressed and cooked a lot of them.
lines.note: Very confident in her abilities

lines.text: One of the first people I met in Appalachia was a hunter who taught me how to spot animal tracks.
lines.note: Recalling a pleasant memory

lines.text: In return, I showed her how to make a respectable meal with anything we caught.

topics.prompt: Don't you fear being attacked?

lines.text: Well, sure... it's always at the back of my mind. You can't tell me you don't think about that too.
lines.note: Being honest, realizes that what the player is saying is true

lines.text: But I've learned how to avoid danger and I can defend myself if it comes to that.
lines.note: Confident. She's a seasoned traveler

lines.text: That said, most people I meet aren't looking for a fight. A warm meal and a conversation are far more common.
lines.note: Friendly, speaking from experience

topics.prompt: A restaurant wouldn't have survived the war anyway.

lines.text: You're right, of course. It took time to realize the war didn't just steal my future.
lines.note: Serious, emphasis on 'my'. Realizing that other people were hurting helped her determine what to do next

lines.text: What helped was understanding there was something I could do about that. I could use my skills to help others adapt.
lines.note: Confident, determined to help others

topics.prompt: I'm sorry you didn't get a chance to do that.

lines.text: Please, don't be.
lines.note: Warm, doesn't want the player to think she only has regrets about not getting to open her restaurant

lines.text: I never expected to find myself traveling this way, but I sure don't regret it.
lines.note: Reflecting, happy

lines.text: I'm still doing what I've always loved: preparing meals, learning new recipes, and finding small ways to pass that knowledge on.
lines.note: Happy, passionate

topics.prompt: Do you always travel alone?

lines.text: Yes, most of the time.
I've traveled with groups and cooked for caravans, but I like setting my own schedule.

topics.prompt: Where did you grow up?

lines.text: I was born in Philadelphia and spent my whole life there until culinary school.
lines.note: Friendly, thinking back fondly on her childhood

lines.text: After graduating, I went back to Philly to be near my family while I started making a name for myself as a chef.
lines.note: Thinking back on happy times

lines.text: My dream was to open my own restaurant.

topics.prompt: What brought you to Appalachia?

lines.text: That's a rather long story.

topics.prompt: Why would they need to know how to make fancy meals?

lines.text: Food does more than just keep you going.
For me, it's always been a way to keep family traditions alive and find common ground with people I meet.
lines.note: Friendly and confident, speaking from experience

lines.text: I want to help others create new traditions to pass on.
lines.note: Friendly and determined

topics.prompt: You can sign me up right now.

lines.text: I'm glad you see the value in it, but I still need to work out some of the details.
lines.note: Happy and grateful

lines.text: It'll be my small way of leaving the world a little better.

topics.prompt: I want to talk about something else.

lines.text: Sure.

topics.prompt: I'd like to buy some recipes from you.

lines.text: Tell me if you see anything you like.

topics.prompt: What do you do with them all?

lines.text: I trade them, of course, but I also use them to teach others how to cook for themselves.
Before the war, it was easy to find a dozen versions of a dish. I want to rediscover and preserve that knowledge for those who come after us.
lines.note: Thoughtful at the beginning, determined to follow through toward the end

lines.text: I used to want to open my own restaurant, but now I think a cooking school would serve better.
lines.note: Thinking her way through as she answers

topics.prompt: Actually, I want to talk about something else.

lines.text: What's on your mind?

topics.prompt: Is there a famous Appalachian food you haven't tried yet?

lines.text: I have a recipe for Scorchbeast Mixed Meat Stew that I haven't been able to make yet.
It calls for just about every cut of meat you can get. I'm a fair hunter, but game like that is beyond me.
lines.note: Impressed by the skills needed to hunt one of these animals

lines.text: I don't know how, but I'll make a banquet of one of those things someday.
lines.note: Doubtful at the beginning, changing to confident at the end

topics.prompt: Why did you become a chef?

lines.text: I could say it was an act of rebellion against my parents.
lines.note: Emphasis on 'could', a little conspiratorial

lines.text: They were academics who wanted me to follow them into their field. But, they came around once they realized my interest wasn't a phase.
lines.note: Quiet, reflective, grateful that they finally understood

lines.text: The truth is, I've always been fascinated by food.
I got my start helping Grandma make little sweets called sandesh for my sister's birthday party. I chose the shapes and the toppings.
lines.note: Happy, thinking about her favorite childhood memory

lines.text: After that, if Grandma was in the kitchen, I was too.
lines.note: Happy, speaking about her favorite thing to do growing up

lines.text: *sigh* That all feels like another lifetime now. I know it sounds foolish, but I still hope to reunite with my parents and sister again.
lines.note: Sad, quieter, hoping against the odds at the end.

topics.prompt: Do you mind if I use your cooking equipment?

lines.text: If I'm not at the stove, feel free to help yourself. There's plenty to do with gathering ingredients and going over my notes.
lines.note: Agreeable, inviting

topics.prompt: I want to buy some recipes.

lines.text: Sure thing. Let me get out my notes for you.
lines.note: Happy to help

lines.text: There are some classics here. Let me know if anything catches your eye.
lines.note: Friendly and helpful

topics.prompt: You mentioned trading stories. I want to know more about you.

lines.text: Ah, my favorite part of traveling. What do you want to know?
lines.note: Happy, glad to answer the player's questions

topics.prompt: Let's talk about cooking.

lines.text: Of course! I love talking shop... err, kitchen.
lines.note: Happy to talk about something that's important to her

topics.prompt: I've worked up an appetite. What do you have to eat?

lines.text: I've got something that'll hit the spot.
Didn't you just have a snack?
lines.note: Lighthearted question to a friend

lines.text: Give it some time to settle and I'll be happy to make something for you later.
lines.note: Friendly and happy to help

lines.text: I bet you're wondering why I'm here. That's exactly what I wanted to talk to you about.
lines.note: Friendly and open

topics.prompt: A traveling chef, how does that work?

lines.text: I've been a recipe collector all my life and found myself on the road again recently.
lines.note: Friendly, happy that the player seems interested

lines.text: I move from place to place, getting to know people and swapping stories and family recipes along the way.
lines.note: Friendly, genuinely interested in the people she meets

lines.text: It's my way of preserving and passing along the knowledge of my trade.
lines.note: Friendly, confident

topics.prompt: Do you make a habit of showing up at people's homes unannounced?

lines.text: Well, I look for a chance to introduce myself and start a conversation.
I can usually tell if someone's up for a meal or willing to have a friendly chat.
lines.note: Friendly, speaking from experience

lines.text: I'm looking for a safe place to practice making the local recipes I've learned. Your C.A.M.P. seems like the perfect spot.
lines.note: Hopeful, speaking honestly about the player's camp.

lines.text: Let me set up here and I'll share my meals with you. You're also welcome to buy copies of the recipes I've gathered.
lines.note: Straightforward, honest. Offering a fair trade

topics.prompt: I already cook for myself.

lines.text: Think of it this way, sharing the work will free up time for your other interests.
lines.note: Talking up the bargain she wants to make.

lines.text: And you won't have to worry about me using your supplies. I forage or trade for everything I need.
lines.note: Friendly, showing how trustworthy she is.

lines.text: All I ask is that you give me a chance to show what I can do.

topics.prompt: That sounds wonderful!

lines.text: Oh, thank goodness! I was afraid I was going to have to give you the hard sell - "No more tossing food onto the coals and hoping for the best.
lines.note: Grateful and relieved, joking about what she was going to say next if the player didn't agree

lines.text: Just because you live in a C.A.M.P doesn't mean you have to eat like a camper.
lines.note: Joking about what she would have said if the player hadn't agreed.

topics.prompt: Buy recipes? Can't you just share them while you're staying here?

lines.text: Well, I'll be sharing the food I make. But there is a cost to documenting and preserving the recipes I find.
lines.note: Friendly and honest about her motives

lines.text: Think of it as donating a few caps to help me stay supplied. I can spend more time turning up new recipes you can't live without.
lines.note: Reassuring while making a little sales pitch

topics.prompt: You'd better not poison me.

lines.text: Chef Hernandez drilled that into us on the first day of culinary school.
Getting diners sick is the best way to make your career a short one.
lines.note: Mimicking a voice of her old teacher, slightly amused

lines.text: I won't be in your way. I'd only need a little space for my equipment.
lines.note: Friendly and honest

lines.text: You're even welcome to use it when I'm not cooking.
Imagine the aroma of a steaming pot of Appalachili welcoming you home from a long day of scavenging. What do you say?
lines.note: Thinking about the kind of meal she'd want to come home to after a hard day

topics.prompt: I'd enjoy the company and the food.

lines.text: I will, too! I'll be able to get a lot more cooking done if I don't have to look over my shoulder at the same time.
lines.note: Grateful and excited

topics.prompt: Let's see how it goes.

lines.text: That's good enough for me. Now, if you don't mind, I'd like to get started setting up.

topics.prompt: It'll work as long as you don't bother me.

lines.text: My work keeps me busy, so you'll hardly notice me. All you have to do is ask if you'd like something or just want to chat.
lines.note: Starts off matter-of-fact, becomes friendly toward the end

topics.prompt: Why do you collect recipes?

lines.text: I wanted to have a record of everything I made, so I started our family cookbook when I was six.
lines.note: Passionate, talking about a lifelong project

lines.text: At first, it was meals I learned from Grandma. As I got older, I added my own creations.
When the bombs fell, I was on a research trip developing recipes for my own restaurant.
lines.note: Becomes quieter here, recalling a sad memory

lines.text: Those notes grew into the collection I have today.
lines.note: Transitions back to happy and passionate

lines.text: Today, I've whipped up a spin on my childhood favorite, Blamco Mac & Cheese with More Rat sausage.
lines.note: Happy with her work

lines.text: I've made you Dandy Boy Apple surprise. The surprise is that I managed to make them edible again.
lines.note: Amused, especially toward the end

lines.text: Give these golden potato cakes a try. You'd never know they were made from Instamash!
lines.note: Friendly, hopes the player will agree

lines.text: How about some hearty Sheepsquatch pie?
Try these deep fried cave cricket glands with a honey glaze. I'm thinking of calling them Blue Ridge Oysters.
Today I've made you a plate of delicate stuffed gourd blossoms.
lines.note: Proud of what she's made

lines.text: You're just in time to sample my braised Megasloth and greens.
lines.note: Pleased with what she made

lines.text: Here, have some of my signature Fog Crawler bisque in a razorgrain bread bowl.
Try a couple of these grilled Radroach skewers. They'd be even better with a nice barbecue sauce.
lines.note: Friendly, hopes the player likes what she made

lines.text: I've prepared a grilled Radstag steak with sauteed Firecaps.
Who said dessert can't be a meal? This is a deconstructed Starlight Berry Cobbler that I've had to... err, reconstruct.
lines.note: Playful, amused

lines.text: This is a Sugar Bomb-crusted Angler filet with roast carrots.
lines.note: Happy, slightly surprised this worked

lines.text: My latest creation is an Angler tartare with crispy tato chips. Bon App�tit.
lines.note: Pleased with what she made

lines.text: My latest experiment is Blackwater Brew-battered Stingwing, try saying that 3 times fast, with a spicy dipping sauce.
lines.note: Really hoping this dish is a success

topics.prompt: Let's talk about something else.

lines.text: That's fine with me.
And before I forget, here's a little something as a thanks for helping me cross this off my list.

topics.prompt: Where do I RSVP for that banquet?

lines.text: *Laughs* Oh, don't worry. You're first on the list already.

topics.prompt: [Give Scorchbeast Mixed Meat Stew] You're in luck. I have a bowl for you right here.

lines.text: Really? Of course I'll take you up on that!

lines.text: I promise I'll try to feel a little guilty for stealing your meal later.
